title: International Growth Practice Senior Associate  (Pharma & Healthcare)
description: Line of ServiceInternal Firm ServicesIndustry/SectorNot ApplicableSpecialismOrganisation StrategyManagement LevelManagerJob Description & SummaryAt PwC, we help clients build trust and reinvent so they can turn complexity into competitive advantage. We’re a tech-forward, people-empowered network with more than 370,000 people in 149 countries. Across audit and assurance, tax and legal, deals and consulting we help clients build, accelerate and sustain momentum. Find out more at www.pwc.com.Headquartered in Singapore, PwC’s International Growth Practice is a global team supporting organizations to address their internationalization ambitions, whilst achieving rebalanced and resilient growth strategies. We are a truly global team, with satellite offices in Europe and the United States, made up of individuals from over 15 nationalities that reflects our diverse and extensive cross-country and multi-industry experience. The practice caters to a wide array of problem statements ranging from international market expansion, global location assessment, international supply chain transformation, international talent strategy, intra-regional trade flow analysis and strategic point of view development. Our global team focuses on several sectors including healthcare and pharmaceuticals, industrial manufacturing, automotive , consumer goods, telecoms, media and technology, financial services as well as government and global institutions. For more information about PwC’s International Growth Practice, please visit our website: www.pwc.com/internationalgrowth About the role We are seeking experienced professionals with expertise in Pharmaceuticals and Healthcare to join PwC’s International Growth Practice. This role focuses on helping leading pharma and healthcare organizations expand globally, optimize their supply chains, and build resilient operating models in an increasingly complex international environment. You will work with senior executives of multinational corporations and governments to design strategies that enable sustainable growth across diverse markets. Responsibilities Develop expansion strategies for clients from the sector seeking international expansion or to realign their existing supply chain and production footprints to being more rebalanced and resilient. Typical engagements will focus on developing in depth analysis and insights for: Market expansion strategies (Where to play) – market, consumer and competitor assessments as well as product and services analysis Market entry scenarios (How to win) – Channel strategies, operating model design, partner evaluation and selection. Global and regional site selection for new HQs, R&D sites, manufacturing / production plants Global talent assessments, to assess the availability of talent for growth strategies Supplier portfolio realignment, identifying and assessing suppliers to meet the needs of realigned supply chains and manufacturing. Strategic points of view focused on international growth Provide points of view for publication on opportunities and challenges of global trade and internationalization Lead bespoke client discussions and workshops to senior executives of corporate organizations and governments. Engage in business development and client pursuit efforts-Develop global relationships and build a pipeline of inbound and outbound projects to sell and deliver Work closely with PwC’s global network of teams and connect relevant expertise in PwC to address clients’ unique business challenges Establish strong international network of external stakeholders including clients and industry associations and participate in regional and international conferences and client events About you 4-5 years of relevant experience working in Pharma and healthcare sectors in either a management consulting setting or within industry in strategy or general management role. Growth markets experience (E.g. Southeast Asia, China, India, Middle East, Latin America, Africa and CEE) Strong experience in delivering on client engagement with multiple stakeholders and teams in different countries Experienced in managing data collection and analysis and resourceful with excellent research and analytical skills; can transform quantitative and qualitative data into insights relating to country, sector and consumer trends, competitive intelligence Possess credentials in business development and sales with ability to develop insightful presentations to support proposals, client discussions and business development pursuits Thrives in a fast-paced and dynamic work environment Possess strong communication and presentation skills Team player comfortable with working in a multicultural and diverse global team Education (if blank, degree and/or field of study not specified)Degrees/Field of Study required:Degrees/Field of Study preferred:Certifications (if blank, certifications not specified)Required SkillsGrowth Development, Growth Planning, Growth Strategies, Healthcare Industry, International Market Entry, Market Entry, Market Entry Strategy, Market Expansion, Pharmaceutical IndustryOptional SkillsAccepting Feedback, Accepting Feedback, Active Listening, Analytical Thinking, Business Data Analytics, Change Management, Coaching and Feedback, Communication, Consumer Markets, Cost Management, Creativity, Customer Relations, Customer Service Excellence, Embracing Change, Emotional Regulation, Empathy, Global Supply Chain, Inclusion, Intellectual Curiosity, Lean Product Development, Learning Agility, Manufacturing Strategy, Market Analysis, Operational Performance Management (OPM), Optimism {+ 14 more}Desired Languages (If blank, desired languages not specified)Travel Requirements0%Available for Work Visa Sponsorship?YesGovernment Clearance Required?YesJob Posting End Date

Project Manager - SaT - GOV - SaT - TCF - Infrastructure Advisory - Hyderabad Location: Hyderabad Other locations: Primary Location Only Salary: Competitive Date: Oct 29, 2026 Job description Requisition ID: 1740619 Requisition Id: 1740619 As a global leader in assurance, tax, transaction and advisory services, we hire and develop the most passionate people in their field to help build a better working world. This starts with a culture that believes in giving you the training, opportunities and creative freedom. At EY, we don't just focus on who you are now, but who you can become. We believe that it’s your career and ‘It’s yours to build’ which means potential here is limitless and we'll provide you with motivating and fulfilling experiences throughout your career to help you on the path to becoming your best professional self.The opportunity : Project Manager-GOV-SaT-SaT - TCF - Infrastructure Advisory - HyderabadGOV : Our Global Government & Public Sector (GPS) is a network of highly skilled professionals dedicated to serving our clients by bringing best-in-class international experience and insight combined with local knowledge to solve the most critical problems facing governments today. We actively focus on building solutions that help public sector entities face the challenges of the future and reinvent themselves. Digital transformation is not just about new technologies; it involves an overhaul of organizational structures, governance, work processes, culture and mindset. It also means realizing a wider vision of relationships and business models that will redesign how public services function. To achieve this vision, we help clients balance strategic choices to re-ignite performance. We have developed a suite of cross-service line strategic solutions that align with our client priorities. We have a proud record of helping governments meet their challenges head-on, and we work closely with them to build a world that works better for all citizens. SaT : The Government and public sector transactions services is part of EY's Government & Public Sector (GPS) Services which is a network of highly skilled professionals from assurance, tax, transaction and advisory services, devoted to serving the government and public sector organizations and institutions. The practice combines private sector leading practice with an understanding of the public sector’s diverse needs, focused on delivering improved public services. Government and public sector transactions services, sits under EY’s Transaction Advisory Services practice, a market-leading, multi-disciplinary team, working with leading businesses across a range of industries. This practice is in a unique position to deliver implementable strategies given the firm’s sector depth, transaction perspectives, and operational insights. The practice provides experience working with various sectors such as, Transport, Social & Health care, Education, Urban & Infrastructure, Economic Development Advisory , Water waste & Sanitation, Power & Utilities and Public Finance & Management. SaT - TCF - Infrastructure Advisory : Strategy and Transactions enables clients to reimagine ecosystems, reshape portfolios and reinvent for a better future. Using our Capital Agenda framework, we work with clients to find answers to today’s toughest strategic, financial, operational and commercial questions. We help corporates, private equity, governments, sovereign wealth funds, private and family businesses, and educational institutions with their key financial issues. description: Skip to main content Atmospheric Scientist - Development Innovation Lab India Location: Delhi Country: India Education: Master's Other advanced degree Start Date (Earliest): 2 November 2026 Language Requirement: Hindi About the University of Chicago Trust:The University of Chicago Trust (the Trust) is a charitable trust in India, established in 2008 by alumnus of The University of Chicago. The objectives of the Trust’s objectives are to provide opportunities for grants to support educational programs, research programs and activities for the betterment of India.The Development Innovation Lab – India (DIL-India):DIL-India, based at the Trust in India, is dedicated to using the tools of economics to develop innovations with the potential to benefit millions of people. We have work in health, education, agriculture, climate change, road safety, and others. We do so by collaborating with government agencies, firms, and non-profits in India to identify, test, and scale evidence-based solutions. DIL-India has a fast-growing portfolio of policy-relevant research. DIL-India supports the development and dissemination of cutting- edge AI-based monsoon onset forecasts to farmers. DIL-India plans to build on this work, aiming to reach more people and expand its research to areas that have the potential to improve livelihoods and impact well-being.Human Centered Weather Forecast Initiative:Collaborating with HCWF, DIL-India brings together climate scientists, artificial intelligence (AI) experts and economists to build and evaluate weather forecasts that can target what citizens need to know, leveraging novel technologies, including AI, and scientific understanding. This interdisciplinary team then works to test forecast dissemination strategies, refine those strategies based on user response, and scale forecast dissemination to inform data-driven decision-making. For example: The Indian Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare distributed AI forecasts to 38 million farmers accurately predicting the start of the monsoon in 2025, becoming a model for using advanced in AI and atmospheric science to help vulnerable populations adapt to climate change. Hundreds of millions of smallholder farmers across the tropics depend on information about when the rainy season, known as the monsoon, will come each year. This advanced knowledge allows farmers to make more informed decisions about when to plant seeds, irrigate, and hire labor. However, accurate forecasting of when the monsoon will begin, especially at long lead teams and local scales, has remained a century-old challenge. AI has revolutionized global weather forecasting, promising new tools for predicting phenomena as complex as the monsoon. DIL-India researchers lead local HCWF research that supports an international, multidisciplinary collaboration to harness advances in AI to better predict the beginning of the monsoon in India.This job opening is part of the launch of a new DIL-India initiative. Position Description :The Atmospheric Scientist Lead, HCWF will support the creation of advanced, built-for-purpose forecasts of high-impact weather phenomena for deployment at scale in low- and middle-income countries. As part of a multidisciplinary collaboration between universities, development agencies, and governmental ministries, the selected candidate will contribute to the development of forecasts of dangerous heat stress, precipitation, monsoon onset, and other tropical phenomena using AI, statistical, and physics-based weather prediction models. This position is focused on large-scale delivery of decision-oriented forecasts together with research and development. The position is well-suited for candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas: monsoon onset prediction; short- or medium-range precipitation forecasting; tropical intra seasonal variability; and extreme heat and heat stress forecasting.Responsibilities:Contribute to the development of novel decision-oriented forecasting metrics and forecasting systems using AI, statistical, and physics-based methods; evaluate forecast skill against baselines tailored for decision-makers.Build fundamental understanding of the forecasting potential for high-impact phenomena, such as extreme heat and monsoon onset, using AI and statistical weather models.Collaborate with meteorological agencies in multiple countries to help build an operational system providing actionable, real-time predictions, leveraging last-mile delivery pipelines developed by non-governmental partner organizations.Conduct benchmarking and validation of AI-based and physics-based forecast systems against observational data.Collaborate with data scientists and ML engineers to build scalable and reproducible forecast pipelines.Contribute to the design of field experiments, including randomized controlled trials, to evaluate the impact and uptake of improved forecasts.Contribute to grant proposals and the preparation of research reports, technical documents, and academic publications.Performs other related work as assigned.Qualifications:Education:Masters in atmospheric science, meteorology, climate science, agrometeorology, physical oceanography, applied math, statistics, physics, engineering, or a related field. Advanced degree preferred. Experience: Minimum of 3 or more years of work experience in a related job discipline, including research or operational roles in weather forecasting or climate science. Experience applying machine learning or statistical methods to weather or climate prediction. Experience with numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems. Experience working in low- and middle-income country contexts, and data-sparse environments.Experience with field work in developing countries, preferably including randomized controlled trials is preferred.Competencies:Strong programming and numerical skills; proficiency in Python and common scientific computing libraries (e.g., NumPy, xarray, PyTorch, TensorFlow).Experience with high-performance computing and analysis of large meteorological or climate datasets (e.g., reanalyses and NWP or AI weather prediction ensemble products).Expertise in weather forecasting, climate modeling/dynamics, or related geospatial applications.Familiarity with theoretical and practical aspects of scientific deep learning and AI weather models (e.g., GraphCast, AIFS).Knowledge of forecast verification methods (e.g., CRPS, reliability diagrams, skill scores).Strong communication and presentation skills, including ability to present to non-specialist audiences.Ability to work both independently and as part of a fast-paced, multidisciplinary, multi-institutional team.Working Conditions:Based in Delhi with regular travel throughout India to project locationsApplicant must be legally authorized to work in India.This is a one-year position subject to renewal. title: Research Associate - Breakthrough Follow Up - J-PAL South Asia
description: Skip to main content Research Associate - Breakthrough Follow Up - J-PAL South Asia Organization: J-PAL South Asia Location: Delhi Country: India Education: Bachelor's Master's Start Date (Earliest): 21 October 2026 Language Requirement: Hindi Length of Commitment: Less than one year PIs: Seema Jayachandran (Princeton University), Diva Dhar (University of Oxford), Tarun Jain (IIM Ahmedabad)About J-PAL South Asia:The Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) J-PAL was established in 2003 as a research center at the Economics Department at MIT. Since then, it has grown into a global network of researchers who use randomized evaluations to answer critical policy questions in the fight against poverty. J-PAL is propelled by a first-rate team dedicated to research, policy, training, and other vital work, supporting J-PAL's mission to reduce poverty by ensuring that policy is informed by scientific evidence.J-PAL South Asia, based at the Institute for Financial Management and Research (IFMR) in Chennai, leads J-PAL’s efforts to advance evidence-informed policymaking in the region. By conducting rigorous randomized evaluations, forging impactful strategic partnerships, and scaling effective programs, we strive to deliver better evidence to help governments design better policies so people can live better lives. Established in 2007, J-PAL South Asia is the oldest and the largest among all J-PAL offices. We have 255 ongoing and completed evaluations in the South Asia region across 11 sectors to dateProject Description:Breakthrough’s school-based program Taaron ki Toli (TkT) is aimed at reshaping gender attitudes via interactive classroom sessions and other activities with male and female adolescent students in grades 7 to 10. Results from the randomized evaluation by J-PAL show that the program had a sizable impact on gender-related attitudes for both boys and girls as well as gender-related behaviors, notably for boys. These results on attitudes persist in follow-up surveys conducted two and six years after the program ended, with spillover effects on younger siblings and fathers. Based on the promising evidence, J-PAL and Breakthrough are continuing to partner with a number of state governments in India to scale up the program. We will now conduct a follow-up ten year endline survey to determine the impacts of attitude change on long term outcomes such as girls’ agency, education, work, marriage and childbirth, which will inform the future scale-up and adaptation of the program.About the Role:J-PAL South Asia is inviting expressions of interest for upcoming Research Associate (RA) positions across a variety of sectors and geographies. RAs at J-PAL play a central role in managing the implementation of randomized evaluations, working closely with researchers from leading Universities around the world, ensuring that each evaluation is designed and implemented with precision and rigor.Key Responsibilities:The responsibilities of a Research Associate typically include, but are not limited to:Supporting researchers in developing and refining study protocols through in-field scoping activities. You will provide contextual and operational insights to help researchers shape experimental protocols that are methodologically rigorous and feasible within the study setting.Strengthening measurement validity and reliability by assisting in the development and piloting of survey instruments. You will be responsible for organizing field tests, analyzing pilot data, and integrating structured feedback loops to improve the precision and accuracy of indicators.Enable accurate and efficient data capture through the programming of digital surveys and development of end-to-end data workflows. This includes incorporating survey logic, real-time checks, and secure data transmission to ensure clean, analysis-ready datasets.Ensuring collection of high-quality primary data—recruiting, training, and managing field teams to collect data that meets rigorous research standards.Safeguarding data integrity in consultation with the research team by setting up and maintaining systems for real-time quality monitoring. You will identify issues in incoming data, identify solutions in collaboration with the researchers, and implement corrective measures.Preparing analysis-ready datasets by writing reproducible code (in Stata, R, or Python), generating summary statistics, and contributing to the analytical preparation for publications, working closely with researchers.Facilitating alignment between research teams and implementation partners to ensure that project implementation aligns with study protocols. You will coordinate timelines, share updates across teams, and help troubleshoot day-to-day challenges while maintaining strong working relationships with external stakeholders.Ensuring transparency and reproducibility by developing and maintaining detailed documentation, including codebooks, field protocols, and project logs that align with academic standards and support eventual replication and publication.Maintaining strict adherence to J-PAL’s research protocols throughout all stages of the research lifecycle.What We’re Looking For:Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive approach to addressing operational and analytical challengesAbility to manage day-to-day work with minimal supervisionExcellent time management and attention to detailAbility to navigate fast-evolving settings that require flexibility and initiativeExcellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to adapt messaging for diverse audiencesRequired Knowledge and Skills:A Bachelor's/master’s degree in economics, sociology, social sciences, public policy, public health or related fields.Sound understanding of impact evaluation methods, especially randomized controlled trials (RCTs)Proficiency in data analysis and statistical tools such as Stata or RExperience with digital data collection platforms such as SurveyCTO or QualtricsFluency in English; proficiency in Hindi (written, reading and spoken) required.Willingness to travel extensively and stay in field locations within Haryana.Experience working with external stakeholders such as government departments or NGOs is a plusLength of Commitment: 10 monthsEducation: Bachelor’s/Master’s in Economics, Statistics, Public Policy or related fieldsLanguage requirement: English and HindiStart Date (Earliest): As soon as possible How to Apply Please apply using this link.

title: Operations Associate - ADEPT - J-PAL Europe
description: Skip to main content Operations Associate - ADEPT - J-PAL Europe Organization: J-PAL Europe Location: Paris, France Country: France Education: Bachelor's Master's Other advanced degree Start Date (Earliest): 20 October 2026 Language Requirement: English French Length of Commitment: One year Summary of the Organisation:The Alliance for Data, Evaluation and Policy Training (ADEPT) seeks to hire an Operations Associate based at J-PAL Europe (Paris School of Economics) to support its mission of expanding training and education in evidence-informed policymaking around the world.Launched in 2024, ADEPT is part of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL), a global research centre working to reduce poverty by ensuring that policy is informed by scientific evidence, and anchored by a network of 2,100+ researchers at universities around the world. Within J-PAL, ADEPT carries a vision of training the next generation of researchers and decision makers in rigorous policy design, evaluation, and analysis. The ADEPT core team develops university partnerships around the world, leveraging the MITx MicroMasters program in Data, Economics and Designs of Policy (DEDP) to launch new programs targeting civil servants, students, development professionals, and faculty. We are a small, dynamic team that works with a high number of external university partners and J-PAL offices worldwide.Summary of the Role:We are looking to hire someone who combines a passion for ADEPT’s mission with strong operational skills to support our work. The Operations Associate will be at the heart of providing crucial operational support to our university partnerships throughout implementation and communications. Length of Commitment: One year, renewable Start Date (Earliest): As soon as possible How to Apply Please submit your CV and cover letter, including details on how your experience and qualifications are relevant to the position and on your authorization to work in France to [email protected]. Applications with incomplete materials will not be considered.J-PAL values the strength that diverse teams bring to our work. We actively welcome applicants from backgrounds that reflect populations most impacted by poverty and from groups that are underrepresented in the economics field. J-PAL is committed to equal opportunity, and all positions are open to people with disabilities.We will review applications on a rolling basis with a deadline of November 15th. Given the volume of applications received, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview. Shortlisted candidates will also be invited to complete a written exercise.

title: AI & Automation Associate - J-PAL Middle East and North Africa
description: Skip to main content AI & Automation Associate - J-PAL Middle East and North Africa Organization: J-PAL Middle East and North Africa Location: American University in Cairo, Egypt Country: Egypt Education: Bachelor's Start Date (Earliest): 1 November 2026 Language Requirement: Arabic Summary of the Organization:The Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab Middle East and North Africa (J-PAL MENA), hosted at the American University in Cairo, works to reduce poverty by ensuring that policy is informed by scientific evidence. J-PAL MENA already uses AI-assisted development to build internal tools, including systems for managing grant financial documentation, supporting staff feedback, and reviewing recordings of field surveys. It is also exploring more ambitious applications, such as Arabic-language AI systems and AI-enabled research back-checks.Summary of the Role:J-PAL MENA is seeking an AI & Automation Associate (part-time, hybrid from Cairo) to help build and improve AI, automation, and software systems that support research, finance, and operations. Designed for an early-career candidate (0–2 years of experience), the role involves working with colleagues across teams to understand their needs and turn promising ideas into tools that are reliable, useful, secure, and maintainable. Roughly a third of the role is dedicated to securing the applications built with AI, both by defining security requirements before development and by finding and fixing weaknesses before colleagues depend on a tool.Responsibilities:Understand operational problems, ask the right questions, and determine whether software, AI, automation, or a simpler solution is appropriate.Rapidly prototype solutions, test them with users, and take projects from initial idea through deployment and maintenance.Build new tools and improve existing systems used across research, finance, and internal operations.Define security requirements before development starts, including what data a tool will handle, who should access it, and what could go wrong, and translate these into clear instructions for AI-assisted development.Review AI-generated code and configurations for vulnerabilities, including weak authentication, missing authorization checks, exposed credentials, injection risks, and unsafe database or API access rules.Use AI tools to run security reviews and tests on applications, then manually verify the findings and confirm the fixes work.Check existing internal tools for security gaps and harden them, prioritizing by the sensitivity of the data involved.Protect systems that involve research participant data, financial records, survey recordings, or confidential staff information, including access controls, secrets management, logging, and backups.Document security decisions and help establish simple, repeatable checks that every tool passes before release.Apply sound engineering practices so tools are dependable beyond the prototype stage, including Git and version control, reviewing and understanding AI-generated code, writing tests and documentation, and considering validation, logging, backups, dependencies, and failure modes.Qualifications:A bachelor's degree; computer science, software engineering, computer engineering, cybersecurity, data science, or another relevant technical field is particularly relevant.0–2 years of relevant experience; recent graduates are strongly encouraged to apply.Experience building software using modern AI coding tools.Knowledge of Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or another general-purpose programming language.Familiarity with Git, SQL/databases, APIs, web applications, and basic deployment.Ability to debug, test, and reason about code rather than relying uncritically on AI-generated output.A solid foundation in cybersecurity, gained through a degree, coursework, certifications, CTFs, bug bounty work, or personal projects.Working understanding of common web and API vulnerabilities (such as the OWASP Top 10) and how to find and fix them in real code.Knowledge of authentication, authorization, and access control, including database-level permissions.Experience with secrets management and the safe handling of credentials and sensitive data.Ability to think through how a system could be misused or attacked before it is built.Familiarity with AI-specific security risks, such as prompt injection and data leakage through LLMs, is a strong plus.Ability to take an ambiguous problem and independently work toward a practical solution.Ability to collaborate effectively with nontechnical colleagues and to learn new tools and approaches quickly.Ability to balance experimentation and speed with attention to reliability, security, and maintainability.Ability to work comfortably in English and Arabic.Ability to attend in person in Cairo, Egypt. How to Apply Candidates apply through the J-PAL/IPA Common Application.

These “Lighthouses” will combine demonstrated impact and cost-effectiveness with strong learning systems and delivery models that can work through government. Position Overview:The Senior Manager will lead the development and launch of the Lighthouse Collaborative. They will work closely with Lighthouse organizations, governments, funders, academic institutions, and other partners to help proven organizations scale through public systems. Early priorities will include developing government partnerships that enable Lighthouse organizations to reach new populations at scale and building partnerships with academic institutions (e.g., graduate, business, and/or public policy schools) to source entrepreneurial talent that could help bring Lighthouse organizations to new geographies. The Senior Manager will lead key workstreams, manage the team, and be accountable for driving the initiative’s execution and results.J-PAL is recruiting a Senior Manager to contribute to this mission of promoting evidence-informed policy. The preferred location for this role is Cambridge, MA, based at MIT, with at least two in-person workdays per week. We will also consider candidates based in New York City or the San Francisco Bay Area. Exceptional candidates in other locations may be considered, provided they can maintain at least four hours of overlap with both Pacific and Eastern Time working hours.Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Build and manage the team: Recruit, manage, and develop a high-performing team, including likely additional regional / country hires as Lighthouse grows. This includes support high-priority projects led by J-PAL’s Global Executive Director and Chief of Staff to the Global Executive Director, and collaborating with teams across J-PAL Global and its regional offices covering Africa, Europe, Latin America, Middle East and North Africa, North America, South Asia, and Southeast Asia. Other tasks may include leading strategic and cross-organizational initiatives, recruitment, onboarding, training, and knowledge management, as well as pursuing professional development opportunities.Supervision Received:Senior Manager will report to the Global Executive Director of J-PAL. Supervision Exercised:None.Professional Development:Learn: J-PAL supports a culture of learning with opportunities to attend weekly MIT–Harvard Development Seminars and take classes for credit with MIT’s generous tuition assistance program. All J-PAL staff are also eligible to take the innovative online MITx MicroMasters credential in Data, Economics, and Development Policy (DEDP) free of charge.Engage: Managers have the opportunity to work with J-PAL-affiliated researchers, as well as interact with J-PAL’s partners, including decision-makers and practitioners, alongside senior staff. As core content creators, Managers’ publications are distributed to development stakeholders worldwide.Travel: Managers have the opportunity to occasionally present at J-PAL’s regional offices, attend policy events worldwide, and participate in a unique “Manager-to-Field” international experience supporting on-the-ground research during their time at J-PAL.Grow: Managers can expect to join a peer group eager to build institutional knowledge and pass on lessons learned. Managers receive one-on-one mentorship from senior staff. Benefits:As a member of the MIT community, you benefit from more than just your salary. J-PAL hires highly qualified staff and rewards them accordingly. Total compensation packages are competitive for the non-profit international development field with excellent MIT benefits, including comprehensive health insurance, a 401(k) match and pension-based retirement plan, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, MIT community discounts, a generous vacation policy, and more. We like working at MIT and think you will too. J-PAL also values work-life balance and offers flexible work days throughout the year; Cambridge-based staff are required to work in-person at least two days per week. Qualifications & Skills:Qualifications: Your technical expertise, strong communication and organizational skills, passion for translating research into action, and interest in international development make you an ideal candidate for Senior Policy Manager.Education: You hold a master’s degree in business, economics, social sciences, public policy, management, or a related field. Experience: You have 7 years of relevant professional experience. Ideal candidates will have experience in one or more of the following: launching or scaling an early-stage social venture; working in or with nonprofits or social enterprises; building partnerships with governments, philanthropic donors, or multilateral institutions; managing complex initiatives in international development; supporting evidence-informed policy and scale; or working in a specific policy sector or cross-cutting area such as climate, gender, health, education, social protection, or AI for social good.Experience working in international development and/or low- or middle-income countries is strongly preferred. Experience working directly with government partners, social ventures, or philanthropic funders is a plus.Entrepreneurial execution: You are a self-starter who is comfortable building in ambiguit

title: Senior Research Associate Education - Morocco Innovation and Evaluation Lab - J-PAL Middle East and North Africa
description: Skip to main content Senior Research Associate Education - Morocco Innovation and Evaluation Lab - J-PAL Middle East and North Africa Organization: J-PAL Middle East and North Africa Location: Rabat, Morocco Country: Morocco Education: Master's Other advanced degree Start Date (Earliest): 1 January 2027 Start Date (Latest): 1 March 2027 Language Requirement: Arabic English French Job summary:The Morocco Innovation and Evaluation Lab (MEL) is looking to hire a Senior Research Associate (SRA) to coordinate its research efforts to foster a culture of evidence-based policymaking in Morocco.The Senior Research Associate will support the implementation of an impact evaluation conducted by a team of international researchers in partnership with the UM6P- OCP ecosystem. This position will be based in our offices at the University Mohammed VI Polytechnic campus in Rabat.About the Morocco Innovation and Evaluation Lab (MEL):The MEL is a collaboration between the University Mohammed VI Polytechnic (UM6P), the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the Harvard Center for International Development (CID). The Morocco Innovation and Evaluation Lab emerged from the Morocco Employment Lab, an initiative that was launched in 2020 in partnership with the Millennium Challenge Account - Morocco Agency (MCA-Morocco) and hosted by the Policy Center for the New South. With the support of Community Jameel, the lab is expanding its work beyond employment into sectors such as education, social protection, firm growth, agriculture, and environment. The MEL works in close collaboration with the public, private, NGO, and philanthropic sectors in Morocco to conduct evaluations that speak to their priorities and share rigorous evidence to inform their decisions.About the position:The position offers a unique opportunity for the Senior Research Associate to support the research infrastructure of the Morocco Innovation and Evaluation Lab and assist the research project in the design and implementation of impact evaluations as well as data collection, management, and analysis, in an organization undertaking cutting-edge development research. The Senior Research Associate will be directly supervised by the MEL’s Director and the Research Manager. The Senior RA will work closely with senior staff from J-PAL and CID, academic researchers and other field staff to perform a variety of research tasks. This research project is a qualitative pilot study designed to inform the development of a full randomized controlled trial (RCT) aimed at strengthening equity in 1337's admissions process. It is conducted by affiliated and international researchers, including Esther Duflo (MIT), Bruno Crepon (ENSAE), Rema Hanna (Harvard University), Florencia Devoto (UM6P), and Kamil Kohen (Paris School of Economics).Key Responsibilities:The Senior Research Associate is responsible for the supervision of the project and its successful implementation in the field, which includes:Propose and, as appropriate, implement innovations in the different stages of a project in coordination with Principal Investigators;Maintain and grow effective relationships with partner organizations;Oversee and lead the field research activities, including the implementation of the evaluation, according to the research design in coordination with partners;Supervise a maximum of two Research Associates working on the projects;Assist with hiring survey firms, including drafting terms of reference;Liaising with field staff running the evaluations and collaborating with them including travel to research field sites;Conduct background research in conjunction with field research activities;Designing survey questionnaires, conducting qualitative research, refining study design and surveying instruments;Supervise in person or phone data collection and ensure the good quality of the data;Assist with the preparation of administrative databases;Assist with data cleaning and preliminary data analysis; andAny other work assigned by Principal Investigators.He/she will also be responsible for ensuring good communication and organization on a daily basis:Facilitate, strengthen and maintain effective and efficient communication as the primary contact point with Principal Investigators;Provide periodic updates on project activities to PIs and subject experts;Participate in the planning and design of any outreach activities;Ensure that project activities are on schedule and prepare project update reports according to agreements with funders and partners.Requirements:EducationA Master's Degree in economics, public policy, mathematics, statistics or related technical fields including training in microeconomics, econometrics, statistics, and advanced mathematics;Graduate-level coursework in economics is a plus.ExperienceMinimum 3 years of relevant experience, including 2 years of research experience;Experience with STATA and/or R data analysis software is a must; experience interpreting data analysis; experience with academic writing;Experience with budget management is a plus;Experience with living in Morocco is a strong advantage.SkillsVery strong quantitative, organisational, and communication skills are necessary;Fluency in French and in English. Arabic command is a strong advantage;Flexible, self-motivating, able to manage multiple tasks efficiently, and a team player;Demonstrated ability to manage high-level relationships with partner organisations;Familiarity with evaluation methods and randomized controlled trials preferred;Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines. How to Apply Send an email to [email protected], using the following as the email subject line: full name (first (given) name and last (family) name), followed by job title: “Senior Research Associate, Education (coding-school), Morocco Innovation and Evaluation Lab”. Please attach pdf copies of your CV and cover letter. Apply through the JPAL Common Application.Please submit your application no later than December 15, 2026 (at midnight).Given the volume of applications received, only short-listed candidates will be contacted for an interview.

title: Engagement Manager, Chanakya
description:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

Engagement Manager is a senior client-facing role in the vertical. You own pipeline development, account strategy, and long-term engagement management. This is a builder role for someone who understands the procurement landscape, can engage at the CXO and technical leadership level, and can convert complex AI capability into funded, deployable programmes.

What You'll Do

• Own the day-to-day management of active client engagements, from scoping and alignment through to operational handover and adoption

• Serve as the primary point of contact for clients across the engagement lifecycle; manage expectations proactively and honestly

• Translate client operational problems into precise briefs that deployment and engineering teams can act on

• Track delivery against commitments; surface risks early and drive resolution without waiting for escalation

• Work with Strategic Deployment Engineers to ensure what is being built reflects what the client actually needs

• Support pipeline development: account mapping, stakeholder outreach, and PoC scoping

• Build and maintain working relationships with mid-to-senior client stakeholders; grow account depth over time

• Surface ground-level observations back to the vertical as market intelligence

What We're Looking For

• 4–6 years of professional experience; foundational background at a top-tier consulting firm strongly preferred — with a track record of owning complex analytical work, structuring ambiguous problems, and being accountable for outcomes

• At least 2 years in strategic or complex enterprise GTM, account management, or programme delivery — where you owned client relationships, not just supported them

• Comfort operating in long-cycle, relationship-driven environments where trust is built over months, not deals

• Strong written and verbal communication, able to hold a room with senior stakeholders and write briefs that people act on

• Familiarity with GenAI or ML concepts sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and translate capability to clients

• Experience in or adjacent to defence, government, critical infrastructure and complex enterprises is a plus

Signals We Look For

• You've owned something - a client, a mandate - and driven it to a conclusion without being

managed to do it

• You've had to deliver a hard message to a client or stakeholder, done it early, and held the

relationship

• You think in structures. You make complex problems legible and actionable for the people who

need to move on them

• You've worked across functions — engineering, finance, policy, or operations — and made thing happen without formal authority

• Experience at a top-tier consulting firm; owning complex analytical problem-solving, structuring ambiguous mandates, and being accountable for outcomes is strongly valued.

Who You Are

• You treat client ownership as a baseline, not a virtue — if the engagement is in trouble, it's your problem to fix

• You are direct; you say what you actually think, including to people more senior than you

• You are comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely energised by environments where the answer isn't obvious

• You move with urgency and bring others with you through influence, not authority

Why Sarvam?

Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.

• Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

• High ownership and high impact, from day one

• Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems

• You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates

If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.

About the Role

Engagement Principal is a senior client-facing role in the Chanakya vertical. You own pipeline development, account strategy, and long-term engagement management across defence and strategic sector clients. This is not a quota-chasing sales role — it is a builder role for someone who understands the defence procurement landscape, can engage at the command and technical leadership level, and can convert complex AI capability into funded, deployable programmes.

 

What You’ll Do

• Own GTM strategy and pipeline for this vertical: from prospecting through programme initiation.

• Build and maintain relationships at the decision-making level: Acquisition directorates, CTO offices, field and HQ command, and PSU leadership.

• Translate Sarvam’s technical capability into proposals and narratives that resonate across technical and command-level stakeholders.

• Lead RFI/RFP responses, PoC scoping, and commercial negotiation — with full technical fluency.

• Collaborate with Strategic Deployment Engineers and the product team to ensure client expectations are grounded in what we can actually deliver.

• Manage account health, renewal strategy, and expansion pipeline for active accounts.

• Surface emerging requirements, policy shifts, and competitor moves that should shape our roadmap.

 

What We’re Looking For

• 7–12 years of total experience, with at least 4 years in strategic sector GTM, defence procurement consulting, or enterprise sales in a technical domain.

• Track record of closing and managing multi-crore engagements in disciplined or complex environments: defence, critical infrastructure, or complex enterprise clients.

• Functional understanding of defence procurement frameworks: DRDO, DPP, emergency procurement, Make-I/Make-II.

• Strong executive presence: comfortable in flag-level meetings and senior CTO offices, and equally comfortable with working-level technical teams.

• Active network in the Indian defence ecosystem (Army, Navy, IAF, DRDO, DPP offices, PSUs, DSSC) is an advantage.

 

Bonus Points

• You’ve built a pipeline in a domain where trust takes years — and moved it faster than expected.

description:

Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.

About the Role

This role sits at the intersection of customer success, technical problem-solving, and market intelligence. You’ll own API customer relationships end-to-end — running demos, debugging integrations, writing scripts to unblock customers, and relaying precise model feedback to Sarvam’s research teams. A strong fit for someone early in their career with genuine technical curiosity and excellent communication skills.

 

What You’ll Do

• Own customer relationships end-to-end: run demos, onboarding sessions, and integration walkthroughs; get customers from API key to working product fast; stay with them through production.

• Build and tinker: write scripts to unblock integrations, build small demo apps that show customers what’s possible, and create reference implementations others can reuse. Handle problems directly rather than escalating them.

• Be the voice of the customer inside Sarvam: relay model feedback (transcription errors, voice quality gaps, translation failures, LLM output issues) to research and engineering with enough specificity that they can reproduce and prioritise; then close the loop with the customer.

• Surface market insights: track what customers and prospects are building, map the competitive landscape, spot recurring patterns across accounts, and bring a point of view to GTM and Product — not just a data dump.

 

What We’re Looking For

• 3+ years in a customer-facing role: customer success, solutions, pre-sales, or developer advocacy at a tech company; strong internship experience counts (impact > years).

• Technically capable: you read API docs fluently, write basic Python or JS scripts, and debug integrations without hand-holding.

• Excellent communicator: confident on demos, clear in writing, equally effective with a business stakeholder and an engineer.

• Genuinely curious about AI: you want to understand how the models work, not just what they return, and you can characterise model errors with precision.

• Organised and proactive: multiple threads in the air, nothing dropped, no prompting needed.

 

Bonus Points

• Familiarity with speech, LLM, or document processing APIs: you know what good output looks like.

• Experience working with engineering or research teams: you can turn a customer complaint into a reproducible bug report.

title: GTM Strategy - Chanakya
description:
About team: 

Chanakya is Sarvam AI's specialised, self-contained vertical for national security and institutions of national importance. It carries its own pricing, business, product, engineering, custom-model and vendor functions under one roof — a complete unit built to solve the most complex problems in the strategic sector: the three armed forces, intelligence agencies, financial regulators, and institutions of national importance such as central ministries and national policy bodies.

What we deploy here must be at strategic parity or higher — anything less is a national-security risk. That standard is the reason Chanakya is a small, exceptionally high-performing team inside Sarvam, and the reason we are deliberate about who joins it.

Why this is one of the most consequential seats in Indian AI

01 — NATIONAL IMPACT

You sit where it all gets decided.

These systems are deployed inside the institutions that safeguard the country. The potential for national impact is not abstract — it is at the core of how the strategic sector reasons, decides, and acts. Few roles anywhere in Indian technology carry this weight.

02 — UNPARALLELED LEARNING

Full-stack, end to end — nowhere else does this exist.

Every deployment runs the entire stack: understanding a customer's real requirement, architecting and customising the stack for it, and where needed building and fine-tuning models, shaping training data, and inventing data representations for extraordinarily complex data, workflows and applications. You touch nearly the whole arc of the work. This experience sets you apart — whether you go on to found a company, or become a business or technology leader in the years ahead, at Sarvam or beyond.

03 — A PATH TO LEADERSHIP

These are leadership seats in the making.

Chanakya's functions are being built out now. We are looking for people who will grow into the leaders of these emerging functions — every one of these roles is a route to leading a part of the vertical, not just filling it.

Where we are. This is not a leap into the unknown. Chanakya has already achieved product–market fit to a meaningful degree, has significant revenue booked, and has large strategic projects officially underway. Things are structured and going well.

The opportunity. This is a genuine zero-to-one journey — but one taken within the reach, talent and standing of a company like Sarvam. You get the ambition and ownership of building something new, backed by the full weight of Sarvam's capability and presence. The golden opportunity: to help build out and lead the emerging functions of Chanakya, with a clear growth path ahead. 

Where client-facing instinct meets technical depth — working directly with the founders.

You will bring your client-facing judgement and technical fluency together to shape and drive Chanakya's go-to-market, working closely with the leadership and the founders to get it built.

•Strong technical foundation plus sharp commercial and strategic instincts.

•Comfortable in the room with senior institutional stakeholders and with our own engineers.

•Entrepreneurial temperament — owns outcomes end to end.

The bar. 

Across every one of these roles, we are looking for people who want to change the world and build something of national consequence — and who will grow into the leaders of Chanakya's verticals. If that is you, the ceiling here is set only by your ambition.

Base: Delhi NCR, with travel across India. All roles involve working inside restricted environments and travelling to client sites at short notice.

title: Product & Strategy Associate
description:
About:

The CEO's Office is a small, cross-functional team that incubates new products, drives the engagements that matter most to the company, and builds the systems that set and raise the bar for how teams across Sarvam work and collaborate. Problems arrive from research, product, and business, and they vary widely in shape and scope. As an Associate, you are a force multiplier for the CEO: you take an ambiguous problem, give it structure, and carry it to a result.

The work needs both breadth and depth. Breadth gives you context across the company and a clear sense of where the most important problems lie. Depth is how you deliver: you go deep on the ones that matter most and own their outcomes, working with the right people inside and outside Sarvam.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Drive 0-to-1 product and strategic bets from idea to a clear outcome, whether that ends in a working business line or a well-understood failure. The goal is to build an engine that comes up with ideas, researches and assesses them, builds and iterates on them, and takes the ones that work to steady state, often by handing them to a dedicated team.

 - Own key customer and partner engagements that are top of mind for the executive team.

 - Find new ways to use AI to set and raise the bar for how teams across Sarvam work and collaborate, and build the systems that make it happen.

 - Create the decks, memos, and prototypes that carry Sarvam's narrative to customers, partners, and government, and that represent the company.




WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - High agency: Ownership comes naturally to you. You drive work end to end, especially when the brief is ambiguous and the path is undefined.

 - Excessive curiosity: You are curious about AI and frontier technology well beyond what any job requires, and you follow new launches and research closely. You are eager to learn, and you are drawn to hard problems that new technology makes solvable.

 - Exceptional people skills: You write and speak clearly, collaborate well across teams, and build trust quickly, and you handle sensitive information with discretion. When a bet needs a team, you can lead it.

 - User obsession and agility: You start with the user’s pain points and reason from first principles about what would actually solve it. You use AI to build agents and products, and iterate quickly, and you keep going until you deliver real value and user delight.



What We’re Looking For

 - 2+ Years of work experience & a degree in engineering is preferred.

 - Excellent communicator: confident on demos, clear in writing, equally effective with a business stakeholder and an engineer.

 - Genuinely curious about AI: you want to understand how the models work, not just what they return, and you can characterise model errors with precision.

 - Organised and proactive: multiple threads in the air, nothing dropped, no prompting needed.

title: Senior Fellow (Digital Economy, Startups and Innovation)
description: Contact Us Search Senior Fellow (Digital Economy, Startups and Innovation) Location Experience New Delhi 10 Years The Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations (ICRIER) invites applications for the position of Senior Fellow in its Digital Economy, Startups and Innovation (DESI) team. The ideal candidate will bring a strong academic and economic policy background in areas such as digital transformation, technology policy, innovation, and entrepreneurship. The candidate will also bring analytical and critical thinking and data analysis skills, with a body of work in research, policy analysis and evaluation. The candidate must have a multi-disciplinary research orientation and understand the complex interplay between economics, emerging technologies, markets, and society. About ICRIER ICRIER is one of India’s premier economic policy think tanks, committed to its mission of “linking India with the world.” Established in 1981 to offer policy guidance in navigating external economic shocks, ICRIER has evolved into an independent development institution and a thought leader in inter-disciplinary research. The organization is widely recognized for providing rigorous, evidence-based, and policy-relevant insights aimed at advancing inclusive and sustainable development. ICRIER actively collaborates with governments (at both national and state levels), the private sector, multilateral organizations, and philanthropic foundations, serving as a crucial bridge between academic research and policy action. About DESI The work program of the DESI team at ICRIER sits at the intersection of digitalisation and development. It focuses on studying the economic impact of new technologies, benefits and risks associated with digital public infrastructure, startup ecosystems, data governance, and innovation policy. The programme engages with diverse stakeholders to provide policy-relevant research and practical insights into India’s evolving digital economy. The DESI team members also contribute extensively to the work program of ICRIER-Prosus Centre for Digital Economy (IPCIDE) and ICRIER and Vodafone Idea Centre for Telecom (InViCT). The Position The Senior Fellow will lead research and policy engagement in DESI’s focus areas. This role demands intellectual leadership, building strategic networks and collaborations, raising funds and bidding for projects, project management capabilities, and active participation in national and international policy discourse. Key Responsibilities Lead original and high-quality research on digital economy topics such as development impact of technologies, digital public infrastructure, tech startups, data governance, and innovation policy Conceptualize and oversee research studies, working papers, policy briefs, and stakeholder engagements under the DESI work program. Build partnerships with government agencies, academic institutions, industry bodies, and international organizations. Supervise and mentor junior researchers and research associates within the DESI team. Organize policy dialogues, roundtables, and conferences to disseminate research and generate impact. Represent ICRIER in national and international forums related to digital policy and innovation. Contribute to institutional development through fundraising, strategic planning, and thought leadership. description: Contact Us Search Research Associate (Climate Change, Urbanisation and Sustainability) Location Experience New Delhi 2 Years Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations: Recruitment Announcement Position: Research Associate (Climate Change, Urbanisation and Sustainability) Location: New Delhi Description: Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations (ICRIER), an autonomous, policy-oriented, not-for-profit, policy think tank based in New Delhi is looking for a Research Associate for its Climate Change, Urbanisation and Sustainability team. The team consists of seasoned professionals belonging to a variety of disciplines, covering multiple facets of this broad theme. The team is engaged in cutting-edge research employing a variety of models to tackle core energy and environmental issues. It offers its research services to different government ministries for shaping their negotiation stances at multiple forums such as the G20, UNFCCC, etc., and also provides timely insights into some of the key questions that the country is grappling with. Specifically, the CCUS division works on four major thrust areas: Clean Technologies and Green Growth: Techno-economics of energy transition solutions (clean power, transport systems and industrial decarbonisation), incl. clean fuels, combined with economic modelling to assess impacts on growth, international trade, carbon pricing and estimating financing needs and sources. Circular Economy and Environment: Economic analysis and modelling of energy transition impacts, with a focus on resource efficiency, recycling systems, critical raw materials, battery circularity, etc. Adaptation and Loss & Damage: Economic Modelling with a focus on energy transition impacts, international trade, carbon pricing and estimating financing needs and sources Job Requirements: Typical requirements include the following: An M.Phil. degree or MA/ MSc. (Economics / Statistics / related fields) from a reputed University with 2 years of work experience in policy research. Advanced quantitative skills are sought. Prior experience of working on econometric or statistical models (specifically optimization models) is required. Candidates with additional experience or training in environmental or energy economics or natural resource management would be preferred. The candidate should have excellent programming capabilities. S/he should be comfortable working on Stata, R or Python. Expertise in GAMS is an additional merit. As collation of data from multiple sources would be required, experience in handling large unit-level government data (ASI, NSSO Unit-level surveys, Census, etc.) is a must. Good research and writing skills. Willingness to travel for surveys, stakeholder meetings and other work-related engagements Work Responsibilities: The Research Associate will support the team with various environmental and climate change projects. The work comprises the following activities: Research and Knowledge Generation: The candidate will work in a fast-paced environment and assist the team with various research projects. S/he will be responsible for data collection, cleaning, and analysis. Research work may involve primary or secondary research, and the candidate must be comfortable with both. The collected knowledge will need to be documented in the form of reports/working papers/policy briefs/strategy papers/op-eds/journal articles, depending on the needs of the project. Stakeholder Management: Management and interaction with stakeholders are critical aspects of the job. The candidate must be comfortable with networking and interacting with stakeholders regularly. Project Management: The candidate is expected to help the team with managing the project and organising events, stakeholders’ meetings, roundtables, etc. The project management activities also include dissemination activities outlined in the project. While the abovementioned activities outline the responsibility of the candidate, it may not be limited to the same, and additional responsibilities could be assigned by the thematic lead. At ICRIER, we believe in recognizing and rewarding excellence. Our commitment to attracting top-tier talent is reflected in our comprehensive compensation package, which includes excellent benefits and a supportive, collegial work environment. As the need for this candidate is urgent, we would prefer candidates who are open to joining immediately or who have to serve minimal notice periods. To apply, kindly send your detailed CV along with a covering letter to jobs@icrier.res.in Last Date of Application: 17th August 2026. However, the application call will remain open until a suitable candidate is found. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further consideration. Candidates available to join immediately will be given preference To know more about ICRIER: www.icrier.org Apply Now @ 2026 ICRIER. All rights reserved. Privacy Policy / Terms & Conditions

title: Internship Programme
description: Skip to main content WHO / Christopher Black WHO Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, met with the 2019 cadre of interns at WHO HQ. They presented him with a map showing their geographic diversity. © Credits WHO Internship ProgrammeFor future leaders in public health A competent and dynamic health workforce at the heart of each health system is essential to advance global health goals. Countries need a pool of health professionals trained and exposed to the systems and processes in the health sector and who understand how stakeholders interact within the international health arena.WHO, as the leader in global public health issues, is committed to building a diverse pool of future leaders in public health. WHO's Internship Programme offers a wide range of opportunities for students and recent graduates to gain insight into the technical and administrative programmes of WHO and enrich their knowledge and experience in various areas, thereby contributing to the advancement of public health. What are the objectives?Provide a framework for assigning eligible students from diverse academic backgrounds to WHO programmes where their educational experience can be enhanced through capacity building opportunities.Provide an opportunity for WHO programmes to benefit from engagement from students specializing in various fields related to technical and administrative programmes of WHO.WHO offers internships in technical areas and administrative programmes such as communication, external relations or human resources. Who is eligible for an internship?Age: You are at least twenty years of age on the date of application.Education: You are enrolled in a course of study at a university or equivalent institution leading to a formal qualification (undergraduate, graduate, or postgraduate), in a public health, medical or social field related to the technical work of WHO, or in a management, administrative, communications, or external relations-related field. Applicants who have already completed a qualification may also qualify for consideration, if they apply to the internship within eighteen months following the completion of the formal qualification. You have completed three years of full-time studies at a university or equivalent institution prior to starting (bachelor's level or equivalent) the internship.Languages: You are fluent at least in one of the working languages of the office of assignment.Family relation: You are not related to a WHO staff member (e.g., son/daughter, brother/sister, or mother/father).Nationality: You hold a valid passport of a WHO Member State.Other: You have not previously participated in WHO’s Internship Programme. How to apply? We invite candidates from across the world to apply to the WHO Global Internship Programme. All applications must be made through the internship position vacancy notices posted on the WHO Careers site using the WHO online recruitment system (Stellis). There is no possibility to apply for an internship at WHO outside Stellis. More information on the recruitment process can be found in the FAQs section. Internship positions are available in various areas of work and in different organizational locations (regional offices, country offices or headquarters). As internship opportunities are posted on a continuous basis, with each containing different requirements and application deadlines, we encourage you to check the internship page regularly for new opportunities. Apply now Frequently asked questions Benefits of the WHO Internship ProgrammeWHO provides all interns with medical and accident insurance coverage during the duration of the internship period. Insurance coverage before the start date of the internship and after the end date of the internship, including travel to and from the duty station location, is the sole personal and financial responsibility of the individual intern.As of January 2020, WHO provides living allowance to eligible selected interns who need financial support. All interns must complete a legal Declaration of Interests form. This form requires intern candidates to declare any relevant financial disclosures, including any financial support in the form of grants bursaries, scholarships, etc. Based on the information provided in this form, the intern candidates’ eligibility to receive financial support from WHO will be assessed.Lunch vouchers may be provided at some duty stations. Watch this video to learn more about being an intern at WHO headquarters in Geneva. 19 October 2022 WHO Global Internship Programme TestimonialRyoko Takahashi Candidate obligations BEFORE an internship offer is extendedInterns must be available to work full-time for a minimum of six (6) weeks up to a maximum of 24 weeks duration, depending on the needs of the WHO technical unit.Interns must provide proof of enrolment in a course of studies or proof of completion of their last qualification.​Interns must disclose any circumstances that could give rise to a potential conflict of interest related to the subject of the activity in which they will be involved during their assignment (Declaration of Interest) including financial support for the internship. ​Interns must provide the completed WHO medical certificate of fitness for work form prior to the start of their internship.​Interns are requested not to send any documents until specifically asked to do so. Further informationInterns do not have the status of WHO staff members and shall not represent the Organization in any official capacity.Any employment with WHO shall be subject to established recruitment and selection procedures. Interns and former interns are free to apply as external candidates to any vacant positions open to external candidates and for which they are qualified.WHO does not sign any agreements, proposed or required by a sponsor, university or equivalent institution.WHO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/. Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and will require individual review. Please note that internships at WHO are very competitive and only a small number of applicants will be selected every year. Only successful candidates will be contacted. If not selected, you may apply again to other posted internship positions if you are still interested and if you meet the eligibility criteria.For internships in Geneva, SwitzerlandAn important reminder: Although WHO is now providing a living allowance to eligible interns (please see the exact amount in the vacancy notices), be aware that living in Geneva is expensive and finding accommodation can be challenging. Learn more Careers main page Apply for a position WHO environment Diversity, equity and inclusion

At ADB, we see you as a potential future leader and you will progress through: Fixed 3-year term appointment Start with an initial placement in an operations or operations support role in the ADB headquarters in Manila, Philippines. This initial assignment offers hands-on experience and exposure to our core operations, policies, and procedures, equipping you with the knowledge and insights to thrive and grow within the organization. Rotational assignment After 18 months, you will transition to a rotational assignment in another area of ADB. This will be aligned with both your career interests and our organizational needs, allowing you to grow your professional experience and deepen your subject matter expertise. It’s a valuable opportunity to advance professionally while contributing in a new and meaningful context within ADB. Muti-faceted development opportunities You will get to participate in a wide spectrum of activities, from facts-finding missions to policy studies and project executions. You’ll also be part of our Young Professional mentorship program, where our experienced technical international staff, many of whom began their careers as Young Professionals, will provide guidance and support that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Be 32 years old and below. Hold at least a first-level university degree with proven academic track record in a field relevant to the job role. Have at least three years of work experience relevant to ADB. Be passionate and committed to development work. Be a keen and agile learner with strong interpersonal skills. Have excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Application and Selection Apply in early September when the application process opens. Visit the “Current Opportunities” tab to explore available positions. Sign up for the ADB Job Alerts to stay in the loop of new postings. If you progress past this stage, you will be invited to panel interviews that take place between December and February. Check your application status through the application site here. Our HR team will also be in touch through email. Current Opportunities There are currently no open opportunities. For the ADB Young Professionals Program, only applicants 32 years old and below will be considered. I have less than three years of work experience. Should I apply? You need to have a minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience to be considered for the ADB Young Professionals Program, including internships. I applied to the ADB Young Professionals Program before. Can I apply again? Yes, you can apply again regardless of how far you have progressed in the application process previously, if you meet the eligibility requirements. What is the typical Young Professional progression? Young Professionals are international staff recruited at grade YP1. After the first 12 months probationary period, confirmed Young Professionals will be promoted to grade YP2. A Young Professional’s promotion to Grade TI1 occurs upon absorption into an assigned position. What is the curriculum of the ADB Young Professional Program? You will start your term with an 18-month initial assignment to either a solutions department (such as Climate, Thematic, or Private Sector Operations Department) or a major non-operational department in HQ (such as Economic Research and Development Impact Department (ERDI) or Office of Markets Development and Private Partnership (OMDP).
