title: Visiting Fellow Program
description: Skip to main content Careers at ADB Step into a job that uplifts lives for millions across Asia and the Pacific. Work with us to solve the region’s complex challenges and deliver development solutions that support sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth. Make Your Move. Home Opportunities Current Opportunities Opportunities Highlights ADB Recruitment Process What We Offer What We Offer Life at ADB Expatriate Spouse Connect Program ADB Staff Association Talent Programs Young Professionals Program Internship Program Japan Scholarship Program Visiting Fellow Program FAQs Contacts ADB Visiting Fellow Program Researchers and academics in the field of economics are instrumental to our development efforts. We invite you to present your ongoing work and trade thoughts with leading experts at the ADB headquarters in Manila. Our ongoing research topics Climate change and environmental sustainability Digital transformation Human capital, jobs, and the future of work Inclusive development Macro and financial stability Private sector development Regional cooperation and integration Your Experience at ADB Join the conversation You’ll exchange research ideas and advise on our current and upcoming projects with our team—experts with deep, on-the-ground experience across the region. Inspire the future You’ll present or lecture on your perspective on a research topic of mutual interest. These include climate change and environmental sustainability, digital transformation, human capital and the future of work, inclusive development, macro and financial stability, private sector development, and regional cooperation and integration. What To Know Eligibility You should hold a PhD in Economics or a related discipline such as development economics, public policy, finance, political economy, statistics, or data science with strong economic applications. A strong research track record is important, demonstrated through publications in high-impact, peer-reviewed academic journals, preferably indexed in SSCI, ESCI, or recognized field-specific rankings. Experience in conducting empirical research using rigorous quantitative or qualitative methods is essential, along with the ability to translate research into policy recommendations or contribute to policy-relevant projects. Application period Applications are accepted annually from 1 January to 31 March. Selection A selection committee chaired by ADB’s Chief Economist will review applications in the second quarter of the year. This will be based on background, expertise, and research relevance. Only successful applicants will be notified by 31 July. Conditions of visit As a successful applicant of the ADB Visiting Fellow Program, you will: Register in the ADB Consultant Management System Come to ADB headquarters in Manila for 5–20 working days Agree on your visit timing with ADB Be assigned an ADB staff as your host Deliver agreed outputs within the set timeframe Publish the research paper as an ADB Economics Working Paper Onboarding Following the selection committee’s decision, you may receive: Economy airfare reimbursement on the most direct, cost-effective route Access to an office space during your visit Per diem and allowance for hotel, meals, and other travel-related expenses A modest honorarium Non-entitlement: Your benefits exclude participation in ADB’s medical and dental retainer plans, staff retirement plan, salary, privileges, immunities, and other privileges for ADB staff. Security: You will be liable for your own security and safety and are advised to register with your respective embassy in Manila. In case of evacuation from the country, you will follow the embassy’s contingency planning. title: Internship Program
description: Skip to main content Careers at ADB Step into a job that uplifts lives for millions across Asia and the Pacific. Work with us to solve the region’s complex challenges and deliver development solutions that support sustainable, inclusive, and resilient growth. Make Your Move. Home Opportunities Current Opportunities Opportunities Highlights ADB Recruitment Process What We Offer What We Offer Life at ADB Expatriate Spouse Connect Program ADB Staff Association Talent Programs Young Professionals Program Internship Program Japan Scholarship Program Visiting Fellow Program FAQs Contacts ADB Internship Program Asian Development Bank 2026 Internship Program is officially open for applications! Graduate students can apply by 16 March 2026. The program is built around research assignments reflecting our current business needs. You will contribute to meaningful impact from day one through the project-oriented learning opportunity. Get Your Head Start Motivated, open-minded, and self-directed learners like you can gain: Hands-on work experience in a major international development organization with a multicultural environment. Global exposure via collaboration with professionals from over 50 countries. Deep insights into development finance. Real-world impact through research outputs. Eligibility Application and Selection Current Opportunities Check Your Eligibility To be eligible for the ADB Internship Program, you must: Be a national of an ADB member country. Possess an excellent command of English. Be enrolled in a Master’s or PhD-level program from a school in an ADB member nation for the entire duration of the internship. Be engaged in academic study in any of the diverse fields that are directly related to ADB’s work. Preferably have 2-3 years of relevant professional experience. We embrace diversity and welcome applicants from a wide range of academic backgrounds. Application and Selection Choose an assignment from the options listed under the “Current Opportunities” tab. Submit your application through the ADB Career and Employment System (ACES), along with documents like CV and Proof of Enrolment. Submissions after the deadline will not be considered. You will be notified if you are invited for an interview. Selections will be made in March-April for interns starting in June. The internship will be for minimum of eight (8) weeks to a maximum of twelve (12) weeks. Current Opportunities There are currently no open opportunities. Note: We encourage you to sign up for job alerts to be notified when new positions become available. Frequently Asked Questions What is the purpose of the ADB Internship Program? The ADB Internship Program provides support for policy research and knowledge sharing with the broader academic community. It also identifies possible future candidates for staff positions. Can undergraduate students apply? No. The ADB Internship Program is only open to students currently enrolled in a Master’s or PhD-level program. What are the internship assignments and application submission deadline? Internship assignments are posted with complete information, including strict application deadlines, at ADB.org. I’m not a national of an ADB member but enrolled in a school of its members. Can I apply? No. The ADB Internship Program is only open to nationals of ADB member countries. I have a relative in ADB. Can I apply? No. ADB does not accept applications from close relatives of ADB staff, such as: Spouse* Children (natural and adopted) Mother Father Brother (including half-brother) Sister (including half-sister) Niece Nephew Aunt Uncle * ADB is piloting a spouse employment program to allow the consideration of spouse and registered domestic partner candidates of international staff for international staff vacancies. This pilot does not apply to spouse or registered domestic partner candidates of national and administrative staff. I am a spouse of an ADB International Staff. Can I apply? Yes, if you meet the eligibility requirements. Is this a paid internship? All interns will receive a stipend for the duration of the internship, unless they fall under a special arrangement category between select schools and ADB. What expenses should I plan for? You will cover your accommodation, transportation, food expenses, and part of the airfare. It is also a strict requirement to purchase a comprehensive insurance coverage for the entire period of the internship prior to departure to Manila. Does ADB offer assistance with airfare expenses? ADB will cover a limited part of the airfare travel cost, should air travel be necessary between the internship location and the authorized point of origin (i.e. school location). I am interested in interning at one of the Resident Missions. Is it available? Internship assignments are mostly based at the ADB’s headquarters in Manila, Philippines. Resident Missions may offer assignments (locations are specified in the posting). How do I know if I’m selected? The application site features updates of every application stage. Our HR team will also be in touch directly through email. Can I travel during my internship? As a general rule, interns are not allowed to travel during the internship assignment. I am required to apply for a visa. How will ADB help? For Manila-based internships, you must ensure that your passport is valid for at least 6 months prior to arrival and departure from Manila. If your nationality requires an entry visa, ADB will request it from the Philippine Embassy in your location, where you can submit your visa application. What are my working hours? The regular work schedule is 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with a one-hour lunch break. Any other preferred scheduled should be discussed with supervisors. I am a past intern. Can I apply? Past interns are not eligible to apply for the ADB Internship Program. Will my internship lead to employment with ADB? Completing an internship does not automatically qualify for employment at ADB. Former interns are welcomed to apply for open positions after graduation. Ready for YouSign up for ADB Job Alerts to be notified when application opens. title: Scholarship Program
description: Skip to main content Scholarships in Asia and the Pacific The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (JSP) offers about 130 graduate scholarships a year for studies in economics, business and management, science and technology, and other development-related fields. Main Academic Institutions Procedures for Applying FAQs Alumni Association ADB-Japan Scholarship Program Since April 1988, with financing from the Government of Japan, we have offered citizens from developing member countries of ADB the opportunity to pursue graduate studies in 27 selected educational institutions across Asia and the Pacific, including 17 in Japan. As a scholar on the program, you will return to your home country after your studies to apply and share your new knowledge and skills to promote socioeconomic development. Find Your Field Science and Technology Agriculture Biological Science Computer Science Energy Engineering Environment Forestry Genetics Health Economics, Business and Management Accounting Business Administration/Management Commerce E-Business Entrepreneurship Economics Finance International Cooperation Social Sciences Development Studies Asia Paciﬁc Studies Development Management Development Studies Law and Public Policy International Business Law International Environmental Law Policy Studies Political Science Public Administration Public Policy What We Offer The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program provides: Full tuition fees Monthly subsistence allowance (including housing) Books and instructional materials Medical insurance Travel expenses For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for thesis preparation. In special circumstances, computer literacy, preparatory language and other similar courses may be covered under the scholarship. JSP Brochure ADB-JSP Annual Reports Eligibility and Application Check Your Eligibility General requirements You should: Be a national of an ADB borrowing member country and Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible country. Not hold dual citizenship of any developed country. Have gained admission to an approved master’s course at a Designated Institution. Hold a bachelor's degree or its equivalent with superior academic record. Have at least two (2) years of full-time professional working experience (acquired after a university degree) at the time of application. You must have proficiency in oral and written English communication skills to be able to pursue studies. Not be more than 35 years old at the time of application, unless waived in exceptional cases with the expressed endorsement of the Government of Japan. Be in good health. Agree to return and work in your home country for at least two (2) years after completion of studies under the Program in order to contribute to its development. Not be an Executive Director, Alternate Director, management, staff and consultant of ADB, or the close relatives of the aforementioned by blood or adoption with the term "close relative" defined as: spouse, mother, stepmother, father, stepfather, sister, stepsister, brother, stepbrother, son, daughter, aunt, uncle, niece, or nephew. Not be a staff of ADB–Japan Scholarship Program Designated Institutions. Not be living or working in a country other than your home country. Not be already enrolled in graduate degree programs. Citizenship The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program is available if you are a citizen of these countries and areas: Afghanistan Armenia Azerbaijan Bangladesh Bhutan Cambodia Cook Islands Federated States of Micronesia Fiji Georgia India Indonesia Kazakhstan Kiribati Kyrgyz Republic Lao People’s Democratic Republic Malaysia Maldives Marshall Islands Mongolia Myanmar Naoero Nepal Niue Pakistan Palau Papua New Guinea Philippines Samoa Solomon Islands Sri Lanka Tajikistan Thailand Timor-Leste Tonga Turkmenistan Tuvalu Uzbekistan Vanuatu Viet Nam Application and Selection Request for information and application forms from your choice of a partner institution. Complete and send required application documents to the partner institution, which include the ADB-Japan Scholarship Program information sheet. Receive evaluation results from partner institution following its assessment and shortlisting of applicants and final selection of scholars by ADB, based on the selection criteria applied by the Japanese executive director. description: Skip to main content Senior Urban Development Specialist Job Vacancy | Friday, October 30, 2026 SHARE THIS PAGE Reference Number 261005 Position Grade TI2 Department Sectors Department 2 Division Water and Urban Development Sector Cluster Location Papua New Guinea Resident Mission Date Posted Friday, October 30, 2026 Closing Date Saturday, November 14, 2026 11:59 p.m. (2359 Manila Time, 0800 GMT) Join Our Mission to Foster Prosperity in Asia Are you ready to make a difference in the future of Asia and be a catalyst for positive change? We are thrilled to offer a unique opportunity to become an important part of the prestigious Asian Development Bank (ADB). At ADB, our mission is simple yet powerful: to alleviate poverty and promote sustainable development in the Asia-Pacific region. Organizational Setting and Reporting Relationship While the position of Senior Urban Development Specialist resides with the Water and Urban Development Sector Cluster (WUD) within the Sectors Department 2 (SD2), you will be outposted to Papua New Guinea Resident Mission (PNRM) within the Pacific Department (PARD) for an initial assignment of three years. After this period, subject to business need, the role may be assigned at our Headquarters in Manila, Philippines or at another resident mission. Relocation is required. All reasonable relocation expenses will be covered. You will report to Country Director, PNRM, and Director, SD2-WUD. You will oversee junior team members and consultants. Your Role As Senior Urban Development Specialist, you will oversee operations in water supply, sanitation, urban flood management, solid waste management, urban policy and governance, municipal finance, affordable housing, and tourism. Working across the East Asia and Pacific region, including People's Republic of China, Mongolia, and ADB's 14 Pacific Developing Member Countries (DMCs). You will lead policy dialogue; formulate sector policies and strategies; lead the identification, preparation, processing, implementation and administration of loans, grants, and technical assistance (TA) projects; and provide technical support and knowledge solutions to relevant stakeholders. For PNG, you will be designated as WUD's sector cluster lead and represent the sector cluster on PNG's Country Management Team. You will be responsible for ADB's business development in the sector cluster ensuring that operations remain responsive to country requests for assistance, and are aligned with the country's policies and strategies. You will ensure that ADB's sector cluster operations in PNG are well coordinated with other development partner assistance in the sector. You will also coordinate with development partners, maintain high-quality sector diagnostics and knowledge products, including updated sector cluster assessments, and oversee the satisfactory implementation of ADB's ongoing sector cluster operations. You will: Sector Strategy, Policy Dialogue, and Pipeline Development Lead policy dialogue with government counterparts, advising on sector reforms, institutional strengthening, and good practices to strengthen country water and urban development sector performance. Assess water and urban development sector policies, strategies, and programs with a view of ensuring comparability to international best practices, smart solutions, and technological advances, and responsiveness to development needs. Identify the priority areas in the urban development sector for ADB support based on government requests for assistance, and the modality and nature of the required assistance, i.e. investment and TA support. Provide guidance on inquiries related to the water and urban development sector development and governance reforms in PNG and other countries. Project Preparation, Processing, and Administration Lead the preparation, processing, and administration of loans, grants, and TA projects in the area of water and urban development with due attention to country's development policies and projects' impacts on climate change. Coordinate with other Regional Departments (RDs), Office of Safeguards, and Climate Change and Sustainable Development Department in identifying, developing, implementing, and administering loans, grants, and TA projects for the water and urban development sector. In collaboration with Procurement, Portfolio and Financial Management Department (PPFD) project focal, propose appropriate contract modalities and support discussions on procurement issues including review of bidding documents and bid evaluation reports. Integrated and Innovative Solutions Collaborate with other sector offices and departments, including Private Sector Operations Department (PSOD), and Office of Market Development and Public-Private Partnerships (OMDP), to propose integrated solutions in response to the region's needs. Identify and introduce innovative and smart solutions and international best practices in the design and administration of loans, grants, and TAs, and promote regional knowledge sharing between East Asia and Pacific DMCs. Partnerships and Knowledge Develop and maintain strategic partnerships with external partners for knowledge and project opportunities. Respond to external inquiries. Lead in generating and disseminating knowledge solutions from ADB operations, international best practices, and country or region specific cross-learning in the urban development sector. Lead relevant in-house studies and seminars and prepare reports or policy briefs on topics crucial to ADB's water and urban development sector operations. Team Leadership and Other Responsibilities Lead, oversee, and support reporting staff, including their performance and development. Ensure the ongoing learning and development of reporting staff. Mentor junior staff and support their learning and integration. Perform other responsibilities as assigned and reflected in your workplan. Qualifications You will need: Master's degree in civil engineering, environmental engineering, urban and regional planning, urban and environmental management, or related fields; or University degree and at least 5 years of relevant work experience may be considered. At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in urban development and municipal service improvement and/ or water utilities, urban and/ or water sector cluster development, and in project preparation and administration of projects, practical knowledge, and experience. Preference to candidates with experience delivering projects and policies with integration of financial, economic, social, social, institutional, and safeguard requirements and experience of project design and execution. International experience working in several countries. Experience in the Pacific region is preferable. Broad experience preparing investment projects and analysis of relevant development policies, including knowledge on procurement and consultant recruitment. Demonstrated team leadership or managerial skills and experience leading professionals, teams, and missions for technical matters and projects processing/implementation. Significant expertise within a specific area of ADB's or similar MDBs and/or bilateral development institutions' operations (economic, sector, or thematic), or breadth across multiple areas with in-depth knowledge within one area. Proficiency in expressing ideas in both spoken and written formats in English. Two years of relevant experience outside ADB within the past five years is required. Years as an ADB-engaged consultant or contractor are considered experience outside of ADB. Please refer to the link for ADB Competency Framework for Technical International 2 (TI2). The salary will be based on ADB's standards and comparator markets, taking into account your qualifications and experience. title: Senior Private Sector Development Specialist / 260972
description: Skip to main content Senior Private Sector Development Specialist Job Vacancy | Thursday, November 5, 2026 SHARE THIS PAGE Reference Number 260972 Position Grade TI2 Department Central and West Asia Department Division Private Sector Development Unit, CWRD Location Kazakhstan Resident Mission Date Posted Thursday, November 5, 2026 Closing Date Monday, November 16, 2026 11:59 p.m. (2359 Manila Time, 0800 GMT) Join Our Mission to Foster Prosperity in Asia Are you ready to make a difference in the future of Asia and be a catalyst for positive change? We are thrilled to offer a unique opportunity to become an important part of the prestigious Asian Development Bank (ADB). At ADB, our mission is simple yet powerful: to alleviate poverty and promote sustainable development in the Asia-Pacific region. Organizational Setting and Reporting Relationship The position of Senior Private Sector Development Specialist is assigned to the Private Sector Development Unit (CWPS) within the Central and West Asia Department (CWRD). You will be outposted to our Kazakhstan Resident Mission office in Astana, Kazakhstan and relocation is required. All reasonable relocation expenses will be covered. You will report to the Country Director, KARM and Regional Head, CWPS and will oversee junior team members. Your Role As a Senior Private Sector Development Specialist, you will lead ADB's work in the Central and West Asia Region to support ADB's private sector development priority with primary responsibility for Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic, and Tajikistan, while also providing support to private sector development activities in other CWRD countries, as needed. You will work closely with country teams, governments, private sector stakeholders, development partners across the region. You will: Work with Country Management Teams to enhance synergies between sovereign and non-sovereign operations, support policy reforms that promote private sector development, and contribute to the design of policy-based lending operations. Contribute to the development of ADB's strategies and policies to support private sector development in collaboration with other departments. Conduct policy dialogue with governments, development partners, and private sector stakeholders to promote private sector development, private investment, and public-private partnership opportunities, including reforms that strengthen the enabling environment for private sector participation. Lead early-stage advisory engagements with public and private clients and investment-like engagements where ADB contributes time and funds to develop projects for future investments. Advance early-stage private sector development opportunities, including policy, institutional, market-building, and project development interventions that can contribute to future investment and advisory operations. Contribute to the development of the private sector nonsovereign and transaction advisory portfolio by identifying investment and advisory opportunities, participating in internal approval processes and other related activities in collaboration with ADB solutions, PSOD and OMDP in particular, with whom CWPS collaborate closely. Prepare and manage technical assistance projects, including contributions to regional programs that promote private sector development. In partnership with PSOD and OMDP, deliver private sector development (PSD) training and capacity-building programs for DMC counterparts in Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic, and Tajikistan. Organize and contribute to relevant knowledge-sharing activities. Support the development and execution of private sector development priorities in the assigned countries, while contributing to regional initiatives, including the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program, and supporting other private sector development activities across CWRD. Identify, design, process, implement, and evaluate projects, and other interventions to promote innovative and structured financing solutions using new approaches and modalities in ADB's developing member countries in the CWRD region. Lead the selection and management of individual consultants and consulting firms, including designing the terms of reference for specialized consulting services. Provide leadership and support to reporting staff - where applicable, manage their performance, provide clear direction and regular monitoring and feedback on performance and ensure their ongoing learning and development. Build and maintain relationships with prospects, clients, and government officials. Perform other tasks as assigned and reflected in your workplan. Qualifications You will need: Master's degree or equivalent, in business or finance related field; or University degree in finance, business and/or related fields combined with at least 5 years specialized experience relevant to the position can be considered. At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in commercial finance, investment banking, or transaction advisory working with private sector investors, banks, governments or international organizations. Extensive expertise in private sector development advisory and investment operations, demonstrate broad experience, and work independently across varied assignments, while closely collaborating with the Private Sector Operations Department (PSOD) and the Office of Market Development and Public Private Partnerships (OMDP). Two years of relevant experience outside ADB within the past five years is required. Years as an ADB-engaged consultant or contractor are considered experience outside of ADB. International experience working in several countries, experience working in Central and West Asia would be an advantage. Experience developing innovative financing structures, particularly in transition economies. Familiarity with multilateral development institutions' processes, financing products and modalities. Excellent English written and verbal communication skills. Knowledge of the Russian language would be an advantage. Please refer to the link for ADB Competency Framework for TI2. Benefits ADB offers a rewarding salary and a comprehensive benefits package. The salary will be based on ADB's standards and comparator markets, taking into account your qualifications and experience. Housing and education allowance (if applicable) Expatriate benefits (if applicable) Retirement plan (if applicable) Medical and health benefits Paid leave (including parental) Life and other insurance plans Staff development Additional Information This appointment is open to internal and external applicants. This position is crucial to the Workforce Rebalancing Framework (2022-2027), a strategic initiative aimed at enhancing ADB's in-house expertise previously sourced from the external workforce. The role seeks seasoned experts with substantial field experience capable of leading policy dialogue, and projects focused on delivering knowledge solutions. Successful applicants may occasionally undertake short-term assignments in other departments or offices, when required. This is a fixed term appointment with option to renew, initially for a period of up to 3 years, or up to the Normal Retirement Date (NRD), whichever comes earlier, for the purpose(s) and conditions determined by ADB, in accordance with Administrative Order No. 2.01 (Recruitment and Appointment). After the initial fixed-term period, ADB may choose to renew the appointment for up to an additional 3 years or not renewed. This decision will be made in the overall interest of ADB, based on factors including but not limited to the requirement of Staff's particular blend of skills and experience for the medium-term work program of the organizational unit, sufficient funding to cover the renewed period, and Staff's performance and suitability for employment. description: Skip to main content Associate Investment Officer Job Vacancy | Tuesday, October 27, 2026 SHARE THIS PAGE Reference Number 261012 Position Grade TL4 Department Private Sector Operations Department Division Trade and Supply Chain Division Location Asian Development Bank Headquarters Date Posted Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Closing Date Wednesday, November 11, 2026 11:59 p.m. (2359 Manila Time, 0800 GMT) Join Our Mission to Foster Prosperity in Asia Are you ready to make a difference in the future of Asia and be a catalyst for positive change? Strong analytical, project management, organizational, and stakeholder coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines. title: Internship Programme
description: The OECD Internship Programme is designed to bring highly qualified and motivated students with diverse backgrounds into the Organisation to work on projects linked to the Strategic Orientations of the Secretary-General and to support the corporate functions of the Organisation. Its main goal is to give successful candidates the opportunity to improve their analytical and technical skills in an international environment. Successful candidates will carry out research and provide support to Policy Analysts in one of the following areas. Please note that the list is non-exhaustive. Agriculture and Fisheries Artificial Intelligence Bribery and corruption Competition Corporate Governance Development Development Effectiveness Digitalisation Economy Education and Skills Employment Energy Environment EthicsFinance Gender and DiversityGlobal Relations Health Industry, Innovation and Entrepreneurship Insurance and Pensions International Migration Monitoring and Evaluation Investment Nuclear Energy Public Governance Regional Development Regulatory Reform Science and Technology Statistics Tax Tourism Trade and Agriculture Transport For internships in the Corporate functions, successful candidates will be involved in one of the following areas: Communications, Media & Public Relations Event Management Finance, Budget and Accounting Human Resources Information Technology Legal services Office Administration Translation Examples of work entrusted to interns include: Participating in the preparation of studies and documents; Carrying out research and reviews of existing materials; Collecting, organising and analysing data; Contributing to the production of documents, working papers and publications resulting from the above activities, including drafting notes and preparing technical annexes; Participating in meetings and seminars; Liaising and building networks with officials in national administrations, researchers, other international organisations and member country Delegations; Contributing to the organisation of events, communication, planning and evaluation. Academic Background Full-time student enrolled in an in-person, degree-awarding programme for the duration of the internship in a field or discipline related to the work of the OECD. Professional Background International experience through studies, internships or professional activities would be an asset. Tools Solid quantitative and computer skills. Knowledge of Microsoft Office. Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and/or knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. Key Competencies Strong analytical skills demonstrated by academic success and professional achievements. Strong interest in the work of OECD in promoting international co-operation. Ability to plan and conduct research independently. Good organisational skills, ability to work effectively on the basis of general instructions, with the capacity to prioritise tasks, often according to tight deadlines. Proven ability to work in a multicultural and team oriented environment and to adapt to changing working methods and technologies. Very good drafting and communication skills.

title: Economist (Consultant)
description:
ABOUT IDINSIGHT



We're a global data and evidence advisory, working with governments, philanthropies, and non-profits to improve lives at scale, using technology and AI where they can deliver the most impact.



IDinsight is a global nonprofit that equips leaders with the data, evidence and technology to improve lives at scale. We partner with governments, NGOs, multilaterals, and funders to support decisions at every stage of their impact journey – from bold pilots to nationwide scale-ups. Our teams bring rigorous evidence and practical insights so leaders can make informed decisions that truly change lives. With our partners, we are pioneering the next frontier of social impact, where data and technology accelerate progress for millions. We help leaders overcome the three main barriers to impact:

 1. Figuring out what works

 2. Learning and improving

 3. Reaching and operating at scale

We work in multiple countries across Asia and Africa. Our work spans a wide range of sectors, including agriculture, education, health, governance, sanitation, financial inclusion, and other areas.

We have expertise in a variety of rigorous approaches and methodologies, which we tailor to each client depending on their needs and constraints. To achieve a positive social impact we:

 - Support our partners with the full ‘data and evidence’ value chain – from primary data collection to data systems, monitoring evaluation and learning tools, and data science

 - Inform funding decisions – toward high-impact initiatives and away from less effective programs or approaches

 - Create cutting-edge AI-for-good products that make the delivery of social interventions and learning tools more cost-effective and scalable

Our diverse, growing team of roughly 250 outstanding colleagues operate in nearly two dozen countries around the world.  Learn more about our mission, values, and principles at www.IDinsight.org http://www.IDinsight.org.




JOINING IDINSIGHT AT THIS MOMENT

IDinsight is entering an exciting new phase of growth. As demand for rigorous evidence and AI-enabled solutions accelerates across the sectors and geographies we work in, we are actively investing in our teams, deepening our regional footprint, and expanding the frontier of what data and technology can do for social impact. This is a moment of real momentum for IDinsight. We're looking for people who want to use data and evidence to improve lives at scale; who are energized by taking on problems without a playbook; and who want a hand in shaping what IDinsight becomes as we grow.




ABOUT THE ROLE

IDinsight engages economists as consultants (hereafter "the Consultant") to bring specialist expertise in applied microeconomics and causal inference to a portfolio of client engagements spanning multiple geographies, sectors, and methods. Engagements may be scoped broadly or specialised along any of these dimensions, depending on the Consultant's expertise and IDinsight's needs.


The core of the role is judgment under constraint. The Consultant will be asked to think critically about how to maximise methodological rigour within our clients' time, operational, political, and budget limits. and to be explicit about the trade-offs that follow. The ideal candidate is comfortable moving between unfamiliar problems, can quickly absorb a programme's theory of change and a client's decision needs, and can give clear, actionable guidance on how to proceed.


The scope of a typical engagement may include:

 - Research design and analysis. Designing and advising on evaluations and other research activities (impact evaluations, descriptive and diagnostic studies, process evaluations, monitoring systems, programme design and advisory, M&E advisory, and scale-up analysis) with a focus on identification strategy, estimation, and interpretation.

 - Technical review and quality assurance. Drafting and reviewing technical documents, including evaluation designs, pre-analysis plans, power and sample size calculations, data collection instruments, analysis code, and technical reports. The Consultant may also be asked to resolve discrete technical questions that arise for project teams mid-implementation.

 - Technical capacity building, where scoped. Where included in the terms of reference, preparing and delivering training on technical topics (for example causal inference, statistical inference, or Stata/R programming) and providing targeted technical mentoring to project staff.

 - Scoping support. Advising on the technical feasibility and design of prospective engagements, in line with IDinsight's commitment to client-focused and decision-focused research.
   

Deliverables, timelines, level of effort, and reporting lines are set out in the engagement's terms of reference. The Consultant is expected to meet agreed deadlines, communicate proactively where scope or feasibility shifts, and flag methodological concerns early rather than at the point of delivery.





QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - Advanced degree in economics, econometrics, applied statistics, or a closely related quantitative field. PhD preferred; candidates with a Master's degree and a demonstrable record of comparable applied research will be considered.

 - Demonstrated command of causal inference and applied microeconometrics, including experimental and quasi-experimental identification strategies, power analysis, and the interpretation of imprecise or null results.

 - At least 5 years of relevant post-graduate experience designing, executing, or advising on evaluations and quantitative research in low- and middle-income country contexts.

 - Proficiency in Stata or R, sufficient to write, review, and debug analysis code that others will reproduce.

 - Ability to produce clear written technical output (evaluation designs, pre-analysis plans, technical memos) that a non-technical decision-maker can act on.

 - Capacity to work independently against agreed deliverables and timelines, with limited day-to-day supervision, and to flag methodological or feasibility concerns early.

Preferred

 - Substantive expertise in one or more of IDinsight's sectors (health, education, agriculture, social protection, governance, or environment).

 - Contextual knowledge of one or more regions where IDinsight works, including familiarity with relevant administrative or survey data sources.

 - Experience advising government or foundation counterparts directly, including translating methodological trade-offs into decision-relevant terms.

 - Experience with additional programming or data tools (Python, SQL, geospatial analysis, SurveyCTO or equivalent).

 - Peer-reviewed or policy publications drawing on applied field research.

 - Filipino citizen with extensive professional experience within the Philippine context.




NUTS & BOLTS

Contracting

This is an hourly consultancy engagement. Rates are commensurate with qualifications and experience and will be confirmed during the selection process. Anticipated volume is approximately 20 hours per month, though this may vary with project cycles. Work is assigned and approved in advance and invoiced monthly. This is a contractor engagement and does not include employee benefits.


Work authorization

If you’re not willing to sponsor work authorization: IDinsight is not able to sponsor work authorization for this role. Successful candidates will not require IDinsight to sponsor their work authorization in the office in which they'll be based.

If you’re willing to sponsor work authorization: IDinsight is able to sponsor employment visas for all nationalities in these locations; however, we will prioritize candidates who do not require IDinsight to sponsor work authorization in the aforementioned countries. All candidates who are not currently located in our country offices listed above will be expected to relocate to their office locations at the onset of their employment.

description:

WE'RE A GLOBAL DATA AND EVIDENCE ADVISORY, WORKING WITH GOVERNMENTS, PHILANTHROPIES, AND NON-PROFITS TO IMPROVE LIVES AT SCALE, USING TECHNOLOGY AND AI WHERE THEY CAN DELIVER THE MOST IMPACT.

JOINING IDINSIGHT AT THIS MOMENT

ABOUT THE ROLE

As IDinsight's West and North Africa (WNA) region grows, we are opening an office in Abuja, Nigeria, and are seeking a Senior Manager to help establish operations there and lead client engagements while building IDinsight’s portfolio of work in Nigeria. 
This dual role combines the analytical and client-facing work of a Senior Manager with the Office Lead responsibilities for the Abuja office. We expect roughly 70% of the role's time to go to client work and 30% to office leadership, with office responsibilities heavier during the first 6–12 months of set-up. The role reports to the WNA Regional Director.

Senior Managers are dynamic, diverse leaders who are passionate about making a difference, possess exceptional analytical skills, and thrive in an entrepreneurial setting. IDinsight invests heavily in our employees' professional development and expects them to think critically and creatively about how to maximize our clients' social impact.

Senior Managers oversee all aspects of client engagements (with support from an IDinsight Director) in order to produce high-quality outputs, but more importantly, to drive each client to maximize its social impact. Towards this end, Senior Managers are expected to develop a diverse skill set, including establishing trusted advisor relationships with clients, mentoring high-performing early professionals (Associates) and developing expertise in a broad range of data and evidence tools.




CLIENT-FACING RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Client relationship management: Senior Managers establish themselves as experts and trusted advisors to IDinsight clients. They use this position to provide high-quality counsel and support, grounded in rigorous evidence, to senior leaders in governments, foundations, NGOs, and socially impactful businesses.

 - Project management, technical & communication skills: Senior Managers lead all elements of IDinsight advisory and evaluation projects, including project management, oversight of analytical processes, engagement of internal and external experts, evaluation design, and development of high-quality materials including policy briefs, technical reports, and presentation materials. Senior Managers are also responsible for cross-functional collaboration with the technical teams at IDinsight, to maintain rigour of the work.

 - Mentorship of junior staff: Senior Managers are responsible for the professional development of IDinsight Associates to help them become better professionals in the development sector and achieve their long-term goals.

 - Financial management: Senior Managers lead project budget design and management and are responsible for identifying financial risks for different stakeholders as early as possible. They lead all funder compliance for the project, and support the Director in managing funder relationships.

 - Business development and partnerships: Senior Managers support Directors to identify and pursue new opportunities in Nigeria, build relationships with federal and state government leaders, funders, and implementing partners, and lead the development of concept notes and proposals.


OFFICE LEAD RESPONSIBILITIES (ABUJA)

As Office Lead, the Senior Manager will:

 1. Represent IDinsight in Nigeria as the main point of contact for government counterparts, partners, and other external stakeholders.

 2. Oversee the office administration and finance with support from the Operations team, Including approving office-related expenses and signing letters on behalf of the office.

 3. Provide day-to-day supervision of the Admin & Finance Lead (dotted-line reporting).

 4. Contribute to human resources management for the office, working with the Operations team to monitor culture and team health and taking part in hiring and staffing decisions

 5. Oversee safety and security for the Nigeria team, on projects and in the office: stay informed about the security situation in the country and work with the Operations and Admin teams to make sure staff are informed and have the right support and systems in place to respond.

 6. Serve as [signatory / legal representative] for IDinsight's Nigerian entity, working with the Operations and Legal teams on registration, tax, and regulatory compliance.

As Nigeria is a new office for IDinsight, the Office Lead will also play a hands-on role in the early setup of operations, working with the Operations team on the practical steps of establishing IDinsight's in-country presence.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Deep commitment to improving lives and a demonstrated interest in the use of evidence, rigorous impact measurement, and data to improve development policies and programs.

ABOUT THE WNA REGIONAL OPERATIONS ROLE

As IDinsight's West and North Africa region grows, we are looking for an operations leader to provide the operating conditions needed for safe, compliant, cost-effective, and locally grounded client delivery across our Senegal and Morocco offices.

This is the most senior operations role in the region and is responsible for owning the internal and operational domains end-to-end. The role holder is the Regional Director's primary partner in running the region, holding operations, compliance, risk, and internal systems with real autonomy so the Regional Director can focus on external growth, funders, and partnerships. As the region grows, three areas will matter most: driving and supporting people growth, scoping new geographies, and strengthening safety, security, and duty of care, and the role is weighted toward those. The role reports to the WNA Regional Director, who works closely with IDinsight's Global Operations team. It manages the WNA Operations Manager and the administrative team and partners with client-facing staff who dedicate a portion of their time to organization building. In the Regional Director's absence, this role deputizes for them on operational, financial, and organizational matters.

When the region sets up a new office or legal entity, this role owns the operational coordination and governance of that build. The hands-on entity mechanics, such as registration, banking, and local filings, are handled by external providers or a dedicated launch resource, in partnership with Legal and Finance, while this role sequences the build, holds it to IDinsight's standards, and integrates the new entity into the region.

We are looking for a self-starter who can run a wide range of autonomous workstreams independently, in a role that emphasizes execution, leadership, and people management.




ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES


STRATEGY AND REGIONAL INTEGRATION

 - Set the strategic direction for WNA Operations and make sure the region's operating model scales as new offices or workstreams come online.

 - Lead the operational scoping of potential new geographies, assessing entity options, the legal and tax landscape, cost, risk, and operating models, so the region can make well-grounded expansion decisions before committing.

 - Translate organizational and regional priorities into WNA-wide operating plans, service standards, and team workflows.

 - Serve as the region's most senior operations voice in global and cross-regional leadership conversations, bringing WNA's operating realities into organization-wide planning and advocating for the resources the region needs.

 - Anticipate structural risks and inefficiencies across the WNA footprint before they become crises, and build systems that make the function more resilient as the region grows.


PEOPLE GROWTH AND TEAM DEVELOPMENT

 - Partner with the Regional Director and People Operations to drive talent and people growth across WNA, building the region’s staffing strategy, career pathways, and the specialization and depth the growing team needs.

 - Strengthen the execution and coordination layer beneath the management tier so that associates, managers, and client-facing staff do not absorb a disproportionate administrative load and that work is performed at the right level by the right role.

 - Directly manage the WNA Operations Manager, coaching toward proactive, strategic ownership, and holding them accountable while protecting team well-being.

 - Own operational responsibility for WNA recruitment coordination and onboarding, partnering with People Operations and hiring managers to bring capacity in ahead of need.

 - Conduct performance reviews for the operations and administrative team and build a cohesive WNA Operations function that collaborates across offices rather than running as siloed country operations.

 - Serve as the escalation point for sensitive or complex people matters, exercising judgment, discretion, and consistency with People Operations and leadership.


SAFETY, SECURITY, AND DUTY OF CARE

 - Owns WNA’s safety, security, and duty-of-care systems, including travel and location risk management, incident-response readiness, and coordination with Global Safety and Security, with particular attention to new and higher-risk operating environments as the region expands.

 - Make sure duty-of-care standards are built into new offices and temporary locations from the day they open, so staff and travelers are protected across all WNA contexts.


STANDARDS, SYSTEMS, AND GOVERNANCE

 - Oversee operational coordination across WNA's legal entities and country contexts (Senegal, Morocco, and any new entity), in partnership with local legal counsel, payroll and accounting providers, Finance, and Global Operations.

description:

SOCIAL SCIENTIST/ECONOMIST/RESEARCHER

The exact title will depend on qualifications and role.



ABOUT IDINSIGHT

We're a global data and evidence advisory, working with governments, philanthropies, and non-profits to improve lives at scale, using technology and AI where they can deliver the most impact.

 

IDinsight is a global nonprofit that equips leaders with the data, evidence and technology to improve lives at scale. We partner with governments, NGOs, multilaterals, and funders to support decisions at every stage of their impact journey – from bold pilots to nationwide scale-ups. Our teams bring rigorous evidence and practical insights so leaders can make informed decisions that truly change lives. With our partners, we are pioneering the next frontier of social impact, where data and technology accelerate progress for millions. We help leaders overcome the three main barriers to impact:

 - Figuring out what works

 - Learning and improving

 - Reaching and operating at scale

 

We work in multiple countries across Asia and Africa. Our work spans a wide range of sectors, including agriculture, education, health, governance, sanitation, financial inclusion, and other areas. 

 

We have expertise in a variety of rigorous approaches and methodologies, which we tailor to each client depending on their needs and constraints. To achieve a positive social impact we:

 - Support our partners with the full ‘data and evidence’ value chain – from primary data collection to data systems, monitoring evaluation and learning tools, and data science

 - Inform funding decisions – toward high-impact initiatives and away from less effective programs or approaches

 - Create cutting-edge AI-for-good products that make the delivery of social interventions and learning tools more cost-effective and scalable

 

Our diverse, growing team of roughly 250 outstanding colleagues operate in nearly two dozen countries around the world.  Learn more about our mission, values, and principles at www.IDinsight.org http://www.IDinsight.org.   

 

Joining IDinsight at this moment

IDinsight is entering an exciting new phase of growth. As demand for rigorous evidence and AI-enabled solutions accelerates across the sectors and geographies we work in, we are actively investing in our teams, deepening our regional footprint, and expanding the frontier of what data and technology can do for social impact. This is a moment of real momentum for IDinsight. We're looking for people who want to use data and evidence to improve lives at scale; who are energized by taking on problems without a playbook; and who want a hand in shaping what IDinsight becomes as we grow.




ABOUT THE SOCIAL SCIENTIST ROLE

IDinsight Social Scientists (hereafter “Researcher”) are experts in quantitative and qualitative research tools who support a large portfolio of projects across diverse geographies, sectors, and methodologies. This position may allow for specialization along any or all of these dimensions.

The Researcher will be required to think critically about how to maximize methodological rigor given our clients’ time, operational, political and budget constraints. The ideal candidate should love having many different types of problems thrown at them, be able to quickly digest and understand the program and evidence objectives, and provide advice and guidance on how best to proceed.

The Researcher will be an important member of IDinsight’s Technical Team. The Technical Team is responsible for ensuring that the services we provide to clients are statistically and methodologically sound. In collaboration with the Technical Team lead and personnel, the Researcher’s role will include, but not be limited to, the following activities:

 - Designing and implementing evaluations and other research activities for IDinsight clients in collaboration with project teams. The Researcher will play a leading role along with our client teams in designing and implementing studies for IDinsight clients, including descriptive studies, diagnostic/needs assessments, impact evaluations, process evaluations, monitoring systems, program design and advisory, M&E advisory, and scale-up plans.

 - Ensuring technical rigor of project deliverables. The Researcher will support project teams in drafting and refining technical documents, which include evaluation designs, pre-analysis plans, sample size calculations, data collection instruments, technical reports, and other documents. The Researcher will also be a crucial resource to the country office where he or she is stationed by providing technical expertise on short-term issues that confront project teams.

 - Working with culturally and geographically diverse project teams. The Researcher will work with project teams that can be spread across the globe, from different nationalities and cultures.

 - Supporting the technical professional development of staff. The Researcher will prepare and lead training sessions on technical topics (such as statistical inference and Stata programming) on a regular basis. He or she will also provide individualized support to staff on their technical professional development.

 - Publishing IDinsight studies in academic and policy journals. The Researcher will have the opportunity to co-author publications in academic and policy journals to showcase results from IDinsight studies, based on IDinsight’s client needs and the Researcher’s interest.

 - Develop new projects and services. The Researcher will have the opportunity to develop new projects and client relationships in accordance with IDinsight’s values of client-focused and decision-focused research.

The Researcher will be expected to fulfill these responsibilities and others with professionalism and on strict deadlines. He or she will also be expected to propose, design and implement new initiatives for supporting project teams and increasing the technical rigor of IDinsight’s work.



QUALIFICATIONS

 - Deeply passionate about social, economic, and environmental policies and programs, and social impact

 - Advanced degree in economics, econometrics, statistics, political science, public policy, public health, sociology, anthropology or other applied field. PhD preferred, although candidates with a Master’s degree and a strong record of success doing similar work will be considered.

 - Outstanding quantitative and critical thinking skills

 - Self-starter who will thrive in a start-up setting by taking ownership and initiative

 - Intellectual curiosity and sense of humor

 - 3+ years of relevant work experience preferred, including designing and managing evaluations, quantitative analysis, field research, and managerial experience in a developing country

 - Significant experience with Stata or R preferred. Experience with additional programming languages a plus

 - Prior work authorization in one of the position locations preferred

 - Deep contextual knowledge and experience in the regions where IDinsight works

 - Candidates interested in the Dakar or Rabat office should be fluent in French.



PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

Professional development for Researchers is essential for IDinsight’s long-term impact. With support from IDinsight leadership, Researchers maintain self-directed professional development plans and are given "stretch" opportunities designed to strengthen their professional skills. Real-time feedback and structured reviews are regularly provided to maximize each Researcher’s expertise. IDinsight’s entrepreneurial culture allows roles and career progression to be tailored to individual strengths, interests, and goals. Researchers have the opportunity to increase responsibilities, and high performers will have the opportunity to move up in the organization along technical, managerial, or client-facing paths.

 - Evaluation design: Estimating required sample size for any monitoring and evaluation activity, coding for impact evaluation design (e.g. random assignment, matching), programming SurveyCTO questionnaires for digital data collection.

 - Evaluation implementation: Coding to ensure high data quality, data management including data

 - Analysis: Conducting statistical analysis on datasets to produce results that inform recommendations and decisions.

Location

This position is based in any of our offices in Africa and Asia. Preference will be given to those with pre-existing work authorization in one of our country offices; however, IDInsight will seek work permits where possible for exceptional candidates.



Compensation

Compensation and benefits are commensurate with relevant experience and background, and competitive within the social sector. Please note, as a non-profit, we are unable to provide compensation similar to leading private sector organizations.


Start Date

The start date of this position is rolling, with preference for candidates that can start immediately. We expect a 1-year minimum commitment, with regular professional development conversations and potential for a longer-term career at IDinsight.


How to Apply

Please click the "Apply for this job online" button at the top right. The application asks various questions in order for us to get to know you, and requires a CV and cover letter. ABOUT THE ASSOCIATE & SENIOR ASSOCIATE ROLE

IDinsight Associates and Senior Associates are high-performing early-career professionals passionate to experience the front-line realities of evidence-informed decision-making. These roles provide a rich, varied experience with responsibilities ranging from in-depth research and analysis, data collection management, client interactions, and internal team building.  We seek intellectually curious, resilient, and team-oriented individuals who – in addition to developing professional and technical skills – are highly motivated to grapple with the difficulties and unpredictability of trying to improve lives at scale.

Associates and Senior Associates are responsible for the following areas of work:

Managing project team workflow, systems, deliverables

 - Driving the day-to-day execution of the project work according to project plans and leading internal coordination efforts for their team

 - Conducting and supporting fit-for-decision and right-fit research design, data collection or acquisition, technical analysis, and results visualization/packaging, etc. for project tasks

 - Creating client deliverables, including reports, slide decks, and oral presentations to inform decisions and actions of clients

 - Developing strategic communications to build awareness of IDinsight projects and learnings, contribute to sectoral knowledge, and shift the sector towards more evidence-informed policy and practices

Supporting their team in developing strong client relationships

 - Engaging with client and stakeholder relationships

 - Contributing to client development, including developing proposals and concept notes

Leading data collection activities

 - Overseeing all data collection activities to ensure quality, including managing data collection teams

 - Traveling to project sites, IDinsight offices, embedded client locations, and other areas as per project needs

Contributing to internal team building

 - Developing, piloting, and implementing internal systems or other organizational contributions (e.g., event management) for IDinsight, in coordination with functional teams such as Operations, Communications, Finance, etc.

 - Contributing to office life and culture building, such as facilitating All Hands Meetings; leading team building efforts at team retreats; participating in Social Cultural Committee events; and engaging with the DEI Working Group.

Associates learn professional, technical and life skills while working on some of the world’s most critical problems. No two experiences are the same. Some work deeply on one project for their entire program commitment, while others work across a variety of projects.  Workstreams can immerse Associates in remote, front-line program contexts, deep statistical analyses, and/or high-level, strategic interactions.

Associates and Senior Associates will be staffed on IDinsight projects according to various factors including organizational need, timeline and availability, team dynamics, skills optimization, and professional growth and development. While we aim to factor in individual preferences whenever possible to staffing decisions, they are one of many factors in the project staffing process.

The Associate role is not a typical “9-5” job, and can require early mornings and late nights to accommodate the time zone differences of a dispersed team, as well as busy periods within project workflows. Associates work hard and so IDinsight encourages balance with flexible work hours and wellness benefits, including comprehensive mental health care support and organization-wide wellness days off. Many find this balance to yield rich professional and personal rewards, and therefore progress to more senior roles with IDinsight.





QUALIFICATIONS

IDinsight Associates and Senior Associates come from a wide range of disciplinary backgrounds, including economics, data science, policy research, development projects, and more. Given that no Associate or Senior Associate comes in with the same exact background as another, we’re typically looking for candidates with a broad range of qualifications and former experiences. Here are some examples of the key qualifications most successful candidates should possess:




Credentials

 - Undergraduate degree in economics, statistics, public policy, or related quantitative/social science fields (Master's degree holders are welcome)

 - 3-5 years of relevant work experience in international development, research and evaluation, data analytics, consulting, or program management

Knowledge, skills, and abilities

 - Strong analytical skills, with exposure to (either via professional work experience or academic coursework) the basics of econometrics, data and research analysis tools, and quantitative and qualitative research processes or an ability to quickly understand these topics

 - Strong writing skills with the ability to translate technical jargon into well-structured, writing-based deliverables (e.g., policy briefs, project memos, analytical reports, external blog posts, and more)

 - Ability to understand complex concepts and topics quickly even with limited prior knowledge or exposure and a willingness to invest in learning new concepts, skills, and methods without being prompted

Behaviors and mindsets

 - Contributing to office life and culture building, such as facilitating All Hands Meetings; leading team building efforts at team retreats; participating in Social Cultural Committee events; and engaging with the DEI Working Group.

Associates learn professional, technical and life skills while working on some of the world’s most critical problems. No two experiences are the same. Some work deeply on one project for their entire program commitment, while others work across a variety of projects.  Workstreams can immerse Associates in remote, front-line program contexts, deep statistical analyses, and/or high-level, strategic interactions.

Associates and Senior Associates will be staffed on IDinsight projects according to various factors including organizational need, timeline and availability, team dynamics, skills optimization, and professional growth and development. While we aim to factor in individual preferences whenever possible to staffing decisions, they are one of many factors in the project staffing process.

The Associate role is not a typical “9-5” job, and can require early mornings and late nights to accommodate the time zone differences of a dispersed team, as well as busy periods within project workflows. Associates work hard and so IDinsight encourages balance with flexible work hours and wellness benefits, including comprehensive mental health care support and organization-wide wellness days off. Many find this balance to yield rich professional and personal rewards, and therefore progress to more senior roles with IDinsight.

 - Build manager-development programs for IDinsight’s many first-time and newer managers.

About the ProjectThere have been persistent efforts focused on improving primary healthcare (PHC) and overcoming the hurdles of low coverage and poor quality of health services through several Digital Health interventions. However, majority of these initiatives are designed with very specific clinical or administrative purposes and lack a comprehensive ecosystem approach resulting in multiple applications and digital portals in use for their health system. This cascades into poor accountability and performance, time and resource wastage, lack of continuum of care, and low coverage of health services, resulting in poor health outcomes. PATH is supporting the state of Maharashtra with digitization of primary level of care and health service delivery in select districts. The project intends to demonstrate end to end digitization in healthcare and develop a digital saturation model at district level, leveraging fit for purpose digital solutions/interventions through the use case of improving reproductive, maternal and child health service delivery indicators. The district saturation model will include coverage across rural & urban areas and service delivery across public and private sectors. The focus will be on digitizing healthcare facilities, community health initiatives/programs and deploying innovations for accelerating service delivery across continuum of care. affordability analysis● Travel to project sites, whenever necessary, to conduct meetings/interviews/training or collect primary information● Publish quality research outputs – peer-reviewed papers, reports, briefs, blogs and opinion pieces – and write memos and issue notes for circulation among senior Government officials and other internal and external stakeholders● Work with senior researchers on conceptualising new projects, and undertake research training to strengthen technical skill sets Programme Assistance● Assist in project implementation by contributing towards detailed activity plans and timelines, resource planning, donor engagement, and building stronger ties with government, industry, financial institutions and institutional partners● Contribute to the team’s outreach efforts, including organising webinars and physical events and representing CEEW at industry eventsSelection CriteriaQualification● Strong academic credentials, preferably a Master’s degree with a specialisation in renewable energy technologies, economics, public policy or related field● Sound understanding of India’s energy markets (specifically grid-connected DRE markets), the policy and regulatory environment, and the financing landscape for distributed renewablesWork experience● 1 – 3 years of experience in research, policy/industry engagement and project management – preferably in electricity policy, renewable energy, energy systems or energy/climate finance – with a track record of timely delivery and of dealing with public and private institutions within and outside India● Prior experience of writing white papers, articles, policy briefs and research reportsKey skills● Superior analytical abilities, a strong research background, and familiarity with quantitative and qualitative research methods● Proficiency in MS-Excel is a must, including building costing and cash-flow worksheets. title: Cancel Reply
description: Blogs/ Career Fair at Kumbarkoppalu Government High School Empowers Students GRAAM ProjectFebruary 10, 2025 Career Fair at Kumbarkoppalu Government High School Empowers Students A Career Fair was organized at Kumbarkoppalu Government High School in Mysuru as part of the “Aim” project. The event was a collaborative effort by GRAAM, the Department of School Education, and Wurth Electronics Services India (P) Ltd., aiming to provide career guidance and skill development insights to students.Project AIM (Aspiration, Inspiration, Motivation) is structured to assist students in assessing their values, interests, skills, and career goals. The program empowers them to make well-informed career decisions that align with their strengths and passions while equipping them with essential resources and guidance to confidently pursue their aspirations.The fair at Kumbarkoppalu Government High School in Mysuru was inaugurated by Mr. Gopalkrishna Sastri, a senior member of the Human Resources fraternity and Former Head of HR at WURTH Elektronics. While addressing the students, Mr. Sastri emphasized the importance of both academic knowledge and practical skills for holistic development. He encouraged them to tackle challenges with determination and stay focused on their career goals to thrive in the competitive job market.Shri K. B. Lingaraju, President of the Mysuru District Industrial and Commercial Association, highlighted the importance of diverse skills beyond engineering and medicine. He stressed that various career paths hold value in today’s global job market and advised students to seek career guidance during their schooling years to make informed professional choices.Adding an interactive dimension to the event, students performed short plays that showcased different career options, engaging their peers in thoughtful discussions about future possibilities. The event was presided over by Ravi Kumar, SDMC President, and received active support from Headmistress Smt. Yogalakshmi, the teaching staff, SDMC members, and the GRAAM team. Faculty members and students participated enthusiastically, making the career fair a meaningful initiative for guiding young minds towards informed career decisions. title: Portfolio Success Manager – Venture Partner and Sprint Excellence
description: Position Name: Portfolio Success Manager – Venture Partner and Sprint ExcellenceReports To: Head of Portfolio SuccessLocation: Delhi NCR (preferred); open to other locationsRole Overview:This role makes sure companies in our accelerator program get real, lasting value from the support they receive. Each company is paired with a Venture Partner (VP), a dedicated advisor who works with them for 12–15 months, guiding them through their growth journey. This role owns that relationship: making sure VP calls happen on schedule, cover the right ground, and, most importantly, actually lead to change inside the company.It also plays an active part in Sprint, a focused 90-day period of hands-on support that companies go through early in the program, not just tracking whether it's on schedule, but assessing whether it's genuinely delivering value, and stepping in when it isn't.Key Responsibilities:Manage the Venture Partner Relationship• Make sure every company has an active, engaged VP throughout their 12–15 month journey with us.• Track that a new company's first two calls with their VP happen on time and result in a clear plan for what the company needs to work on.• Review that plan for quality, and confirm the company is on board with it.Track Calls & Follow-Through• Make sure VPs check in with companies at the mid-point and end of each work cycle, and that these calls are properly documented.• Ensure regular check-in calls are happening in between.• Check whether companies are actually acting on what the VP recommends, this is the real measure of whether the relationship is working.Manage Feedback• Regularly ask companies how their VP relationship is going.• If something isn't working, raise it with the VP directly and help course correct.• Be the first point of contact if a company or VP needs something to change.Drive Sprint Excellence• Keep an eye on whether a company's first support sprint is on track and finishing on time.• Go beyond paperwork: assess whether the sprint is genuinely helping the company make progress, not just hitting scheduled milestones.• Flag quality issues or a sprint that's off-track to the assigned expert or the Head of Portfolio Success, and help course correct.• Make sure basic sprint paperwork, like the kickoff document, is completed.• Feed sprint details, like hiring numbers or funding raised, into shared reports.Keep Records & Reporting• Maintain simple, accurate dashboards tracking VP calls and sprint status for every company.• Flag any issues or bottlenecks to the Head of Portfolio Success.Key Outcomes:• Onboarding calls with new companies completed, with a plan the company agrees to.• Mid-point and closing calls completed and documented, every cycle.• Regular check-in calls happening and tracked.• Companies acting on what their VP recommends.• Feedback collected and relationship issues resolved.• Sprint paperwork and timelines on track.• Sprint quality and value assessed, with issues flagged and addressed.• Company data, hiring, funding, next steps, accurate and up to date.Qualifications & Experience:• 5–8 years in program management, client success, or relationship management; startup, impact, or development sector experience preferred.• Comfortable managing long, ongoing relationships (12+ months), not just short projects.• Experience working with external advisors, consultants, or mentors.• Good at judging whether a conversation or piece of delivery work is actually landing, and coaching people to improve it.• Comfortable with dashboards and tracking tools.• Strong communicator, equally comfortable with founders and senior advisors.• Organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable with a role that will evolve as the team grows.

title: WSN Ecosystem Program Manager -Vijayawada
description: Position Title: Ecosystem Program ManagerReporting To: GM EcosystemLocations: Chennai, AhmedabadRole SummaryThe Ecosystem Program manager will be responsible for end-to-end management and expansion of the skilling ecosystem in the assigned region.
