title: Outcome Analyst -Lucknow
description: Position Summary: To further Wadhwani Foundation’s mission of accelerating job growth through skilling and entrepreneurship, we are seeking an Outcomes Analyst – Ecosystem Impact to support the measurement and improvement of program outcomes across our Skilling and Entrepreneurship initiatives in India.This role will work closely with Central Program teams and on-ground program operators to understand how programs are performing across partners, geographies, and cohorts. The Outcomes Analyst will generate data-driven insights on what is working, what is not working, and why, enabling timely course corrections and stronger program outcomes.The role will combine outcome tracking, ecosystem diagnostics, and operational insights, ensuring that program teams have the intelligence required to strengthen program delivery and improve long-term impact.While the analyst will work closely with program teams in the ecosystem, they will maintain a dotted line alignment with the Central Impact function, ensuring adherence to impact measurement frameworks, outcome definitions, and data quality standards. About Wadhwani Foundation: Wadhwani Foundation is a high-growth, not-for-profit tech organization dedicated to accelerating job growth and enabling millions to earn a family-sustaining wage and lead a dignified life.Over two decades since its inception in 2001, the Foundation has focused on a simple but powerful mission: creating jobs and enabling entrepreneurs.The Foundation works in partnership with governments, foundations, corporations, and educational institutions through the following initiatives:Wadhwani Skills Network – Enables jobseekers with employability and professional skills to acquire family-wage jobs.Wadhwani Entrepreneur Network – Enables aspiring and practicing entrepreneurs to start, survive, and thrive through customized interventions.Wadhwani Global Digital Transformation – Upskills governments with emerging technologies to accelerate population-scale projects and define new-age policies.Innovation & Research – Accelerates academic innovation in emerging technology domains including AI, biotech, and advanced computing. Key Responsibilities1. Ecosystem Intelligence & Program Diagnostics· Analyse program performance across partners, geographies, and cohorts to identify patterns in outcomes and program effectiveness· Identify drivers of success and underperformance in skilling and entrepreneurship ecosystems· Surface early signals on learner progression, partner performance, job placement outcomes, and venture creation· Generate ecosystem intelligence insights to help program teams understand where interventions are succeeding and where course correction is needed2. Outcome Measurement & Monitoring· Support the implementation of approved outcome measurement frameworks across programs.· Track program KPIs such as employment outcomes, income progression, job retention, and venture sustainability· Monitor participant journeys across the program lifecycle to ensure accurate tracking of outcomes· Operationally manage outcome validation exercises such as surveys, tele-calling, third-party validations, and field verifications3. Data Analysis & Operational Insights· Analyse program data to identify bottlenecks in learner or entrepreneur journeys· Identify partner or geography-specific performance variations; stakeholder-specific analysis· Translate data into actionable insights and operational recommendations for program teams· Support the development of performance dashboards and insight reports4. Field & Stakeholder Coordination· Work closely with program managers, trainers, placement teams, and partner organizations to understand operational realities· Support program teams with data-backed insights to improve mobilization, training effectiveness, employer engagement, and venture support· Coordinate with external stakeholders such as employers and ecosystem partners5. Continuous Improvement & Program Learning· Conduct root cause analysis for underperforming partners, geographies, or cohorts· Support testing and analysis of pilot interventions or operational improvements· Document lessons and insights from program implementation6. Data Quality & Compliance· Maintain high standards of data accuracy, completeness, and reliability· Ensure outcome data aligns with approved measurement frameworks and definitions· Support quality assurance processes for outcome measurement and reporting Required Qualifications· Bachelor’s or master’s degree in economics, Development Studies, Public Policy, Data Analytics, Statistics, or related fields· 3–5 years of experience in impact measurement, program analytics, development sector analytics, workforce development/skilling programs, or entrepreneurship ecosystem program· Experience working with primary and secondary data to generate operational insights is strongly preferred· Experience working with field teams or ecosystem partners will be an advantage Technical Skills· Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving ability· Proficiency in advanced MS Excel (advanced formulas, pivot tables, structured analysis)· Experience using data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau· Familiarity with MIS platforms and survey tools· Ability to conduct statistical and cohort analysis· Strong ability to translate data into clear written insights and presentations Core Competencies· Analytical and structured thinking.· Ability to combine data insights with field understanding.· Strong collaboration skills with program and GTM stakeholders.· Strong written and verbal communication skills.· High attention to detail and commitment to data integrity.· Comfort working with field teams, partners, and diverse communities. What Success Looks like· Program outcomes are accurately measured and validated across ecosystems.· All relevant stakeholders’ teams receive timely insights on partner and ecosystem performance.· Early signals of program challenges are identified and addressed proactively.· Data and field insights inform program improvements and ecosystem strategy.

title: Program Manager - AICTE Indovation Center Partnership - Hyderabad
description: Job Description for Program Manager under Wadhwani Innovation Network – AICTE Indovation Center PartnershipBackgroundThe Wadhwani Innovation Network (WIN) is dedicated to driving innovation, translation and entrepreneurship with a prime objective of fast-tracking commercialization of academic research in cutting-edge areas such as biotechnology, bioengineering, synthetic biology, healthtech, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, spacetech, advanced computing, quantum technology, critical minerals and mining.These transformative initiatives will be implemented through strategic partnerships with various academic institutions / incubators / Government agencies such as AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education).The Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell (MIC), in collaboration with AICTE, has established 13 Indovation Centers across the country to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in higher education institutions. These Indovation Centers, operating in a hub-spoke model, aim to facilitate technology transfer, IPR, commercialization, and provide a one-stop resource for information on innovation and startup schemes. The mission of the Wadhwani Innovation Network – AICTE Indovation Center partnership is to accelerate innovation and translate multi-disciplinary research into new products and startups. Post/ RequirementEducational Qualifications and Experience Required Program ManagerEssential:· B.Tech. or MSc (engineering or science disciplines) or MBA· Desirable:· Additional qualification in management or law or patent agent.· Experience:· More than three years’ experience in incubation, IP development & commercialization, technology transfer, business development etc. in a research or academic environment or in a technology transfer / incubator office/research park etc.· · Deliverables:· Coordination of Innovation Programmes, stakeholder liaison, and HUB-SPOKE operation plan implementation.· Carry out policy research, analysis and documents, development of reports· Communication material development for IP and Technology transfer related activities.· Design and implement capacity building programs, trainings etc. on regular basis.· Handhold institutional resources for managing IPRs & Technology Transfer assignments in SPOKE institutions.· Support in market assessment of identified technologies, stakeholder mapping and coordination.· Build and manage IP repository, technology compendium development at the centre level.· Innovation and entrepreneurship promotion and development in HEIs.· Streamlining incubation and pre-incubation system in HEIs· Assist the manager and handhold Innovation fellow and other team members at the Center. Location:Ahmedabad, Chennai, Kanpur, Guwahati, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad

title: Senior Implementation Manager, FPO Program
description: Designation: Implementation Manager, FPO ProgramLocation : Delhi Role Overview: The Wadhwani FPO Program is an important new initiative aimed at providing capacity-building to Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) and their support organizations, Cluster Based Business Organizations (CBBOs). Implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, the program will deliver high-quality interactive content, AI copilots, and human services, all leveraging the Wadhwani GenieAI platform We are seeking a strong candidate for the role of Implementation Manager. This person will partner directly with the Small Farmers' Agri-Business Consortium (SFAC) in Delhi and will play a pivotal role in overseeing the successful implementation of the initial pilot program and the evolution of the program as it expands. The Implementation Manager will be responsible for establishing and maintaining strong relationships with key national stakeholders, including SFAC, Bankers Institute of Rural Development (BIRD), Lucknow and LaxmanraoInamdar National Academy for Co-operative Research & Development (LINAC), as well as relevant state government officials. Key Responsibilities: · Serve as Single Point of Contact (SPOC) and project manager for all program workstreams: technical integration, content development, training, deployment, and evaluation.· Provide direct leadership in the training and deployment workstreams; liaise with Wadhwani Foundation staff leading the technical integration, content development, and evaluation workstreams.· Collaborate effectively with Wadhwani Foundation staff and partners to identify and overcome program obstacles.· Provide regular reports to leadership on activities and outcomes.· Develop a comprehensive understanding of the FPO ecosystem and the Wadhwani Foundation's capabilities in order to assess and propose additional partnership opportunities.· Represent the Wadhwani Foundation in relevant forums, conferences, and events to promote the Wadhwani FPO Program. Skills & Experience: · At least 10 years’ experience in program management.· Proven track record of managing successful program implementations in the Indian agricultural ecosystem, preferably with FPOs specifically.· Demonstrated ability to interface effectively with partners, including senior leadership, to ensure program success.· Excellent verbal and written communication skills.· Collaborative mindset, with the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams. · Experience working in Ministry of Agriculture. · A genuine passion for FPO capacity-building, with a sense of urgency for achieving change

This incumbent will play a critical role in measuring, analysing, and strengthening the impact of hyperlocal skilling and job creation interventions. As part of a larger team, the Outcome Analyst will ensure that program outcomes are effectively tracked, validated, and translated into actionable insights that improve program design, delivery, and long-term impact. One of the key functions for this role will be to support the connect between data, program execution, and strategy — ensuring concurrent data-based advisory helps the initiative efforts translate into measurable KPIs/outcomes. The Wadhwani Foundation works in partnership with governments, foundations, corporations, and educational institutes through the below Initiatives: Wadhwani Skills Network: Enables jobseekers with new-age employability skills to acquire family-wage jobs Wadhwani Entrepreneur Network: Enables aspiring and practising entrepreneurs to start, survive and thrive through customised interventions. Wadhwani Global Digital Transformation: Upskills governments with emerging technologies to accelerate population-scale projects and define new-age policies Innovation & Research: Accelerate academic innovation in groundbreaking tech domains of AI, biotech, and advanced computing, pushing the envelope from pioneering research to commercialization. About Global Impact Team: The Global Impact team is the “Voice of the Beneficiary” within the foundation and serves the vital role of understanding their needs and providing insights to enhance program Impact. We do this by learning alongside our beneficiaries and stakeholders, using a right mix of technical and practical experience, to deliver the data and insights our programs need, fast. Key ResponsibilitiesA. Outcome Measurement & Monitoring· Support in implementation of frameworks to track program outcomes (e.g., employment rates, income changes, retention, enterprise sustainability).· Timely monitoring and reporting of the program KPIs· Monitor program participant performances from start to end of the prescribed initiative journey, as per the approved approach and methodology.· Operationally manage periodic outcome validations through surveys, tele-calling, and field visits, including those done through a third-party.B. Data Analysis & Reporting· Quality assure, reference, analyse, and interpret program data to assess effectiveness.· Ensuring data pipeline connectivity to dashboards and monthly/quarterly performance reports.· Engage with the Impact leads for the initiative to Identify trends, drop-off points, and bottlenecks in prescribed program pathways.· Support in providing actionable recommendations to improve placement and retention outcomes. C. Field & Stakeholder Coordination· Work in close coordination with the program managers, trainers, placement officers, and field coordinators.· Support local implementation teams with data-backed insights.· Liaise with employers and community stakeholders to track job retention and satisfaction. D. Continuous Improvement· Conduct root-cause analysis for underperforming geographies or cohorts.· Support in identification of any modifications/re-alignments required in context of the geography of operation.· Recommend modifications in curriculum, mobilization strategy, or employer engagement.· Support pilot testing of new skilling or job linkage interventions.· Contribute to impact assessments and evaluation studies. E. Documentation & Compliance· Maintain accurate beneficiary databases and outcome records.· Ensure compliance with the agreed initiative-specific reporting requirements.· In case required, support on other internal organizational processes related to impact data and beneficiary verification. Required Qualifications· Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Development Studies, Public Policy or related field.· 3–5 years of experience in impact measurement, data analytics, or program analytics.· Demonstrated experience of working in skilling, livelihoods, workforce development, job creation, or startups/ SMBs performance and growth programs preferred.· Demonstrated experience of managing and analysing primary and secondary data to generate timely and requirement specific insights· Demonstrated experience of working in a fast-paced results-driven environment preferred. Technical Skills· Analytical thinking· Proficiency in advanced MS Excel (advanced functions, pivot tables, dashboards).· Experience with data tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or similar.· Familiarity with MIS systems and data collection tools.· Ability to conduct basic statistical analysis.· Strong report writing and presentation skills. Core Competencies · Analytical and detail-oriented.· Strong problem-solving mindset.· Ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams.· Strong communication skills (written and verbal).· Comfortable in travel and working with field teams and diverse communities.· High level of integrity and data confidentiality. What Success Looks like · Program data is trusted, timely and decision-ready · Program teams have timely access to outputs and outcomes · Impact operations are managed and quality-assured along with timely inputs for improvements as per needImpact operations is seen as a strategic partner, not a reporting

title: Child Protection Specialist, NO-3, Fixed Term Position, New Delhi, India, APR, Post Number #46974 (Open for Indian Nationals Only)
description: Skip to main content Vacancies Current vacancies Explore our current job opportunities Filter results Search using keywords Search for jobs Contract type Fixed Term Appointment Locations South Asia Region India Functional Area Programme Child Protection Position level Child Protection Specialist, NO-3, Fixed Term Position, New Delhi, India, APR, Post Number #46974 (Open for Indian Nationals Only) Apply now Job no: 596731 Contract type: Fixed Term Appointment Duty Station: New Delhi Location: India Categories: Child Protection UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to Protection How can you make a difference? As a Child Protection Specialist, you will contribute to UNICEF India’s efforts to strengthen child protection systems and ensure that all children, especially the most vulnerable, are protected from violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect. Reporting to the Chief of Child Protection, you will provide technical and programmatic support for the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of child protection initiatives, while working closely with government, civil society and development partners to achieve sustainable results for children. You will help translate evidence into action, strengthen partnerships, influence policy, and drive innovative solutions that improve child protection outcomes at scale. The Child Protection Specialist reports to the Chief, Child Protection for guidance and general supervision. The Specialist supports the development and preparation of the Child Protection programme(s) and is responsible for the management, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and evaluation of the child protection programmes/projects within the country programme. The role has a strong focus on upstream engagement through policy advocacy, systems strengthening, strategic partnerships, and the application of UNICEF's 3Cs (Convene, Converge, and Catalyze) for Every Child approach. The Specialist provides technical guidance and management support throughout the programming processes. The Specialist facilitates the administration and achievement of concrete and sustainable contributions to national and international efforts to create a protective environment for children against all harm, and to protect their rights to survival, development and well being as established under the Convention on the Rights of the Child, international treaties/frameworks and UN intergovernmental bodies. The Specialist contributes to the achievement of results according to plans, allocation, results based-management approaches and methodology (RBM), and UNICEF’s Strategic Plans, standards of performance and accountability framework. Summary of key functions/accountabilities: Support to programme/project development and planning Programme management, monitoring and delivery of results Technical and operational support to programme implementation Networking and partnership building Innovation, knowledge management and capacity building If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Child Protection Specialist Level 3.doc To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have… Minimum requirements Education: Master or equivalent (Advanced University Degree) in International Development,Psychology,Sociology, human rights, international law, child protection, social work and any other related fields. Work Experience: At least 5 years of relevant work experience in Child Protection, social development, upstream programming, policy advocacy, systems strengthening, strategic engagement. and any other related fields. Skills: Child Protection, Policy Advocacy, Programming, Partnership and engagement with stakeholders, System strengthening, Upstream programming. Language Requirements : English - Proficient/Fluent Desirables Language: Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language UN system experience in child protection programme development, resource mobilization, experience in child protection legislation and legal reform Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts. For every Child, you demonstrate... UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values UNICEF competencies required for this post are… (1) Builds and maintains partnerships(2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness(3) Drive to achieve results for impact(4) Innovates and embraces change(5) Manages ambiguity and complexity(6) Thinks and acts strategically(7) Works collaboratively with others(8) Nurtures, leads and manages people Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels. UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance. UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct. UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable. Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selec

description: Skip to main content WHO / Yoshi Shimizu Ms Grace Gonzales, Secretary at the Regional Director's Office. September 2016. © Credits Apply for a position Explore career opportunities across the WHO SystemWHO offers a wide range of job opportunities across the globe, reflecting our commitment to putting countries at the center of our work. Vacancies Vacancies and profile access.Staff member accessExternal candidate accessWHO Internship ProgrammeIf you are interested in opportunities with the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), WHO’s Regional Office for the Americas, or the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), please visit their dedicated career portals.PAHO vacanciesIARC vacancies Job alerts WHO uses an online platform called Stellis to publish vacancies and manage candidate profiles.Should you wish to receive Job alerts from Stellis, please register through the profile access links as user/login. Once you're logged into the system, go to your Profile and then to Preferences, to activate a Job alert and save your job search criteria. You will then receive email alerts when jobs matching your criteria are published.RSS (Really Simple Syndication) feeds offer another way to get job openings content. You can subscribe by clicking the RSS URL link provided in the external candidate and the Internship Programme portals. Need help? In case the site does not display properly or you are unable to move around the site, check the following:You are using the latest version of your web browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox browsers). Retry access using Firefox browser, which provides optimum experience.Javascript is enabled.Clear your browser history and open the career portal in a new browser (not a new tab within the same browser); or try using another device.If you have difficulty submitting your application, please write to us at globalservicedesk@who.int, including details of the job vacancy and screenshots of error messages (if applicable). Beware of scammers pretending to be WHO!WHO never asks for money for recruitment; it is not WHO's policy to charge registration fees for conference meetings; and WHO does not conduct lotteries, or offer prizes or awards via any digital media.If you receive a suspicious email or message claiming to be from WHO or PAHO, please verify its authenticity by contacting us. Your application Preparing your applicationResearch our organization to understand the work we do, what sort of an environment you are applying to work in and to make sure that the job opportunity is a good fit for your career aspirations.​See the documents published on this page for guidance on how to apply and instructions for ex-employee to access their profiles.Review your own qualification, experience and skills with those published in the vacancy. Fill in a self-assessment table if it helps you, as you may be asked to complete self-assessment questions as part of your application. WHO vacancies are filled in accordance with the WHO competency Model, which you can refer to from here.​Applying onlineOnce you have identified a job opportunity that interests you and for which you are suitably qualified, please create an online profile to apply to the same. You may also include a cover letter describing your motivation for applying. It is important to provide accurate and complete information about your work experiences, achievements and competencies as it will provide the basis for the evaluation of your eligibility and suitability for the vacancy.As per the instructions contained in the documents featured on this page, you can create a general profile, which serves as a basic template, and​ use it to apply to several vacancies. Each job application can be customized separately. The general profile will always be updated with the data submitted in the latest application. Pay close attention to the closing date and time, which is automatically reflected in your personal device’s system settings. Applications received after the indicated deadline will not be accepted. If you have submitted your job application successfully, you will promptly receive an automated acknowledgment e-mail.Selection processTo ensure a thorough review of applications, the selection process may take several weeks, or months to complete. Please note that only shortlisted candidates, under serious consideration are contacted further to undergo an assessment (one or more screening steps) and a competency based interview as part of the selection process, before a position can be offered. title: Read the testimonial
description: Skip to main content WHO / Jawad Jalali Polio vaccination campaign in Asadabad, Afghanistan. © Credits Workforce testimonials Asantesana KamuyangoTechnical Officer – Headquarters, SwitzerlandWhen I was a young girl growing up in Malawi I saw first-hand the striking health disparities that lead to so many preventable deaths in mothers and their children. My awareness of these deep-rooted health inequalities prompted me to become a state-registered nurse and midwife. I remember relying on WHO’s Family planning global handbook in my job and would often think about how valuable an asset it is to have an organization dedicated to global health.From the beginning of my career I have worked on the development and management of sexual and reproductive health programs, focusing on the reduction of child marriage and adolescent pregnancy in Malawi. I’ve led teams of mobile clinic service providers, community facilitators for demand creation, community based distributor agents, peer educators and community volunteers.Today I am a technical officer for contraception and fertility care at WHO headquarters in Geneva. I joined through the Young Professionals Programme for least developed countries, which gave me the opportunity to sit at the table with other professionals who work to develop knowledge for the global good. I synthesize knowledge and contribute to the development of standards and guidelines in contraception and fertility care. I have conducted multi-country research studies focused on evaluating the influence of social structural and national family planning programs on contraceptive use. My work with WHO has taken me on a journey to develop my skills and deepened my understanding of the global health space.Our team recently launched the latest version of the Family planning global handbook, and I had the privilege to lead the launch of this work at the international conference on family planning. Working with other experts to disseminate this important document made me remember the early days of my career, and how that book was both an essential guide to my work and a source of aspiration for where life could take me. It is such a beautiful transition from being a user of knowledge to an expert working with WHO to create knowledge that can help others around the world. Title of WHO staff and officials reflects their respective position at the time the testimonial was provided. Tuan Nghia TonTechnical Officer – Viet Nam Country OfficeI am a Technical Officer in WHO’s Environmental Health team for the WHO Viet Nam country office. I am happy to work with WHO today, but I didn’t set out on this path. I enjoyed the sciences at school and went on to complete a chemical engineering degree. This led to a job in atomic energy research, which I found to be a rather isolated environment. My father motivated me to think more about the value of my work, rather than simply aiming for the highest qualification and then hoping I would find a purpose. I took a fellowship opportunity in India so I could branch into environmental solid waste management, as this was clearly an area for development. When I returned to Viet Nam, the government was in the process of normalizing relations with the US, and I was surprised to be accepted on a scholarship there to further my environmental science studies.During my master's degree, I not only learnt about waste management, environmental impact and policy development, but I also noted the regard for evidence-based studies and the many WHO linkages to sanitation and water borne diseases, and many other environmental related health issues. I was well qualified and inspired when I got back to Viet Nam, but it was not easy to find work in this specialized area at the time. Eventually I found a Danish bilateral environmental project where I could apply my knowledge and was engaged in a multifaceted environmental project in a steel and tea production town north of Hanoi. I gained experience in waste management, air pollution and many aspects of occupational health. My focus moved further towards the management of environmental problems and their health impacts on the Vietnamese population. At the end of this project, I applied to work in various international organizations. I felt that after my reorientation, further studies and my specific experience, it was pure fate that my application to WHO was successful. It was as though everything had been leading to this.Today I work with water suppliers and the government to support the development of the water safety plan. This is part of a WHO global project, and the implementation guidelines, which manage risks in the whole production process of drinking water, have already been successfully implemented in several cities in Viet Nam. The outcomes in reducing water borne diseases are clear. It will take a long time to implement the project across the entire country, but we are on the right road and seeing results. I’m proud of Viet Nam’s progress in water and waste management to date and of WHO’s involvement.I find it inspiring to be part of these global WHO projects and I’ve been involved in others like the water sanitation and hygiene practices projects, which have been rolled out in a growing number of health care facilities. As we look at the effects of climate change, I’m looking forward to progressing this project and improving conditions in healthcare facilities across the country. I’m also grateful to be part of WHO’s transformation into a more diverse workforce and really feel I have a place to contribute to WHO’s mission. Title of WHO staff and officials reflects their respective position at the time the testimonial was provided. Hala HabibCommunications Officer – Lebanon Country OfficeMy name is Hala Habib. While I was growing up in Nigeria, I remember clearly hearing and seeing reports about the terrible injustices of the apartheid system in South Africa. Even as young as 11 years old, I wanted to reach out and help those who were discriminated against in their own country. As I grew older, I realized that there were elements of apartheid around me in my own country. In Nigeria I saw firsthand how impoverished local people were treated harshly and unfairly by a minority of privileged expats. There were few repercussions for their cruel actions and like in South Africa it just did not seem right to me. This spurred my interest in humanitarian work and in the rights that we all have. From then on, I wanted to be part of a movement to improve human rights. I simply never saw myself working in any other field. Today I am a Communications Officer in the WHO Lebanon Country Office. I think of myself as “the right to health office megaphone”! I love working with people in communities and feel I have a sacred role to deliver clear messages in order to further WHO’s mission to serve the vulnerable and change lives. The current COVID-19 pandemic is accompanied by a misinformation pandemic, and fighting it is just as urgent as the vaccine. I believe that one of our biggest communications achievements here in Lebanon, has been staying ahead of the misinformation about COVID-19 and other diseases. We have used every channel available to us to provide information and avoid panic in an already anxious population.Our team has achieved many successes here, from our key role in the recovery efforts after the 2020 Beirut blast to being part of the drive to vaccinate children against polio. I am proud to be part of the team that work relentlessly to make sure no one is left behind. Everyone, no matter their status, color, religion, or sexual orientation, can in their small way, contribute to global public health communications and thus save lives. title: Compensation and benefits
description: Skip to main content WHO / Yoshi Shimizu WHO staff are on their way to visit fishermen in South Tarawa, Kiribati. People in Kiribati are experiencing extensive coastal erosion, not just of the beaches, but also of the land. © Credits Staff appointments RemunerationWHO has an attractive remuneration package with competitive pay and benefits in accordance with the United Nations Common System which is established by the International Civil Service Commission (ICSC). There are three main categories of staff: Professional and higher categories (IP), National Professional Officer (NPO) and General Service (GS). Offers for these positions are either Fixed Term Appointments or Temporary Appointments. Staff in the professional and higher categories are paid on the basis of salary scales applied worldwide and established by the General Assembly of the United Nations on the recommendation of the ICSC. A common job classification system developed by the ICSC provides the structure for this salary scale. Staff in the General and National Professional Officer categories are paid in accordance with local salary scales based on the best prevailing local conditions through surveys of local salaries, which are conducted and reviewed periodically. Job classification standards differentiate between levels of responsibility and provide a framework for comparison with local labour markets. BenefitsAs an IP, NPO or GS staff member, you are eligible for 30 days of annual leave per year on a fulltime basis (or the pro rata equivalent). For most appointments, will be covered by the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Scheme and the WHO worldwide medical insurance (including dental). Salaries, grants and allowances paid by WHO are generally exempt from income tax in most countries. An employment offer will include all relevant information on benefits and your onboarding process will explain how to apply for and receive applicable entitlements.Other staff benefits vary according to contract type and level and may include: Dependency allowanceEducation grant for schools and first-level university educationHome leave and family visit Maternity/paternity/surrogacy or adoption leaveSettling in grant Relocation grantHardship allowanceMobility incentiveRental subsidyRepatriation and/or end of service grant Appointment types Fixed Term Appointments​Fixed Term Appointments are issued to international professional, national professional and general service staff for one or two years. These appointments may be renewed subject to the Organization’s needs and the staff member’s performance. ​ Temporary Appointments​Temporary Appointments are issued to international professional, national professional and general service staff to meet short term programmatic needs. Temporary appointments may be renewed up to a maximum period of 24 months, after which a mandatory break in service of more than 30 days is observed. Find out more about WHO Rules and Regulations.Explore joining WHO via one of our talent programmes. International staff mobility WHO is committed to making a measurable difference in people’s health at the country level. To drive impact at the country, regional and global levels, our workforce needs to be agile and highly competent. Mobility makes our workforce more diverse at all levels of the Organization while improving organizational performance in three ways: 1) it increases the talent pool; 2) it brings new perspectives into discussions and decision making processes; and 3) it brings the voices of the people with health challenges more directly into the discussion. The mobility programme is implemented fairly but vigorously with enhanced attention to the retention of women leaders and people from developing countries at senior positions. Mobility is also part of the wider UN system, where many organizations have adopted it in various forms. The International Civil Service Commission (ICSC) has placed mobility at the heart of the career management pillar in its Framework for Human Resources Management.International Professional staff on fixed term contracts adhere to the geographical mobility programme. Staff categories and requirements International Professional Required qualifications (indicative list) Proficiency in English or French and a good working knowledge of a second official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, Spanish) is required for most positions. International Professional and Higher Graded levels run from P1 to D2. P1: One year of relevant professional work experience (1) and first university degree (3) P2: Two years of relevant professional work experience (1) and first university degree (3) P3: Five years of relevant professional work experience (1) and first university degree (3) P4: Seven years of relevant professional work experience (1) and master's level university degree (2) P5: Ten years of relevant professional work experience (1) and master's level university degree (2) P6/D1/D2: Fifteen years of relevant professional work experience (1) and master's level university degree (2) National Professional Officer Required qualifications (indicative list) Requirements for our National Professional Officers (NPO) are similar to those for our International Professional Officers; however, there is often more emphasis on working at a national level. NPOs are also an essential part of our professional teams. NO-A: One year of relevant professional work experience (1) and first university degree (3) NO-B: Two year of relevant professional work experience (1) and first university degree (3) NO-C: Five year of relevant professional work experience (1) and first university degree (3) NO-D: Seven year of relevant professional work experience (1) and master's level university degree (2) General Service positions Language qualifications (indicative list) General Service positions usually require a strong command of one official UN language and a working knowledge of a second. Knowledge of a third would be an advantage. Language requirements depend on the duty station. Educational level (indicative list) G3: Minimum 2 years of experience and completion of a secondary, technical or commercial school programme G4: Minimum 3 years of experience and completion of a secondary, technical or commercial school programme G5: Minimum 5 years of experience and completion of a secondary, technical or commercial school programme G6: Minimum 8 years of experience and completion of a secondary, technical or commercial school programme G7: Minimum 10 years of experience and completion of a secondary, technical or commercial school programme (1) Experience in developing countries an asset(2) Or equivalent educational qualification(3) For WHO staff only, equivalent professional training or self study/work experience Learn more Careers main page Apply for a position Other contractual arrangements Workforce testimonials

title: Non-staff contracts
description: Skip to main content WHO/ G. Elham Abdhul Rahman, polio vaccination volunteer, gives oral polio vaccine to an Afghan boy on a busy street. © Credits Other contractual arrangements WHO contracts subject matter experts to provide time-limited, project-focused professional level support to attain specific programme deliverables. These are not employment contracts and remain outside the scope of the WHO Staff Rules and Regulations. Consultants Consultancy contracts are offered to individuals to perform specific tasks in a given time frame (for example a research assignment or a translation). Presence at the duty station offering the contract may or may not be required. These contracts are not employment contracts and remain outside the scope of the WHO Staff Rules and Regulations. Consultants are contracted in a technical, advisory or consultative capacity, for a time-limited period to deliver clearly defined programme related deliverables. Consultants perform work in their personal capacity and not as representatives of a government or of any other authority external to the Organization.The qualifications, experience, skills and knowledge required for delivering the piece of work are described in the Terms of Reference prepared by the hiring office.Contracts may be offered for up to a maximum period of 24 months.Rates are paid in accordance with the established pay band ranges for internationally contracted consultants or national consultants. Internationally-contracted consultants may receive an amount towards living expenses.The conditions of contract are established as per the terms and conditions outlined in the consultant contract. WHO/Yoshi Shimizu © Credits Special Services Agreements (SSA)An SSA is a contract between the Organization and a national or resident of a host country. WHO use SSA contracts for either long or short assignments on a specific national projects or activities; including for services of a technical or administrative support nature.Rates of pay are determined in consultation with the Government and are in line with the practices of the UN agencies in the same country and are paid in local currency. Should SSA holders have a continuing pension fund, and/or life insurance commitments, WHO may meet those costs for the duration of the agreement, up to the maxima applicable locally.As SSA contract holders are not staff, their rights and obligations are according to the terms and conditions in their contract.Contracts do not usually exceed one year but it may be renewed for further maximum periods of one year at a time. ADB as a Borrower A leading triple-A borrower, ADB raises funds regularly through international capital markets. ADB’s overriding borrowing objective is to ensure availability of funds at the most stable and lowest possible cost for the benefit of its OCR borrowers. Subject to this objective, ADB seeks to diversify its sources of funding across markets, instruments, and maturities, and has so far issued bonds in 51 currencies. ADB pursues a strategy of: issuing liquid benchmark bonds to maintain a strong presence in key currency bond markets; and raising funds through bonds issued in both public and private placement format in various currency markets. ADB also seeks to develop domestic capital markets in its developing member countries through local currency borrowings and derivative activities. ADB Debt Products ADB's borrowing proceeds finance Ordinary Capital Resources operations, including development projects and programs within its developing members with the aim of reducing poverty in Asia and the Pacific region. Blue bonds include investments that contribute to marine and coastal ecosystem management and restoration, pollution control for marine and coastal environments, and sustainable coastal and marine development. title: ADB Green and Blue Bonds
description: Skip to main content Investor Relations A leading triple-A borrower, ADB raises funds regularly through bond issues in international and domestic capital markets, reflecting strong credit fundamentals and conservative financial policies. Home ADB Debt Products Credit Fundamentals ADB Green and Blue Bonds ADB Theme Bonds Translate 日本語 ADB Green and Blue Bonds ADB Green and Blue Bonds The Green Bond program enables ADB to support its developing member countries seeking to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and adapt to the consequences of climate change, whilst delivering environmentally sustainable growth to help reduce poverty and improve the quality of life of their people. The Green Bond portfolio specifically targets projects that promote the transition to low carbon and climate resilient growth as set out in the ADB Green Bond Framework. Asia and the Pacific depend on healthy and resilient oceans for disaster resilience, food security, and livelihoods. Healthy oceans also drive economies through fisheries and aquaculture. However, climate change, overfishing, pollution and unsustainable development have pushed our oceans to the brink of collapse. In order to address the growing funding gap required to protect and restore ocean health, global markets need to systematically change. Blue bonds encourage that shift by increasing the amount of capital that can be invested in oceans to finance solutions at scale. ADB Blue Bond Flyer Latest Newsletter How can companies and investors benefit? Projects eligible for Green Bond financing should be in the following areas: Climate Change Mitigation Climate Change Adaptation Eligible projects are identified by using the joint multilateral development bank approach for tracking and reporting climate change mitigation and adaptation finance. Projects eligible for Blue Bond financing should be in the following areas: Ecosystem and Natural Resources Management Pollution Control Sustainable Coastal and Marine Development Eligible projects for blue bond financing are identified by taking into account the additional selection criteria, including the project’s classification as outlined above, and the Sustainable Blue Economy Finance Principles. title: ADB Theme Bonds
description: Skip to main content Investor Relations A leading triple-A borrower, ADB raises funds regularly through bond issues in international and domestic capital markets, reflecting strong credit fundamentals and conservative financial policies. Home ADB Debt Products Credit Fundamentals ADB Green and Blue Bonds ADB Theme Bonds Translate 日本語 ADB Theme Bonds for Sustainable Development ADB launched its first theme (water) bond for sustainable development in 2010, in response to a growing demand among its investor base to highlight key initiatives. Since launching the water bond, ADB has expanded its theme bond offerings to include health, gender, education, and biodiversity and nature bonds. The projects funded by theme bonds are aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted by the United Nations on quality education, gender equality, clean water and sanitation, good health, and protection of terrestrial ecosystems. Latest Newsletter How can companies and investors benefit? Projects eligible for ADB Theme Bond for Sustainable Development financing should be in the following areas: Biodiversity and Nature Bonds These bonds support projects that protect, restore or enhance sustainable management of biodiversity and support nature mainstreaming. Digital Solutions Bonds These bonds promotes digital investments in connectivity, public infrastructure, cybersecurity, government systems, public service delivery, and other digital solutions. Education Bonds ADB’s projects in the education sector seeks to improve access to, and the quality and relevance of, education and training, and to amplify the returns to students and the workforce. Gender Bonds Investing in gender equality makes economic sense. Globally, it is estimated that $12 trillion could be added to the gross domestic product by 2025 by advancing gender equality. Health Bonds Health Bonds accelerate the progress of universal health coverage in ADB member countries. Water Bonds These bond issues support projects under the Water Financing Program and highlight ADB’s efforts to address Asia’s water sanitation needs. orgName: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
title: Auditeur interne
description: Responsabilités principalesMener à bien des activités d'audit interneparticiper à l'élaboration de la stratégie et des plans de travail annuels de l'audit interne, ainsi qu'à la production de rapports périodiques à ce sujet ;planifier, exécuter et rédiger des rapports des missions d'audit, examens et autres activités d'audit ou de conseil qui lui sont confiés, visant à fournir une assurance et/ou à renforcer la gouvernance, la gestion des risques, le contrôle interne, la conformité et la performance au sein des opérations de l'OCDE ainsi que de ses entités hébergées et autonomes ;gérer l'assistance technique fournie par des consultants externes dans le cadre des mandats d'audit qui lui sont confiés, en veillant au respect du guide (manuel), de la méthodologie et des modèles d'audit interne ;assurer un suivi périodique des recommandations d'audit interne auprès du management, afin de s'assurer que les actions convenues soient mises en œuvre, dialoguer avec les entités auditées pour s'assurer que les mesures mises en œuvre répondent aux problèmes et aux risques identifiés, et veiller à ce que les outils et processus informatiques associés restent adaptés à leur finalité ;apporter son assistance dans la liaison et la coordination des travaux de l'auditeur externe ;participer à l'assurance qualité et à l'amélioration constante de l'audit interne, afin de garantir la conformité aux normes de l'Institut des auditeurs internes (IIA) ;contribuer à l'innovation par le biais d'un développement professionnel continu et d'activités menées avec des homologues d'autres organisations internationales, l'Institut français de l'audit et du contrôle internes (IFACI), l'IIA et/ou d'autres organismes de normalisation, afin de garantir l'utilisation continue des meilleures pratiques et des méthodologies de pointe en matière d'audit interne ;apporter son soutien à l'auditeur(trice) principal(e) et accomplir toute autre tâche qui lui est confiée.Participer aux réunions du comité d'auditprésenter les rapports d'audit interne relatifs aux mandats d'audit qui lui ont été confiés ;présenter les résultats de la mise en œuvre par le management des recommandations de l'audit interne ; etrédiger les procès-verbaux des réunions du comité. Profil du/de la candidat(e) idéal(e)Formationun diplôme universitaire en gestion, finance, comptabilité, informatique, droit ou dans des domaines connexes ; etune certification professionnelle en comptabilité ou en audit, telle que CIA (Certified Internal Auditor), CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor), CFE (Certified Fraud Examiner), CPA (Certified Public Accountant) ou ACCA (Association of Chartered Certified Accountants).Expérience professionnelleau moins cinq ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente en audit, analyse financière, comptabilité ou dans un domaine étroitement lié, de préférence au sein d'organisations internationales, d'institutions financières multilatérales et/ou du secteur privé ;une expérience pratique dans le traitement des questions de gouvernance, de risques et de contrôle interne, ainsi qu'une bonne compréhension de leurs implications dans un contexte national ou international (sens diplomatique et interculturel), avec une capacité avérée à formuler des analyses et des recommandations ;une expérience pratique de la gestion de consultants externes et une capacité à mener à bien des missions d'audit interne sous supervision limitée.OutilsConnaissance des systèmes informatiques et de leur application aux processus financiers et administratifs (par exemple, l'analyse de données) ; maîtrise de la suite Microsoft Office ; la connaissance de SAP constitue un atout ; la connaissance de l'intelligence artificielle dans un contexte d'audit constitue également un atout.Compétences clésLes membres du personnel de l'OCDE sont censés faire preuve d'un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d'emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 2) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2).Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de compétence 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l'OCDE.LanguesParfaite maîtrise de l'une des deux langues officielles de l'OCDE (le français et l'anglais) et excellente maîtrise écrite et orale de l'autre.

orgName: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
title: Internal Auditor
description: Main ResponsibilitiesConduct Internal Audit activitiesparticipate in the development of, and periodic reporting on, the Internal Audit Strategy and annual Work Plans;plan, execute and draft reports for assigned audits, reviews and other audit/advisory activities aimed at providing assurance on and/or strengthening governance, risk management, internal control, compliance and performance across OECD operations as well as hosted and autonomous entities;manage technical assistance from external consultants on assigned audit mandates, ensuring compliance with the Internal Audit guide, methodology and templates;perform periodic follow-up with Management to ensure that agreed actions are on track to be implemented, engage with auditees to ensure that the actions implemented address the issues and risks identified, and ensure that the related information technology (IT) tools and processes are kept fit for purpose;assist in the liaison and co-ordination with the External Auditor;participate in Internal Audit quality assurance and improvement to ensure compliance with the standards of the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA);contribute to innovation through continuous professional development and activities with international organisation peers, the Institut Français de l'Audit et du Contrôle Internes (IFACI), the IIA and/or other standard setters, to ensure continued use of best practices and leading-edge methodologies in internal auditing;provide support to the Principal Auditor and perform other duties as assigned.Contribute to Audit Committee meetingspresent internal audit reports for assigned audit mandates;present the results of the implementation of internal audit recommendations by Management; anddraft the minutes of the Committee meetings. Ideal Candidate ProfileAcademic Backgrounda university degree in business, finance, accounting, information technology, law or related fields; anda professional certification in accounting or auditing, such as CIA (Certified Internal Auditor), CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor), CFE (Certified Fraud Examiner), CPA (Certified Public Accountant) or ACCA (Association of Chartered Certified Accountants).Professional Backgrounda minimum of five years of relevant experience in auditing, financial analysis, accounting or a closely related field, preferably in international organisations, multilateral financial institutions and/or the private sector;practical experience of dealing with issues of governance, risks and internal controls, and an understanding of their implications in a national or international forum (diplomatic and intercultural acumen), with a proven ability to formulate assessments and recommendations;practical experience in managing external consultants, and an ability to execute internal audit engagements with limited supervision.ToolsKnowledge of computer systems and their application to financial and administrative processes (e.g. data analysis); proficiency in the Microsoft Office suite; knowledge of SAP would be an asset; knowledge of artificial intelligence in an audit context would also be an asset.Core CompetenciesOECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 2); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 2); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 2); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2).To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies.LanguagesFluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and excellent written and oral communication in the other.

orgName: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
title: Responsable de la trésorerie de l’Organisation
description: Responsabilités principales Stratégie et direction en matière de trésorerie Fournir des conseils stratégiques à la haute direction concernant les liquidités, les placements à court terme, les arrangements bancaires, les risques financiers et les opérations de trésorerie à l’appui des priorités de l’Organisation et de sa viabilité financière. Surveiller l’évolution des liquidités et des flux de trésorerie, et recommander dans ce cadre des mesures visant à optimiser les disponibilités de trésorerie et à renforcer la résilience financière. Recenser, évaluer et atténuer les risques liés aux activités de trésorerie, notamment les risques de liquidité, de change et de contrepartie, ainsi que les risques opérationnels. Diriger l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie, des politiques, des procédures et du cadre de gouvernance de l’Organisation en matière de trésorerie. Piloter des initiatives de modernisation et d’amélioration continue des activités de trésorerie, en tirant parti de l’optimisation des processus, de l’automatisation et des technologies émergentes. Assurer la gestion, l’encadrement et le perfectionnement du personnel chargé de la trésorerie, en favorisant une culture d’équipe axée sur les performances, la collaboration et le service. Promouvoir la mise en commun des connaissances, le renforcement des capacités et le développement professionnel au sein de la fonction de trésorerie. Opérations de trésorerie, gestion de trésorerie et liquidités Superviser les activités de trésorerie et veiller à l’exécution, au suivi et au rapprochement en temps utile des opérations de trésorerie, conformément aux règles, politiques et exigences de contrôle interne de l’OCDE. Maintenir un niveau de liquidités suffisant pour répondre aux besoins opérationnels tout en optimisant l’utilisation de la trésorerie entre plusieurs comptes bancaires et dans différentes devises. Superviser la gestion des placements à court terme conformément aux politiques de placement approuvées et aux conditions du marché. Diriger l’établissement et l’affinement des prévisions de trésorerie à court et à long terme afin d’étayer la prise de décision et la planification des ressources. Gérer les relations stratégiques avec les partenaires bancaires et négocier des accords bancaires afin d’assurer des services efficaces et d’un bon rapport coût-efficacité. Contribuer à la préparation des états financiers (analyses et informations connexes à fournir) et coordonner les activités d’audit liées à la trésorerie ainsi que la mise en œuvre des recommandations. Préparer et présenter des rapports sur la performance de la trésorerie, les liquidités et les risques à l’intention de la haute direction et des organes de direction. Systèmes de trésorerie et amélioration des processus Superviser les systèmes de gestion de la trésorerie, les plateformes bancaires et les technologies de paiement, en veillant à l’efficience opérationnelle, à la résilience et à l’intégrité des données. Recourir à des techniques avancées d’analyse des données et de modélisation de scénarios afin d’améliorer les prévisions de trésorerie, d’évaluer les besoins de liquidité et de fournir des conseils prospectifs à la haute direction.Élaborer des tableaux de bord et des rapports analytiques qui traduisent les données de trésorerie, bancaires et financières en informations exploitables sur les liquidités, les risques, les coûts et les performances opérationnelles. Recenser et déployer des solutions d’automatisation et basées sur l’IA appropriées pour les processus de trésorerie, les contrôles, les rapprochements et l’établissement des rapports, en veillant à garantir une supervision humaine, la vérifiabilité des informations et le respect des exigences en matière de sécurité de l’information et de protection des données. Collaborer avec les équipes chargées des finances et du numérique afin de renforcer la qualité des données et leur intégration dans les systèmes bancaires, de trésorerie et de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), en favorisant la conduite d’analyses fiables et en réduisant les interventions manuelles.Utiliser les données et l’analytique à l’appui de la prise de décision, du suivi des performances et de la planification. Piloter l’examen et l’amélioration des systèmes afin de renforcer les contrôles internes, de réduire les risques opérationnels et d’améliorer la prestation de services. Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur (master ou équivalent) en finance, comptabilité, administration des entreprises, économie ou dans une discipline connexe, associé à une qualification professionnelle en comptabilité ou à une qualification professionnelle de niveau supérieur en trésorerie. Expérience professionnelle Au moins huit ans d’expérience marquée par une montée en responsabilités dans la gestion de trésorerie, la finance d’entreprise ou la gestion financière, avec notamment une expérience solide à un poste de direction de la trésorerie. Expérience avérée de la conduite de la transformation numérique des fonctions de trésorerie grâce à l’adoption de technologies de trésorerie, de l’automatisation et d’outils d’analyse des données, tout en renforçant les dispositifs de contrôle.Aptitude avérée à piloter l’amélioration des processus à l’aide des technologies, depuis le recensement des besoins opérationnels et l’appréciation des avantages jusqu’à la mise en œuvre et l’évaluation des résultats. Une expérience pratique de l’évaluation ou du déploiement de solutions basées sur l’IA dans un environnement financier, assortie d’une compréhension de leurs limites et des exigences en matière de gouvernance, constituerait un avantage. Expérience avérée de la gestion de liquidités, des prévisions de trésorerie, des relations bancaires et des placements à court terme au sein d’une organisation complexe. Compétence avérée en matière de normalisation et d’optimisation des processus de trésorerie et d’amélioration continue en vue de renforcer les contrôles, d’accroître l’efficience et de favoriser une gestion efficace des liquidités et des risques. Jugement stratégique avéré et aptitude à traduire des questions complexes en recommandations claires et en propositions concrètes. Expérience avérée de la direction d’équipe et du perfectionnement de ses membres dans un environnement collaboratif et axé sur les résultats. Outils Excellente connaissance des systèmes de gestion de la trésorerie et des systèmes ERP, de l’informatique décisionnelle, des outils de visualisation des données et de modélisation analytique, et aptitude à combiner et interpréter des données issues de sources multiples. Une expérience de SAP, des plateformes bancaires, des solutions basées sur l’IA et des technologies de paiement constituerait un avantage. Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 2) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 3) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 3) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 3) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE. Langues Parfaite maîtrise d’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE (le français et l’anglais) et connaissance de l’autre langue, que la personne retenue s’engage à porter à un bon niveau.

orgName: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
title: Economiste Junior
description: Principales responsabilitésRecherche, analyse de politiques économiques et rédaction de documentsMener des recherches de haute qualité et analyser les politiques sur les questions émergentes qui touchent l'Afrique.Utiliser des méthodes quantitatives pour analyser l'impact des politiques socio-économiques. Réaliser des analyses empiriques et des évaluations des politiques dans des contextes nationaux et comparatifs.Contribuer à la coordination de la recherche, des consultations, des examens par les pairs, de la rédaction, de la production et de la diffusion du rapport «Dynamiques du développement de l'Afriqu».Participer à la coordination et au contrôle qualité des publications, rapports et documents de travail de l’Unité Afrique, y compris le rapport «Dynamiques du développement de l'Afriqu».Préparer des notes conceptuelles et la documentation associée pour le Forum économique international annuel sur l’Afrique.Rédiger des notes d’information, des supports de communication, des présentations de rapports et des synthèses de haute qualité à l’intention des hauts responsables européenne (UE), l’AUDA-NEPAD, l’ACBF, l’ACET, le BMZ, la GIZ, ainsi que des fondations et des réseaux universitaires.Participer aux discussions au sein de groupes d’experts et contribuer à Profil du/de la candidat(e) idéa(e)Formation académiqueDiplôme universitaire de haut niveau en économie (spécialisation en macroéconomie souhaitée) ou dans un domaine connexe pertinent.
