orgName: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
title: Concepteur en formation et développement
description: Responsabilités principalesCe poste sera axé sur la conception du programme de formation en ligne du GAFI, en constante expansion, utilisé par des fonctionnaires de plus de 200 pays et juridictions. Il impliquera également des travaux de conception visant à contribuer à d’autres formations en présentiel et mixtes proposées par le GAFI. À terme, le candidat retenu jouera un rôle important dans l’amélioration de la compréhension des mesures de lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux, le financement du terrorisme et le financement des armes de destruction massive à l’échelle mondiale.• Conception pédagogique. Appliquer les principes de la théorie de l’apprentissage pour structurer de nouveaux produits d’apprentissage en ligne et d’autres supports de formation de manière à ce qu’ils soient captivants et stimulants, en étroite coordination avec des experts en politiques provenant de différents services du Secrétariat du GAFI et des pays membres.• Création de contenu. Utiliser les outils de conception les plus récents pour créer des supports de formation visuellement attrayants et s’inscrivant dans les thèmes généraux de conception du GAFI, en recourant à divers formats (vidéos, quiz, storyboards).• Assurance qualité, suivi et évaluation. Développer des mécanismes d’évaluation et analyser les données produites afin de tirer des enseignements de l’expérience des utilisateurs, ce qui permettra d’alimenter les mises à jour des supports de formation.• Collaboration. Entretenir des relations de travail étroites avec des homologues de l’OCDE et d’autres organisations internationales concernées (ONUDC, FMI, Banque mondiale, Groupe Egmont), en coordonnant et en échangeant les meilleures pratiques afin de soutenir la production de supports de formation et d’expériences d’apprentissage de haute qualité.• Travaux de conception ponctuels. En fonction du parcours du candidat retenu, contribuer, de manière ponctuelle, aux travaux de conception graphique destinés aux publications générales du GAFI et aux supports de communication externe. Profil du/de la candidat(e) idéal(e)Formation• Un diplôme universitaire ou équivalent dans les domaines suivants : e-learning, conception pédagogique, théorie de l'enseignement, technologies éducatives, formation des adultes, conception multimédia ou toute autre discipline pertinente. Expérience professionnelleAu moins trois ans d’expérience, et de préférence au moins cinq ans, en tant que développeur de formations en ligne.Expérience dans la planification de cours et de programmes pédagogiques ainsi que dans la création de storyboards, et connaissance et mise en œuvre des modèles Agile et ADDIE dans la conception de supports pédagogiques.Expérience dans la conception, le développement et la mise en œuvre de solutions d’apprentissage utilisant des méthodes telles que l’apprentissage par le jeu, la vidéo, le micro-apprentissage, les simulations et les scénarios immersifs comportant de multiples embranchements.Expérience dans le développement d’interactions complexes (c’est-à-dire utilisant des variables), d’activités d’apprentissage et d’animations.Maîtrise des logiciels de conception standard du secteur (par exemple, Adobe Creative Suite et Articulate 360) et utilisation de l’IA dans le processus de conception de supports pédagogiques.Expérience dans la gestion de projets impliquant différents groupes de parties prenantes aux profils variés, y compris des experts métier ayant une connaissance limitée de l’ingénierie pédagogique.Expérience de travail au sein d’une équipe multiculturelle ou d’une organisation internationale.Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 1) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2).Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE.LanguesMaîtrise courante d’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE (français et anglais) et connaissance de l’autre langue, que les candidat(e)s retenu(e)s s’engagent à porter à un niveau opérationnel. La maîtrise d'autres langues (par exemple, l'arabe, le chinois, le russe ou l'espagnol) serait un atout.

orgName: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
title: Assistants
description: Main Responsibilities Administrative and Operational Support Provide high-quality administrative, coordination and operational support to managers and teams. Draft, edit and format correspondence, reports, presentations and other business documents. Manage information, records and documentation, ensuring accuracy, confidentiality and compliance with organisational procedures. Use office productivity and digital collaboration tools effectively to support team objectives. Planning and Organisation Support the planning and coordination of meetings and prepare agendas, organise logistics and ensure timely follow-up on actions and deliverables. Monitor priorities and activities and manage multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced environment. Contribute to process improvements and the efficient functioning of the assigned team or Directorate. Stakeholder Relations and Communication Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders. Facilitate communication and information flow across teams and organisational levels. Provide responsive and client-focused support, handling enquiries professionally and efficiently. Resource and Logistical Support Coordinate travel arrangements and related logistical requirements, as needed. Assist with contract administration, procurement-related activities and budget monitoring, in accordance with OECD policies and procedures. Professionalism and Discretion Exercise sound judgement, discretion and professionalism when handling sensitive or confidential information. Demonstrate a proactive, solution-oriented approach and the ability to work independently in a multicultural and collaborative environment. The areas of specialisation: Executive assistance – Supporting senior leaders through calendar management, executive correspondence, stakeholder liaison, travel coordination and executive office operations. Administrative assistance– Supporting team operations and organisational activities through administrative coordination, records management, financial support, and/or the communication and delivery of meetings, missions, conferences and events. Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background A good secondary level of education, preferably in studies related to administration. Training in office management or as a secretary/assistant would be an advantage. Professional Background At least one year of relevant experience providing administrative, operational or executive support, including document preparation, correspondence, records management and routine follow-up. Experience supporting meetings, missions, travel arrangements, events or other logistical activities. Experience working with colleagues, managers and various stakeholders in a responsive, professional and service-oriented manner. Experience working in an international or multicultural environment would be desirable. Technical skills Strong drafting, editing, formatting and document production skills. Strong organisational skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage priorities, deadlines and follow-up actions. Good coordination skills for meetings, missions, events, travel arrangements and related logistics. Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to manage records, databases and confidential information with discretion and sound judgement. Familiarity with administrative, financial, procurement, travel, meeting or event-support processes. Problem-solving skills and willingness to learn organisational systems and new procedures. Tools Excellent knowledge and experience in the use of Microsoft 365 applications, including Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams. Demonstrated AI literacy, including the effective and responsible use of AI-powered tools such as Copilot, and the ability to quickly learn and adapt to new technologies and software applications. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 1); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 1); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 1). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies. Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. For certain positions, knowledge of other languages would be an asset.

orgName: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
title: Assistant(e)s
description: Responsabilités principales Appui administratif et opérationnel Fournir aux responsables et aux équipes un appui de qualité sur les plans administratif et opérationnel, ainsi que de la coordination. Rédiger, réviser et mettre en forme de la correspondance, des rapports, des exposés et d’autres documents internes. Gérer des informations, des dossiers et de la documentation, en veillant à leur exactitude, à leur confidentialité et au respect des procédures de l’Organisation. Utiliser efficacement des outils de bureautique et de collaboration numérique à l’appui des objectifs de l’équipe. Planification et organisation Faciliter la planification et la coordination des réunions et préparer les ordres du jour, organiser la logistique et assurer un suivi en temps voulu des actions et des résultats attendus. Assurer le suivi des priorités et des activités et gérer plusieurs tâches simultanément dans un environnement marqué par un rythme soutenu. Contribuer à l’amélioration des processus et au bon fonctionnement de l’équipe ou de la Direction d’affectation. Relations avec les parties prenantes et communication Développer et entretenir des relations de travail efficaces avec les parties prenantes internes et externes. Faciliter la communication et la circulation de l’information entre les équipes et les différents niveaux de l’Organisation. Apporter un soutien adapté aux besoins et axé sur le client, en traitant les demandes avec professionnalisme et efficacité. Ressources et soutien logistique Coordonner l’organisation des déplacements et les besoins logistiques connexes, en tant que de besoin. Prêter son concours à l’administration des contrats, aux activités liées aux achats et au suivi budgétaire, conformément aux politiques et aux procédures de l’OCDE. Professionnalisme et discrétion Faire preuve de discernement, de discrétion et de professionnalisme dans le traitement d’informations sensibles ou confidentielles. Agir de façon proactive, dans une démarche axée sur la recherche de solutions, et être capable de travailler de manière autonome dans un environnement multiculturel et collaboratif. Domaines de spécialisation : Assistant(e)s de direction – Apporter un soutien à de hauts responsables en s’occupant de la gestion du calendrier, de la correspondance, des contacts avec les parties prenantes, de la coordination des déplacements et des activités du bureau de la direction. Assistant(e)s administratif(ve)s – Faciliter l’exécution des tâches de l’équipe et/ou des activités de l’Organisation en assurant la coordination administrative, la gestion des dossiers, le soutien financier, la communication ainsi que l’organisation des réunions, missions, conférences et autres manifestations. Profil idéal Formation Bon niveau d’instruction secondaire, de préférence dans un domaine d’études en lien avec l’administration. Une formation en gestion administrative ou en qualité de secrétaire/assistant(e) constituerait un avantage. Expérience professionnelle Au moins un an d’expérience pertinente en matière de soutien administratif ou opérationnel ou d’appui à la direction, notamment en ce qui concerne la préparation de documents, la correspondance, la gestion de dossiers et le suivi des affaires courantes. Expérience de l’appui aux réunions, aux missions, à l’organisation des déplacements, aux manifestations ou à d’autres activités logistiques. Expérience de la collaboration avec des collègues, des responsables et diverses parties prenantes, dans un esprit d’ouverture, de professionnalisme et de service. Une expérience professionnelle acquise dans un environnement international ou multiculturel serait souhaitable. Compétences techniques Solides compétences en matière de rédaction, de révision, de mise en forme et de production de documents. Sens aigu de l’organisation et du détail, et capacité à gérer les priorités, les délais et les actions de suivi. Bonnes compétences de coordination pour ce qui concerne les réunions, les missions, les manifestations, l’organisation des déplacements et la logistique connexe. Très bon sens de la communication et des relations humaines. Aptitude à gérer des dossiers, des bases de données et des informations confidentielles avec discrétion et discernement. Bonne connaissance des procédures administratives et financières, ainsi que de celles relatives aux achats, aux déplacements, aux réunions ou à l’organisation de manifestations. Compétences en résolution de problèmes et volonté de se familiariser avec les systèmes et les nouvelles procédures de l’Organisation. Outils Excellente connaissance et solide expérience de l’utilisation des applications de Microsoft 365 (Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams). Maîtrise avérée de l’IA, notamment utilisation efficace et responsable d’outils fondés sur l’IA, par exemple Copilot, et aptitude à se familiariser rapidement avec de nouvelles technologies et applications logicielles et à s’y adapter. Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 1) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 1) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 1) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 1). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE. Langues Parfaite maîtrise d’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE (le français et l’anglais) et connaissance de l’autre langue, que la personne retenue s’engage à porter à un bon niveau. Pour certains postes, la connaissance d’autres langues serait un atout.

title: Associate Consultant - Growth Strategy and Sales Operations
description: Associate Consultant - Growth Strategy and Sales OperationsWork type: Contract · Department: Central Delivery · Workplace: HybridGurugram, Haryana, India Job detailsApplication formPosition: Associate Consultant – Growth Strategy & Sales OperationsLocation: Delhi NCRAbout SattvaWe Partner to deliver social impact at scaleSattva Consulting is a global impact consulting firm from India. Since 2009 we have been engaging with communities, business and government to achieve societal impact at scale.We believe that Civil society, Business and Government all have a critical role to play in building an equitable and sustainable world, and we actively partner with all stakeholders to enable impact through our advisory & orchestration services, knowledge and data platforms which we have built as public goods for the ecosystem and collaborative solutions and partnerships.Our teams are based in India, Singapore, Denmark and UK, but as a global organization our work has spanned 25 countries and 5 continents. For more information, please visit: www.sattva.co.in The OpportunitySattva is looking for a highly analytical, detail-oriented and execution-focused Associate Consultant to support the leadership and senior management team in driving business growth across North India.This role sits at the intersection of growth strategy, business development, pre-sales, and sales operations. title: AI Solution Lead – Bengaluru
description: AI Solution LeadWork type: Full time · Department: Central Tech and Data · Workplace: HybridBengaluru, Karnataka, India Job detailsApplication formPosition: AI Solution LeadLocation: Bangalore, HybridBusiness Unit: Technology, Data & AIAbout SattvaWe Partner to deliver social impact at scaleSattva Consulting is a global impact consulting firm from India. Since 2009 we have been engaging with communities, business and government to achieve societal impact at scale. We believe that Civil society, Business and Government all have a critical role to play in building an equitable and sustainable world, and we actively partner with all stakeholders to enable impact through our advisory orchestration services, knowledge and data platforms which we have built as public goods for the ecosystem and collaborative solutions and partnerships.Our teams are based in India, Singapore, Denmark and UK, but as a global organization our work has spanned 25 countries and 5 continents. For more information, please visit: www.sattva.co.inThe OpportunityThis is the role that anchors Sattva’s AI transformation. You drive the agenda for how AI changes the way we work, and you carry the organisation along that journey.You are accountable for making Responsible AI adoption happen; the business units and enablement teams you work with own the outcomes in their areas. You are inheriting live momentum from an outgoing AI Solution Lead: tools in place, a policy about to land, pilots in validation, a knowledge-management effort under way and an engaged network of AI champions. Alongside internal transformation, this role involves client engagements under the AI for Nonprofits offering, where the lessons of our own journey become the substance of what we deliver.Key responsibilities:You will focus on four pillars. 1. AI Adoption, Fluency and Responsible AI Make AI fluency universal, so that every Sattvan knows which tools suit which tasks and uses them responsibly and well. Build on what exists, including the AI Ninja Program, the AI Open House and the responsible-use assessment results.Keep the organisation informed. Run regular updates for leadership and for all of Sattva, so progress, lessons and next steps stay visible.Steward the AI Policy. With security, legal and IT, assess privacy, consent, confidentiality, vendor terms, access and data retention, and translate policy into pragmatic controls and plain-language guidance.2. Workflow Solutions with Business and Enablement UnitsDiscover and prioritise opportunities with business unit leaders, enablement heads and delivery teams. Understand real workflows, assess feasibility, value, data readiness, cost and risk, define measurable outcomes, and keep a transparent pipeline of use cases.Design practical solutions such as assistants, agentic workflows and reusable skills and playbooks, combining AI with the systems and data we already use. Build first versions yourself with AI and low-code tools, make build-versus-buy choices, and bring in external partners for larger builds.Grow and equip the AI champion network, so capability spreads well beyond you. Coach champions, give them ready-to-use playbooks, and learn from what they see in the field.Move pilots into stable, dependable use, each with an accountable business owner.3. AI for Nonprofits Client WorkHelp take the AI for Nonprofits offering from definition to its first engagements, working alongside the consulting teams that lead it.Support delivery directly through discovery workshops, use-case design, prototypes and hands-on training for nonprofit teams.4. Portfolio, Platforms and VendorsEvaluate AI products and implementation partners, and oversee the relevant licences, budgets and integrations.Keep the portfolio manageable and current, retiring tools and pilots that no longer earn their place.Skills Required: ExperienceTypically 6+ years across product or software delivery, technology consulting, digital transformation or similar work, with demonstrable hands-on experience designing and deploying GenAI workflows that people actually use. Equivalent capability matters more than a rigid tenure threshold.Led adoption or change across a largely non-technical workforce, and can show what changed as a result.Developed AI PoCs and run AI pilots with accountable business owners. Has taken some of them to productive use and adoption.Worked across multiple teams, business units or clients, facilitated workshops, and mentored champions or junior builders.CapabilitiesHighly hands-on with today’s frontier models, harnesses and tools. You use them every day and know what each is good for.A pragmatic builder who gets a working first version up fast with AI and low-code tools. Deep coding skills are not what we are looking for.Strong at workflow discovery, problem framing and prioritisation, and at turning pilots into maintainable services.A clear writer and communicator who can explain trade-offs to a busy consultant and a senior leader alike.AttributesExceptional at working with people. You earn time and commitment from colleagues who are busy with their own projects, and you lead through influence rather than authority.Genuinely enthusiastic and curious about AI, while clear-eyed about its pitfalls.Fast and pragmatic: you build a first version quickly, test it against real work, and prefer measured impact to tool novelty.A patient teacher who enjoys helping people from any background become confident with new tools.Helpful, Not MandatoryFamiliarity with social-sector consulting, NGO operations, due diligence, monitoring and evaluation, field data collection, research workflows or organisation-wide knowledge management.What Success Looks Like-In 3 months, you will have completed a structured handover of priority pilots, knowledge systems, governance, tool access and vendor obligations, each with a clear sponsor and next decision. You will have met every business unit head, enablement head and AI champion, published a concise use-case rubric and pipeline, and chosen a small set of high-value opportunities with baselines, milestones, owners and go/no-go criteria. For at least one workflow, you will have shown a repeatable benchmark, a failure taxonomy and a human-review design, and reached a decision to pilot, redesign or stop. You begin engaging with clients on AI strategy and implementation projects.-In 6 months, the first pilots will be in stable use with accountable owners, the AI Policy will be working as practical controls and guidance, and adoption will be measured at the level of real workflows. You would have delivered a few client engagements via the AI for Nonprofits offering.-In 12 months, selected use cases will show verified outcomes, with evidence of quality, adoption and a credible estimate of time, cost or service improvement. Every business unit and enablement team will have AI use cases in regular use, and Sattva will have documented solution patterns, review standards, reusable assets, trained champions and a current portfolio. Externally, Sattva would have established itself as a key enabler of AI transformation for Nonprofits.What Won’t WorkThis won’t work if you are a pure technologist who builds elegant tools nobody adopts. Adoption is not an afterthought to the job.This won’t work if you are an evangelist who runs inspiring workshops but cannot build, test or evaluate a solution yourself.This won’t work if your strength is writing production code and that is how you want to spend your days. We need someone who moves fast with AI tools and gets others moving, not a software engineer.This won’t work if you need a large team or formal authority to get things done. You will have a couple of interns, a network of champions and your ability to bring people along.What’s Hard About This JobInfluence without authority. description: PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges. Location: Pune, Maharashtra About the ProjectThere have been persistent efforts focused on improving primary healthcare (PHC) and overcoming the hurdles of low coverage and poor quality of health services through several Digital Health interventions. However, majority of these initiatives are designed with very specific clinical or administrative purposes and lack a comprehensive ecosystem approach resulting in multiple applications and digital portals in use for their health system. This cascades into poor accountability and performance, time and resource wastage, lack of continuum of care, and low coverage of health services, resulting in poor health outcomes. PATH is supporting the state of Maharashtra with digitization of primary level of care and health service delivery in select districts. The project intends to demonstrate end to end digitization in healthcare and develop a digital saturation model at district level, leveraging fit for purpose digital solutions/interventions through the use case of improving reproductive, maternal and child health service delivery indicators. The district saturation model will include coverage across rural & urban areas and service delivery across public and private sectors. The focus will be on digitizing healthcare facilities, community health initiatives/programs and deploying innovations for accelerating service delivery across continuum of care. The project aims to form a digitally competent health workforce, improve access to health and systems-level data for resource planning and management, enable creation of longitudinal health records for patients, and enable interoperability of digital systems across healthcare facilities. This will result in data-driven decision-making leading to improved access and service coverage, citizen empowerment, quality care, and enhanced healthcare provider accountability. title: Associate- Energy Transition and Renewable Energy Policy
description: About the Organization Swaniti Initiative is a social enterprise that is working at the intersection of climate, governance and last mile delivery. We believe that while the willingness and resources exist, there are fundamental gaps in the execution within communities that is the biggest crisis in the climate movement. Accordingly, Swaniti works with subnational governments to conduct microplanning exercises with consultations with community and key stakeholders to understand the pathways forward, provide technical assistance to subnational governments to provide support in program implementation and support in monitoring and delivery of programs.Swaniti has been working across multiple geographies in the global south to unlock capital. Our three core metrics include unlocking public capital, ensuring last mile communities are directly benefitted and creating systemic changes in the public service systems. While we are continuing to focus on impact, it is critical to have a lead who has a deep understanding about monitoring, evaluation and learning. Our intention is to create an institutional capability to measure and document the scale of our impact and look at how learning can be replicated across the institution.1. About the RoleSwaniti Initiative is looking for a technically qualified and research-oriented professional with 2–3 years of experience in energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy policy analysis.The candidate will contribute to research, policy analysis, regulatory assessment, and stakeholder engagement to support energy transition and industrial decarbonisation initiatives.2. Key Roles and ResponsibilitiesA. Energy Efficiency and Industrial DecarbonisationResearch energy consumption patterns and energy efficiency opportunities across industrial sectors, particularly MSMEs and industrial clusters.Assess potential energy efficiency interventions, technology adoption, and industrial decarbonisation pathways using available data and stakeholder inputs.Understand industrial manufacturing processes and identify opportunities for improving energy performance and operational efficiency.Analyse the potential benefits of energy efficiency interventions in terms of energy savings, cost reduction, productivity improvement, and emissions reduction.Identify policy and implementation gaps affecting the adoption of energy-efficient technologies.B. Renewable Energy Integration and C&I SolarisationResearch opportunities for renewable energy adoption among commercial and industrial (C&I) consumers.Analyse different renewable energy procurement models, including rooftop solar, captive, group captive, third-party open access, and hybrid renewable energy systems.Assess the technical, regulatory, and economic aspects of renewable energy integration.Analyse electricity tariffs, landed power costs, open-access charges, and the financial implications of renewable energy adoption for C&I consumers.Study the role of battery energy storage systems, distributed energy resources, and emerging renewable energy technologies.Identify barriers and enabling factors for scaling up renewable energy adoption among industries and MSMEs.C. Energy Policy Research and Regulatory MappingConduct research and analysis of central and state-level policies related to renewable energy, energy efficiency, and industrial decarbonisation.Map relevant government schemes, financial incentives, regulatory frameworks, and institutional mechanisms.Review state electricity tariff orders, open-access regulations, net metering provisions, and other relevant regulatory developments.Undertake comparative assessments of state-level energy policies and identify gaps in policy implementation.Track emerging policy developments and assess their implications for industries, DISCOMs, and other energy-sector stakeholders.Develop policy recommendations to support renewable energy adoption and industrial energy transition.D. Research, Data Analysis and Knowledge ProductsCollect, compile, and analyse energy-related information from government reports, regulatory documents, DISCOMs, industries, and other credible sources.Conduct state-wise and sector-wise assessments of renewable energy potential and energy efficiency opportunities.Analyse electricity consumption, tariff structures, renewable energy procurement, and industrial energy-use datasets.Prepare policy briefs, research reports, analytical notes, concept notes, presentations, and knowledge products.Support the development of presentations and briefing materials for government and industry consultations.E. Government and Industry Stakeholder EngagementSupport consultations with state energy departments, renewable energy agencies, DISCOMs, industry associations, MSMEs, financial institutions, and technical experts.Participate in government meetings, stakeholder consultations, workshops, and roundtable discussions.Undertake industrial cluster visits to understand manufacturing processes, existing technologies, energy-use practices, and decarbonisation challenges.Support coordination and collaboration with government institutions, industry representatives, and development partners.Requirements3. Essential Qualifications and ExperienceB.E./B.Tech in Electrical Engineering or Electronics/E&C Engineering from a recognised institution.2–3 years of relevant professional experience in the energy sector, particularly in renewable energy, energy efficiency, power-sector research, or energy policy consulting.Good understanding of India's renewable energy landscape, energy efficiency programmes, and electricity regulatory framework.Strong written and verbal communication skills.4. Technical Knowledge and SkillsThe candidate should ideally have:Understanding of renewable energy technologies, particularly solar PV, rooftop solar, captive solar, and open-access renewable energy.Understanding of energy efficiency technologies and industrial decarbonisation opportunities.Knowledge of central and state renewable energy policies, regulations, and government schemes.Strong data analysis skills, particularly using MS Excel.Proficiency in MS Word and PowerPoint for preparing reports and presentations.Familiarity with RETScreen, PVsyst, or other energy assessment tools would be an added advantage.5. Preferred ExperiencePreference will be given to candidates who have worked with:Think tanks, policy research organisations, or development-sector consulting firms.Renewable energy companies or energy-sector consulting organisations in research and policy-related roles.Government departments, state renewable energy development agencies, or DISCOM-related assignments.Industrial decarbonisation, MSME energy transition, or C&I renewable energy projects.Please Note- In case you do not hear from us within 30 days, please consider your application to be unsuccessful and your application has been retained in our database for future opportunities.

title: Program Manager, SPARC-AI Fellows
description: About the ProgrammeSupporting Parliamentarians on Analysis and Research in the Constituency (SPARC) is a flagship program at Swaniti Initiative. The SPARC program aims to improve economic and social outcomes in select Parliamentary constituency by focusing on pointed interventions and leveraging changes through the office of the Parliamentarian. We believe that working at the constituency level allows for us to create sandboxes across the country for developmental progress.In 2026 we plan on focusing on creating economic opportunities for last mile communities through the use of AI. Select Parliamentarians will, through the support of a Fellow, work with last mile communities such as SHGs, artisans and weavers, in order to improve economic opportunities. The programme works with women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to help them use AI tools for their businesses, improve business practices and access new opportunities.The interventions will focus on working with SHG women where we will identify points of entry for AI, develop appropriate interventions, train local master trainers called AI Saathis, track the use of AI tools and document the delta of impact that will take place. The programme follows a common methodology across all constituencies to ensure reliable and comparable findings. The intervention as well as the documented takeaways from each intervention will be critical to the success of the program.About the RoleThe Program Manager will lead oversee the interventions of the SPARC-AI Fellows across selected constituencies and will work with them to ensure that key metrics are met. The role involves - · Connecting periodically with Fellows in order to assess how they are completing their marked deliverables.· Supporting Fellows in order to complete program deliverables, including in areas of documentation, guidance on how to develop interventions etc.· Coordinating with Hon’ble MP offices and government officials to ensure programs are completed.· Ensuring the quality of research and documentation are impact.· When appropriate, conduct field visits to understand where programs currently stand​· Course correct interventions, when needed.Key Responsibilities1. Programme and Fellow Management· Detailing each phase of the program which would include a constituency wise intervention timeline for programs, deliverables expected and possible risks (based on geographies).· Organise Fellow training on field research, surveys, data collection, AI tools, informed consent and data protection.· Track monthly deliverables and support Fellows in resolving implementation challenges.· Organise expert training sessions and regular cohort reviews.2. Research and Field Implementation· Oversee the baseline study in all constituencies, including surveys of SHG women, in-depth interviews and consultations with relevant stakeholders.· Ensure Fellows follow the common sampling guide, questionnaire and data collection methods.· Review baseline findings and oversee the preparation of constituency-level diagnostic reports.· Follow up and ensure the completion of periodic documentation (including mid-term) and ensure accuracy and detailing.· Ensure the findings inform the selection of suitable AI applications and training priorities for each block.· Oversee limitations including in areas of data safety and security.3. MP and Government Engagement· Manage relationships with participating Hon’ble MP offices and coordinate regular progress reviews.· Support Fellows in identifying focus blocks and obtaining the necessary support from district and block officials and SHG federations.· Ensure the programme remains non-partisan and consistent across constituencies.· Coordinate presentations of programme findings to MP offices and, where appropriate, through district level meetings.· Ensure handover arrangements are in place by Month 11 so that AI Saathis can continue supporting women after the fellowship.4. AI Training and Roll-out· Oversee the development and local testing, along with short training videos and printed materials.· Coordinate with the relevant team to ensure AI tools are tested before they are introduced to SHG women.· Ensure Fellows train AI Saathis to conduct hands-on sessions and support women in using AI tools independently.· Track monthly SHG sessions and follow-up activities, including support for women who face difficulties using the tools.5. Monitoring, Research Quality and Reporting· Review Fellows’ weekly updates and monthly monitoring reports to track participation, independent usage, skills and changes in business practices.· Ensure data quality through questionnaire checks, back-checks and field-level verification.· Maintain a programme-wide dashboard showing implementation progress and SHGs requiring additional support.· Ensure problems are addressed promptly, particularly recurring AI errors or SHGs showing low usage for two consecutive months.· Oversee household checks of trained women during Months 8–10 to assess actual usage and changes in business practices.· Coordinate the 20 constituency reports and the national report, State of Last-Mile AI in India.6. Ethics and Responsible AI· Ensure Fellows and AI Saathis follow informed-consent, confidentiality and data-protection requirements.· Ensure women are advised not to share Aadhaar numbers, bank details, PINs or OTPs with AI tools.· Ensure AI-generated financial information is checked and that errors or harmful responses are reported and addressed.· Ensure no unauthorised promises are made regarding loans, grants or buyers.RequirementsQualifications and Experience· 5 - 8 years of experience in programme management, AI, development, livelihoods, governance, public policy, digital tools or related fields.· Familiarity with AI tools, digital inclusion or technology-led development is highly desired· Experience managing teams, multi-location programmes or fellowships.· Familiarity with SHG and livelihood ecosystems· Experience working with government departments, district or block administrations, elected representatives or community institutions.· Understanding of field research, sampling, data quality and monitoring systems.· Strong writing, analytical and reporting skills, with proficiency in spreadsheets.· Fluency in English and Hindi, and willingness to travel regularly to programme locations.· Strong organisational skills, sound judgement and a commitment to political neutrality, data privacy and ethical programme delivery.Ideal CandidateA hands-on programme manager who can manage multiple stakeholders and locations, support a distributed team, solve field-level problems and ensure that programme results are supported by credible evidence.Application Deadline: Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by 10 November 2026.​

title: Lead Consultant – AI & Future of Skilling (Desk Research)
description: About Swaniti Initiative Swaniti Initiative is a social enterprise working at the intersection of public policy, climate, governance, and technology implementation across the Global South. We support governments, industry leaders, and development partners with evidence-based policy design and last-mile execution. Role Overview We are seeking a senior expert with 10–15 years of deep experience in workforce skilling and economic development to lead a intensive, desk-research assignment over a 1–2 month period. The consultant will map existing workforce skill landscapes, analyze job tasks vulnerable to AI automation, and synthesize the emerging skill architecture required to build and deploy autonomous AI systems (agentic workflows). The primary output will be a comprehensive synthesis report and executive presentations designed to guide organizational leadership and external partners. Key Responsibilities Evidence Synthesis: Conduct a deep-dive review of existing Indian research, policy frameworks, and empirical studies (e.g., NITI Aayog, ICRIER, NASSCOM, ILO, and leading policy think tanks) mapping workforce readiness and skill exposure to AI. Three-Layer Skill Mapping: Analyze and synthesize data across three key dimensions: Baseline Domestic Skill Sets across key sectors in India and regional emerging markets. Job Task Exposure & Automation Risk driven by modern generative and agentic AI architectures. Emerging Agentic Skill Requirements needed for youth to become producers and owners of AI solutions. Strategic Framework Development: Translate complex research data into actionable frameworks for establishing localized AI sandbox experiments. Executive Presentations: Structure, design, and deliver clear, high-impact decks to present research insights to internal leadership and key external ecosystem stakeholders. Requirements Qualifications & Key Requirements Work Experience: 10 to 15 years of core experience in workforce development, skilling policy, digital economy, or human capital research within the Global South context (with significant exposure to India). AI & Tech Literacy: A established understanding of how AI works—specifically moving beyond basic generative AI/prompting to autonomous agentic workflows, API orchestration, and task automation mechanics. Research Track Record: Proven background in conducting high-level secondary research, policy analysis, and synthesizing complex national-level data sets into clear strategic insights. Publication & Citation Knowledge: Deep familiarity with existing Indian labor, economic, and skilling research papers; ability to draw upon established literature quickly without needing basic onboarding. Presentation Skills: Exceptional ability to translate dense desk research into clean, visually compelling executive slide decks and pitch documents. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit their CV along with 2–3 samples of previous research reports or presentation decks to the HR team at Swaniti Initiative. Swaniti Initiative is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion across its global operations.

We are driven by our mission to transform the school education system with a focus on improving children's learning outcomes, especially in low-income communities. Learn more at the website. About the position Early Childhood Education (ECE) refers to the pre-primary years, between the ages of 3 and 6, before a child enters Grade 1. Research across economics, neuroscience and education has shown that 90% of brain development happens before the age of 5, and that the quality of these years shapes a child’s schooling, health and income for life. The National Education Policy 2020 calls for three years of pre-primary education for every child. CSF partners with state governments and academic bodies to support the institutionalisation of developmentally appropriate pre-primary education within government school systems through curriculum, teacher preparation, classroom resources and implementation support. We work at scale in states including Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, and Telangana, and our work aims to create evidence and implementation playbooks to make quality pre-primary a regular part of the school system everywhere. The Project Manager supports the Project Lead across the ECE workstream and owns defined pieces of work within it. The role offers early exposure to the full spectrum of the work, from policy-level engagement to what actually happens in classrooms, and involves working with state teams, partner organisations, government counterparts, and CSF’s research and fundraising teams. Key ResponsibilitiesReview on-ground implementation: Spend regular time in schools, teacher trainings, district meeting and reviews to assess how pre-primary classes are being set up and run against the programme design. Document what is working, what is not, and why.Create and improve the playbooks: Turn field learning into playbooks, setup guidelines and resource packages that a state can adopt, and keep them current as states adapt them.Run diagnostics and handhold states: Design and run diagnostic tools for states setting up pre-primary classes, and provide hands-on support to state teams and officials through rollout.Build the evidence base: Maintain structured field notes, case studies and implementation data that feed the research team, policy notes and funder proposals, and support pilots and studies on the ground.Coordinate partners and state teams: Run the day-to-day working rhythm with partner organisations and CSF’s state teams, including joint workplans, reviews and follow-through.Manage delivery: Own workplans and trackers for central ECE workstreams, manage consultants and vendors, and flag risks to ensure high quality delivery Required Qualifications, Skills, and AbilitiesRelevant Experience (2–4 years) - Two to four years of strong performance in public policy, consulting, education or development, including through a structured fellowship. A Master’s in Education, Public Policy, Social Sciences or Management preferred.Synthesis and Communication - The ability to turn research, field observation and stakeholder input into clear, well-structured written drafts and presentations Fluency in English and Hindi - Both spoken and written, at a standard that supports drafting for government audiences and working with state teams.Exposure to Government - Some experience of working with government officials or department processes, through a fellowship, a PMU or a government-facing role will be an advantageExecution Discipline - A record of running workplans, tracking several pieces of work at once and coordinating people without losing detail.A Hands-On Temperament - Suited to a small organisation with shifting priorities and frequent travel, and comfortable operating without a settled plan. title: Project Associate - High Potential Students
description: <iframe src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-WNGRBS6" height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe> Project Associate - High Potential Students Delhi, India Apply for Position Or refer someone Job Openings Project Associate - High Potential Students About the job Project Associate - High Potential Students Central Square Foundation: Founded in 2012, Central Square Foundation (CSF) is a non-profit philanthropic organization working with the vision of ensuring quality school education for all children in India. We believe that effective foundational learning is essential for better learning outcomes for all children in school. The development of foundational literacy and numeracy skills by Class 3 can help children progress to higher levels of learning and is an essential building block in a child's life. We are driven by our mission to enable the school education system to adopt solutions that are scalable, sustainable, and effective so that all children get equal access to opportunities needed for leading a better life. Read more about our work here: www.centralsquarefoundation.org About High Potential Students workstream at CSF: India’s school education system serves ~25 crore children. Many of these students come from underserved communities and face systemic gaps in identification and support. With most interventions beginning only after Grade 10, much of this potential remains untapped and underdeveloped. To bridge this gap, CSF introduced a new workstream in 2025, High Potential Students (HPS), to support India’s bright young minds from underprivileged backgrounds in becoming future innovators, researchers and leaders. By 2030, we aim to transform the learning journeys of 1 lakh students by equipping them with the skills, support and exposure needed to thrive in higher education and high-growth careers. Through this work, we are committed to advancing equity and excellence, empowering young minds from every corner of India to realise their full potential. CSF is working with government model school systems to strengthen pathways for high-potential students (HPS) from underserved communities. The work focuses on designing and implementing initiatives within government model schools to support students’ academic, socio-emotional, and career development. Key areas include programme planning and implementation, partner and government coordination, field engagement, documentation, and evidence generation. The work also supports effective classroom practices, academic enrichment, structured advanced learning opportunities, career pathways, and overall student progression. Position Summary: CSF is seeking a Project Associate to join the High Potential Students workstream in Delhi and support the planning and implementation of HPS programme. The Project Associate will be responsible for supporting assigned programme priorities, managing day-to-day implementation, maintaining trackers and documentation, supporting review and reporting processes, conducting field visits, analysing implementation data, and identifying risks that require course correction. The role requires strong project management skills, comfort with data, clear written communication, field orientation, and the ability to work in a dynamic and evolving environment. The core areas of contribution are: Programme Implementation and Coordination Support the execution of key programme priorities under the High Potential Students workstream, especially across model schools.Build and manage working relationships with diverse stakeholders, including regional government teams, school leaders, programme partners, educational nonprofits, vendors and internal CSF teams.Coordinate with implementation partners to monitor and review programs across EdTech, assessments, academic enrichment, and career pathways, ensuring effective progress tracking, timely identification of gaps, and appropriate follow-through on action items.Support stakeholder convenings, partner check-ins, review meetings and government updates by collating data, preparing materials, documenting discussions and tracking next steps. Project Management, Reviews and Reporting Maintain programme trackers, timelines, meeting notes, action-item logs, data templates and other tools required for day-to-day monitoring and review.Manage timelines and deliverables for assigned workstreams to ensure that activities are on track and aligned with project objectives.Prepare clear written outputs, including field visit notes, meeting minutes, update emails, review notes, progress summaries, presentations, reports and internal briefing documents.Provide timely updates to internal teams and CSF leadership on implementation progress, key insights, risks, opportunities and areas for course correction. Data, Field Insights and Documentation Support rigorous data cleaning, validation and analysis to identify trends, implementation gaps, inconsistencies and areas requiring follow-up or course correction, while also supporting the development and maintenance of dashboards, trackers and other data platforms for programme monitoring and review.Conduct targeted field visits to schools and institutions to gather operational and academic insights, understand implementation realities and document observations.Document key learnings, field insights, implementation challenges and emerging practices to inform reviews, reporting, programme improvement and future scale-up. Problem Solving and Agile Support Identify, assess and escalate implementation risks and bottlenecks in partner delivery, school-level execution, data availability or communication, while supporting proactive issue resolution.Collaborate with internal teams to ensure smooth project delivery, timely communication of progress and follow-through on agreed priorities.Support emerging priorities and time-sensitive tasks that may arise from government stakeholders, programme partners or internal teams, with the ability to respond quickly, organise next steps and drive closure in a dynamic work environment. Required Qualifications, Skills, and Abilities: We are looking for a young professional who brings: 0 to 2 years of post-qualification work experience for the Project Associate role, preferably in the education sector, development sector, programme management, EdTech implementation, assessments, school-system reform, or government-facing projects.Strong project management skills or demonstrated ability to manage timelines, trackers, follow-ups, action items and multiple priorities simultaneously.Good writing and oral communication skills, with proficiency and fluency in English and Hindi.Good project delivery skills, including the ability to coordinate with partners, schools, government teams and internal colleagues to drive execution and ensure closure on deliverables.Ability to work with student-level, school-level, assessment, platform usage or programme monitoring data to derive implementation insights and support reviews.Strong documentation and reporting skills, including the ability to prepare meeting notes, progress updates, field visit reports, review materials and concise internal briefs.Strong growth and learning mindset, with attention to detail, ownership of assigned tasks, problem-solving orientation, agility to take up emerging priorities, and willingness to travel across implementation schools within/outside of Delhi NCR. We are driven by our mission to transform the school education system with a focus on improving children's learning outcomes, especially in low-income communities. Learn more about CSF by visiting our website. About the team: Strategic Support States: Strategic Support States (SSS) team at Central Square Foundation assists the States in designing and implementing the respective state missions to ensure FLN learning outcomes for children. Spread across five states, the Project Management Units (PMUs) of the team work closely with the state bodies in co-ideating goals for state’s FLN mission, identifying critical workstreams, setting indicators of success across the workstreams, and reviewing mission progress. Apart from these core activities, the SSS team also conducts action research projects and pilots, as well as context-specific programs to accelerate student learning. CSF’s work in Assam: CSF has been actively working with the Samagra Shiksha, Assam, on its FLN mission, NIPUN Axom, ensuring that all children in Foundational Grades receive quality education and achieve the desired FLN outcomes. CSF's interventions go beyond mere support; they involve strategic planning, capacity building, and continuous monitoring of the implementation process. By closely working with state, district, and block-level administrators, CSF aims to address implementation challenges, identify gaps, and prioritize areas that can drive significant improvements in FLN outcomes. Roles and Responsibilities of the SPM: 1. Numeracy academic design. Lead the design of the state’s foundational numeracy package for Foundational Grades— learning outcome framework, teacher lesson plans, student practice material, TLM kits and assessment tools — sequenced along an explicit competency progression, especially in numeracy and aligned to NEP 2020, NCF-FS 2022 and the NIPUN Bharat Guidelines. 2. Data analysis and interpretation. Analyse learning data from state assessments, spot tests, classroom observations and national benchmarks (NAS, PARAKH) to locate precisely where children are stuck — by competency, grade, block and classroom practice. Distinguish the underlying cause (curriculum gap, teacher content knowledge, time on task, practice load, assessment misfit) rather than reporting aggregate scores. 3. Evidence-based academic interventions. Convert diagnosis into a small number of targeted interventions, each with a stated hypothesis, target competency, dosage and a measurable success indicator. Draw on the Indian and global evidence base on structured pedagogy, teaching at the right level and spaced practice, and adapt it to Assam’s classrooms. 4. Deep engagement in one block. Take direct ownership of one block as a learning and demonstration site. Work with its CRCCs, teachers and block officials over a sustained period, test academic interventions in a tight design–implement–measure–refine loop, and use the evidence generated to decide what merits state-wide scale. 5. Teacher professional development. Build TPD — teacher content knowledge, common student errors and misconceptions, use of manipulatives, questioning and error correction — designed from observed classroom gaps rather than generic modules. 6. Review and course correction with the government. Present analysis and recommendations to Samagra Shiksha and district leadership in formal review forums. Reduce data to a short set of decisions and follow each through to implementation.. 7.Reporting. Produce timely, accurate and evidence-grounded proposals, government notes and reports. Required Qualifications, Skills, and Abilities 1. Master’s degree in Education, Mathematics, Science, Development Studies, Public Policy, or the Social Sciences. Candidates with a master’s degree in mathematics or science will be preferred. 2. 4 to 6 years of work experience preferably in the education sector demonstrating remarkable project delivery and stakeholder management including teaching experience. Experience of working in foundations, mission mode projects will be given preference. 3. Prior experience working with state/district-level governance and institutional structures in designing/supporting academic and Teacher Professional Development (TPD) programs is highly desirable 4. Ability to undertake field travel (schools, clusters, blocks, districts) for at least 10 days in a month 5. Fluent in English with excellent written and oral communication skills. Proficiency in Assamese / Bodo/ Bengali will be an added advantage 6. Strong skills in stakeholder management, problem-solving, and analytical thinking 7. Excellent project execution skills, including the ability to break down tasks, adhere to timelines, balance multiple priorities at a time, and hold oneself and others accountable to deliverables 8. Will to thrive in ambiguous and evolving environments 9. A strong intent to solve educational problems at scale Compensation Remuneration will be competitive with Indian philanthropy pay scales and will depend upon the candidate’s experience levels. title: Project Manager/ Senior Project Manager - School Governance
description: <iframe src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-WNGRBS6" height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe> Project Manager/ Senior Project Manager - School Governance Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India Apply for Position Or refer someone Job Openings Project Manager/ Senior Project Manager - School Governance About the job Project Manager/ Senior Project Manager - School Governance Organisation: Central Square Foundation Team: School Governance Location: Gandhinagar, Gujarat (travel within the state and periodic travel to Delhi) About Central Square Foundation Central Square Foundation is a nonprofit organisation working with the vision of ensuring quality school education for all children in India. Since 2012, we have been partnering with the government and ecosystem stakeholders to improve the learning outcomes of children, especially from low-income communities. We are driven by our mission to enable the school education system to adopt solutions that are scalable, sustainable, and effective, so that all children get equal access to opportunities needed for leading a better life. CSF has prioritised 4 critical areas of work: (1) Foundational Literacy & Numeracy (FLN) (2) EdTech (3) Early Childhood Education (ECE) (4) School Governance Learn more about CSF on our website. About the Team: The School Governance team at Central Square Foundation envisions a transformed school education delivery system that is principally accountable and transparent about its learning outcomes. It targets measuring and publicising the achievement of quality outcomes in public and private schools and establishing a State Schools Standards Authority to enable this reform. The Problem Despite extensive efforts to increase access to education, learning outcomes have remained alarmingly stagnant in the current educational landscape. Major government initiatives have focused on expanding access and providing input to schools, but their impact on improving educational outcomes has been tenuous, at best. An absence of outcomes-oriented and evidence-based governance is aggravated by a regulatory system where the government runs its own schools and regulates all schools, posing a conflict of interest due to the operator being the regulator. Further, there is no way to reliably measure the learning attainment of schools, making it difficult to hold them accountable for results. The Solution CSF's Schools Governance team acknowledges the pressing need for a systemic reform in education, which can be solved with a two-fold approach. The states need to: - Establish a robust and reliable learning outcome indicator at the school level by assessing student competencies through a competency-based census assessment (CCA). This will involve public disclosure of school data, while keeping the student data anonymous, to transparently show every school's quality and nudge them to make the necessary improvements.Create an independent school regulator, the State School Standards Authority (SSSA), which will operate outside the current Department of School Education. This body will focus on setting school standards and demand accountability from all schools, government or private. About the work in Gujarat CSF's School Governance team helps states move from input-based regulation to outcome-based regulation, in line with the National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020). In Gujarat this means three connected pieces of work: building a reliable, school-level learning indicator through a Competency-based Census Assessment (CCA); enabling public disclosure of school quality while keeping student data anonymous; and supporting the State School Standards Authority (SSSA) as a regulator. Gujarat already runs a school quality programme, Gunotsav, which this work seeks to strengthen and align to outcomes. Position Summary You will run CSF's day-to-day execution of this programme in Gujarat. You are the single point of accountability who keeps government partners, technology vendors, and the internal team moving together. You are stepping into a live programme with existing relationships, an in-progress portal build, and a current roadmap, so the first priority is to absorb context quickly and hold continuity, not to rebuild from scratch. Key responsibilities 1. Programme execution Own the Gujarat workplan, timelines, and deliverables for the SSSA programme, covering the CCA, public disclosure, and the supporting portal systems.Keep the programme on track against milestones, surface risks early, and drive decisions to closure. 2. Government and stakeholder management Be CSF's primary working contact for the state education department, GCERT (Gujarat Council of Educational Research and Training), the SSSA body, and data or hosting agencies.Build trust at both the official and field level, manage approvals and clearances, and turn CSF's recommendations into actions the government can adopt. 3. Quality assurance and Gunotsav Develop a clear view of where Gunotsav helps and where it falls short against the outcome-based intent of NEP 2020, keeping students and parents as the test of value.Work with the state to improve how assessment is done, how results are disclosed, and how findings feed back into teaching and school improvement. 4. Product, portal, and vendor coordination Translate ground realities into clear requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria for the school quality and assessment portals.Manage technology vendors on scope, delivery, quality, and timelines, and steer the path to production readiness across security, performance, scale, data privacy, and hosting.Coordinate integrations where needed, for example with UDISE+ (Unified District Information System for Education Plus). 5. Monitoring and continuity Track adoption and usage, and share regular dashboards and honest progress updates with the state team and leadership.Keep clean documentation, decision logs, and a current handover record so the programme never depends on one person's memory. Required Qualifications, Skills, and Abilities 4 to 7 years of experience delivering complex programmes or technology-enabled projects, ideally in government, public systems, or the social sector.A graduate or postgraduate degree in any discipline.A track record of managing external vendors on time and quality.Strong stakeholder management, structured problem-solving, and clear written communication.Comfort working with data and digital platforms, including requirements, quality assurance, and releases. You do not need to write code, but you must be able to hold vendors to account on it.Fluent in English. Working Gujarati is a strong advantage for the field and government interface.Willing to be based in Gandhinagar and travel within the state.Familiarity with the Indian school education landscape and state-level systems. (preferred)Exposure to GovTech or large public sector platforms, and to government hosting and compliance, for example NIC hosting, security audits, and data protection. (preferred)Experience taking a product or programme from pilot to stable operation at scale. (preferred) Other Details:Remuneration competitive with Indian philanthropy pay scales, based on experience.Start date: Immediate.
